subResults.subsystem: apps/web — Next.js 16 / React 19 UI layer (pages, editors, knowledge-graph viz, Zustand state, i18n, collab wiring)
subResults.purpose: The user-facing web client for SayKnowMind: memory/document list + detail, multi-tab document editor (BlockNote notes + Univer sheets + embedded HTML), mind-elixir mindmap editor, a knowledge-graph visualization, real-time collaborative editing over Hocuspocus/Yjs, document version history, public share/gallery views, and a hand-rolled 4-locale i18n layer.
subResults.architecture:
App Router (Next.js 16) with a heavy "use client" surface. Every expensive editor is code-split behind `next/dynamic` with `ssr:false` (doc-editor-dynamic.tsx, mindmap-editor-dynamic.tsx, office-tab via dynamic in doc-tabs.tsx, graph-canvas via dynamic in knowledge-dashboard.tsx) so BlockNote, Univer, mind-elixir, Yjs and the force-graph canvas never enter the SSR/initial bundle — disciplined and consistent.

State is Zustand: store/memory-store.ts (list/pagination/filter/optimistic CRUD), categories-store.ts, runtime-store.ts, plus a hand-rolled i18n store in lib/i18n.ts (zustand + persist, custom `t()` over imported JSON, no next-intl). Editors own their own local React state/refs; the list view is the only large global store.

The defining trait is THREE different collaboration fidelities all riding the same Hocuspocus provider keyed by docId:
1. BlockNote notes (doc-tabs.tsx CollabTabEditor): true Yjs CRDT — one XML fragment per tab (`tab:${id}`), the tab list itself is a shared Y.Array, awareness drives presence avatars, with JWT refresh + exponential-backoff auth-reconnect. This is the gold path.
2. Univer sheets (office-tab.tsx): no OT in OSS Univer, so a best-effort mutation op-log over a per-tab Y.Array (`office-ops:${id}`), last-write-wins, snapshot is the durable source of truth.
3. mind-elixir mindmaps (mindmap-editor.tsx): whole-document JSON blob in a single Y.Map key `data`, last-write-wins with a 1500ms "defer remote while typing" heuristic.

Persistence is uniform: debounced PATCH /api/documents/{id} writing flat plaintext (for RAG/search) + structured metadata, plus a sendBeacon to /process on unmount to re-index. Graph view is its own island (knowledge-dashboard.tsx) fed by /api/knowledge/graph with an SSE live-refresh channel.
whats_good: Code-splitting discipline is excellent: all four heavy editor/viz libraries are dynamic + ssr:false, so the base bundle stays light and SSR never touches canvas/DOM-only libs.

BlockNote collaboration is done correctly: per-tab Yjs XML fragments, awareness-based presence with id-dedup (doc-tabs.tsx:918-939), a deterministic seedTabId() to stop two clients creating duplicate 'Tab 1' rows (doc-tabs.tsx:131), and full-replace writeTabs() to dodge the empty-array clobber race (doc-tabs.tsx:830).

Resilient collab fallback: a 3.5s token-fetch timeout flips to single-user editing so the editor ALWAYS opens even if the relay is down (doc-tabs.tsx:444), and notes collab refreshes the JWT + reconnects with capped exponential backoff (doc-tabs.tsx:846-880).

i18n key parity is effectively perfect: 901 leaf keys in each of en/ko/zh/ja with 0 missing/extra; the ~14 identical-to-English values are product names, placeholders and tech terms (CSV, Webhook, Sheets) — i.e. intentional.

knowledge-dashboard.tsx computes a structural signature of nodes/edges and skips setState when unchanged (graphSigRef, line 93-101), preventing SSE refreshes from restarting the d3-force simulation — a genuinely thoughtful perf fix.

Optimistic UI with rollback throughout memory-store (favorite/archive/trash/tag mutations revert on fetch failure), and request-id guarding on fetchMemories to drop stale responses (memory-store.ts:489).
Univer mount/dispose is React-19-StrictMode-safe: macrotask yield before build, deferred dispose past commit, per-tab remount via React key (office-tab.tsx:141, 311).
HTML embeds are sandboxed without allow-same-origin, so embedded scripts cannot reach parent cookies/DOM (html-block.tsx:22).

risks.title: Mindmap collaboration is whole-blob last-write-wins, not a CRDT
risks.detail: mind-elixir maps sync by stringifying the ENTIRE map and writing it to a single Y.Map key ('data'). Two people editing different branches concurrently overwrite each other — whoever saves last wins, the other's edits vanish. The 1500ms 'defer remote while editing' window only reduces, not prevents, loss. This silently corrupts shared mindmaps under real concurrency.

risks.title: Mindmap collab never refreshes its JWT
risks.detail: The mindmap HocuspocusProvider is constructed with a static `session.token` (no token-getter, no refresh, no auth-failure reconnect) — unlike the notes editor which has getTokenForConnect + backoff. When the short-lived collab JWT expires mid-session the socket closes and never re-authenticates, so a long open mindmap silently stops syncing with no UI signal.

risks.title: Univer collab op-log grows unbounded and embedded images bloat every mindmap sync
risks.detail: office-tab pushes every spreadsheet MUTATION onto a Y.Array forever with no pruning/compaction (office-tab.tsx:288) — the relay persists this, so a long-lived sheet accumulates an ever-growing op history. Separately, mindmap image upload embeds base64 data-URLs directly into the map JSON (mindmap-editor.tsx:483), and that whole JSON is restringified and pushed on every operation — a couple of images turn each keystroke-sync into hundreds of KB over the wire.

risks.title: Public/shared HTML embeds execute arbitrary author JavaScript in every viewer's browser
risks.detail: Full-page HTML tabs and shared rich views render user-authored HTML via iframe srcDoc with `allow-scripts allow-popups allow-forms allow-modals`. The sandbox correctly omits allow-same-origin (no cookie/parent access), but a malicious author of a SHARED or published doc still runs JS in viewers' browsers in a unique origin — enabling popups, redirect/phishing, form exfil and fingerprinting. shared-rich-view.tsx exposes this on the public share surface.

risks.title: Knowledge graph reimplements hit-testing around the library because FG2D click handling is 'broken in React 19'
risks.detail: GraphCanvas disables react-force-graph's pointer-area painting and onNodeClick, then does its own O(n) nearest-node scan in screen space on every click/move (findNodeAtScreen). It works but is tightly coupled to FG2D internals (graph2ScreenCoords, d3ReheatSimulation) and to a fixed 22px hit radius; a library bump can silently break selection/drag.

risks.title: List view over-renders and recomputes filtering several times per render
risks.detail: MemoryContent destructures the entire useMemoryStore() (no selector), so any store change re-renders the whole content subtree. Within one render getFilteredMemories() runs at line 281 and again at 283, and getDerivedTags() calls it a third time internally — each pass is an O(n log n) filter+sort over all memories. Fine for tens of items, wasteful as the corpus grows.

risks.title: Heavy graph dependencies are dead weight
risks.detail: sigma, @react-sigma/core, graphology and graphology-layout-forceatlas2 are all declared in package.json but imported nowhere in app/components/lib — the actual knowledge graph uses react-force-graph-2d. These are unused install/supply-chain surface and audit noise. (@xyflow/react IS used, but only in category-graph.tsx.)
risks.evidence: apps/web/package.json (sigma/graphology entries) vs grep showing zero source imports

risks.title: Orphaned Yjs fragments and unbounded localStorage on delete
risks.detail: Deleting a tab removes it from the shared list but its `tab:${id}` XML fragment and `office-ops:${id}` array stay in the relay-persisted ydoc forever. Likewise GraphCanvas persists dragged-node positions to localStorage keyed by node id and never prunes entries for deleted nodes — both are slow, unbounded growth.

code_review.issue: getNestedValue returns the raw dotted key path as the fallback when a translation is missing, so a missing key renders literally as 'knowledge.nodeType.foo' in the UI. Several call sites also abuse this sentinel (t(key) === key) for control flow (node-detail-panel typeLabel/propLabel), coupling presentation fallback to business logic.
code_review.suggested_fix: Return the last path segment or an explicit '' fallback for display, and expose a separate has(key)/tExists() helper for the type-detection logic instead of string-comparing against the key path.

code_review.issue: useTranslation hard-codes locale='en' until useSyncExternalStore reports mounted, so non-English users get a flash of English on every load before the persisted locale applies (FOUC). Also useI18nStore() subscribes to the whole store.
code_review.suggested_fix: Persist locale to a cookie and read it during SSR (or inject it on <html lang>) so the first paint matches; subscribe with a selector (useI18nStore(s=>s.locale)).

code_review.issue: Whole-store destructuring of useMemoryStore() plus 3x getFilteredMemories() per render (see risks). Re-renders and re-sorts on every unrelated store mutation.
code_review.suggested_fix: Select only the fields used via per-field selectors, and compute filteredMemories once with useMemo (or move the derived selectors to memoized store getters keyed on inputs).

code_review.issue: Mindmap collab gating re-reads process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_COLLAB_WS_URL inside the editor even though the parent already passes collab based on the same env, and fetches the collab token itself — duplicating the token-acquisition logic that doc-tabs centralizes in fetchCollabSession.
code_review.suggested_fix: Share one collab-session helper (fetchCollabSession + provider factory + token refresh) across notes/mindmap/sheet so all three paths get refresh + reconnect for free and the mindmap LWW/token gaps close.

code_review.issue: persist / scheduleAutosave / saveNow / handleAddTab / handleDeleteTab / commitRename are duplicated almost verbatim between DocTabsSingle and DocTabsCollab (~150 lines), differing only by the writeTabs vs setTabs + canWrite guard.
code_review.suggested_fix: Extract a useDocTabsModel hook that takes a tab-writer strategy (local setState vs Yjs writeTabs) so both variants share one implementation.

code_review.issue: fetchNodeDetail and handleNodeClick both GET /api/knowledge/node/{id} with near-identical bodies; handleNodeClick duplicates the fallback-to-bare-node logic inline.
code_review.suggested_fix: Collapse into one async getNodeDetail(node?) helper used by both click and drill-down.

improvements.what: Unify the three collab editors behind one Yjs session/provider helper with shared JWT refresh + backoff reconnect, and replace the mindmap whole-blob LWW with a structured Yjs representation (or at minimum gate concurrent writers).
improvements.why: Two of the three collaborative surfaces (mindmap, sheet) silently lose data or auth on real concurrency / long sessions, while notes already solved all of this — the fix is mostly consolidation.

improvements.what: Remove unused sigma/@react-sigma/core/graphology/graphology-layout-forceatlas2 from package.json (or actually adopt them if a sigma renderer was intended).
improvements.why: Dead heavy deps inflate install size and supply-chain/audit surface for zero benefit.

improvements.what: Add selectors + memoization to the memory list (per-field useMemoryStore selectors, single memoized getFilteredMemories).
improvements.why: Eliminates whole-tree re-renders and triple O(n log n) recompute per render as the corpus scales.

improvements.what: Prune Yjs sub-docs (tab fragments / office op-logs) on tab delete and compact the Univer op-log; GC stale localStorage graph positions for deleted nodes.
improvements.why: All three are unbounded growth that degrade collab sync size and relay storage over a document's lifetime.

improvements.what: Make missing-i18n-key fallback render-safe (last segment, not full path) and add a server-readable locale cookie to kill the English FOUC; consider adding zh-TW if Traditional Chinese is a target market.
improvements.why: Improves perceived polish for non-English users and decouples i18n display from type-detection logic.

improvements.what: Reconsider allow-scripts on shared/published HTML embeds (e.g. strip scripts for public share views, or require explicit opt-in).
improvements.why: Public share is a trust boundary where one author's JS runs in every viewer's browser.

subResults.data_flow: "Server components fetch the document (docs/[id]/page.tsx forwards request headers/cookies to the internal /api/documents/{id}) or the list client-fetches via memory-store. Editors hydrate from doc.metadata (docTabs / mindmap / univer snapshots). Edits flow: editor onChange -> in-memory refs (blocksByTab / univerByTab / lastJsonRef) -> debounced (800ms) PATCH /api/documents/{id} writing flat plaintext (content, for RAG/search) + structured metadata. Structural changes (add/delete/rename tab) persist immediately via saveNow. On unmount, navigator.sendBeacon hits /process to re-index. When NEXT_PUBLIC_COLLAB_WS_URL is set, a collab token is fetched (/api/documents/{id}/collab-token) and a Hocuspocus provider (room = docId) syncs a Y.Doc: notes via XML fragments, sheets via an op-log Y.Array, mindmaps via a single Y.Map JSON key; awareness drives presence. The knowledge graph is a separate flow: knowledge-dashboard fetches /api/knowledge/graph, dedupes by structural signature, renders via force-graph, and listens on /api/events/stream (SSE) to silently refresh on document/ingest events; node clicks fetch /api/knowledge/node/{id} for the detail panel. Version history reads /api/documents/{id}/versions and restore POSTs then full-page-reloads to re-seed editors."

key_files.role: Multi-tab document editor: BlockNote notes (true Yjs CRDT) + Univer sheets + full-page HTML, single-user and collab variants, persistence, presence, version-history entry. The most complex and best-engineered file in the subsystem.
Univer spreadsheet host with StrictMode-safe mount/dispose and best-effort op-log collaboration over Yjs (LWW, unbounded log).
mind-elixir mindmap editor with whole-blob LWW collab and no token refresh — the weakest collab path.
Knowledge-graph canvas on react-force-graph-2d with hand-rolled hit-testing, drag-to-pin layout persisted to localStorage, theme-aware rendering.
Graph data orchestration: fetch + structural-signature dedup + SSE live refresh + node-detail panel wiring.
Zustand store for the document/memory list: pagination, server+client filtering/sorting, optimistic CRUD with rollback.
Hand-rolled i18n: zustand+persist locale store, dot-path JSON resolver with raw-key fallback, useTranslation hook.
Main list/grid view + gallery + in-place editor switch; the primary over-rendering / redundant-compute hotspot.
Version list with line-diff preview and restore (full reload to re-seed).
4-locale translation catalogs, 901 leaf keys each, full parity.

subResults.subsystem: apps/web/lib — core intelligence pipeline (agents, ultrarag, ingest, edgequake client, zvec, versions, collab, relay)
subResults.purpose: The web app's brain: ingest content (file/URL/image/video) → AI-enrich (summary, entities, tags, categories) → index into EdgeQuake (Rust RAG over shared pgvector+AGE) → retrieve on chat with app-layer visibility re-filtering → orchestrate LLM answer/create/share actions, plus offline relay sync and document version history.
subResults.architecture: Two clearly separated layers. (1) The HOT, wired path: app/api/chat/route.ts → agents/pipeline.ts runPipeline(). Pipeline is a regex-first router: detectIntent() classifies create|share|recommend|search|explain|general across 4 languages with pure regex (no LLM), then branches. create/share act directly on Postgres via doc-actions.ts (in-process, no HTTP). search/general run searchKnowledge() (EdgeQuake vector query → Postgres visibility re-filter → keyword fallback → catalog fallback) then generateAnswer() streams via chat-router.ts. chat-router cascades: user cloud providers (cloud-chat.ts, OpenAI-compatible SSE, with OCP/Codex relay branch) → AI server (NestJS :4000) on 400/402/429. (2) The INGEST path: ingest/job-queue.ts processJob() is a fixed 5-step state machine (metadata→entities→categories→edgequake index→related-docs) with per-step failure tracking, in-memory concurrency semaphore (MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS=10), exponential-backoff setTimeout retries, and DB-table job state. ai-processor.ts wraps cloud-ai.ts callAiCloudFirst for all enrichment. edgequake/client.ts is a thin fetch wrapper hardcoding a SINGLE shared workspace/tenant for all users. Versions (versions/store.ts) and relay (relay/sync-service.ts encrypt→push/pull→conflict-resolve) are independent. DEAD/secondary: agents/orchestrator.ts, agents/langgraph.ts (zero callers), zvec/engine.ts (tests only), ultrarag/* (wired only to /api/pipeline).
whats_good: pipeline.ts searchKnowledge() does defense-in-depth: every EdgeQuake hit is re-filtered through Postgres readableClause() (pipeline.ts:586-601) before reaching the user — essential since the EdgeQuake index is a single shared tenant for ALL users (edgequake/client.ts:11-12).

job-queue.ts has genuinely thoughtful resilience: isDocumentAlive() liveness checks before each expensive step (lines 231,287,311,382), per-step failure flags with a 'both core steps died → retry, single failure → partial complete' policy (lines 225,457-461), and skips paid LLM calls when an OCP fast-path already filled summary (line 238-249).
Good SSRF hardening in url-fetcher.ts validateUrl(): DNS-resolves the host and rejects private/loopback/link-local/metadata ranges (lines 24-72) before fetching.
doc-actions.ts avoids an HTTP round-trip by writing editor-exact metadata shapes (docTabs/univer/mindmap) directly — and only the owner can share (user_id check, doc-actions.ts:278).
versions/store.ts is clean and well-reasoned: throttle + content-dedup + MAX_VERSIONS prune in one capture point, injectable db for tests, best-effort by contract.
cloud-chat.ts correctly handles streaming <think>/reasoning_content filtering across providers and folds the relay (OCP/Codex) path into the same onToken contract.
ultrarag validator.ts is solid — real cycle detection (DFS), duplicate-id and timeout validation.

risks.title: Entity knowledge-graph collides and cross-links across ALL users/orgs
risks.detail: insertEntities() inserts only (document_id,name,type,confidence,metadata) and relies on column defaults for tenant_id/workspace_id. The table constraint is UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) (db/init/01-edgequake-init.sql:155), and migration 049 only ADDED document_id without changing the constraint. So every web-app entity inserts as (NULL,NULL,name) → user A's 'React' and user B's 'React' are the SAME row. ON CONFLICT keeps document_id = COALESCE(existing, new) — the FIRST writer's document wins the linkage. Any entity→document graph view leaks one user's doc to another and silently corrupts confidence/metadata. This is the 'two data models' tension manifesting as a live data bug.

risks.title: EdgeQuake results are trusted WITHOUT visibility re-filter in secondary code paths
risks.detail: Because all users share one EdgeQuake workspace/tenant, isolation depends entirely on the post-query readableClause re-filter that ONLY pipeline.ts performs. orchestrator.ts executeStep('search') returns eqResult.sources snippets directly (orchestrator.ts:122), and ultrarag executor.ts 'search' returns queryEdgeQuake output raw (executor.ts:138-144) — neither re-filters by user/org. job-queue related-docs linking also trusts EdgeQuake document_ids cross-user (job-queue.ts:431-442). orchestrator/langgraph are currently dead, but /api/pipeline (ultrarag) and the related-docs linker are live: a user can get document_relations rows pointing at another tenant's doc id.

risks.title: Hand-rolled YAML parser cannot parse pipeline step lists — /api/pipeline broken for YAML
risks.detail: parseSimpleYaml()'s array handler does currentArray.push(parseScalar(value)) — it can only build arrays of scalars, never arrays-of-maps. But the validator REQUIRES steps to be an array of objects each with id/type/config. A real `steps:` block (list of maps) parses each `- id: x` into the scalar string 'id: x', so validation always fails. The YAML path is effectively dead; only JSON request bodies work, despite the public framing as a YAML pipeline engine.

risks.title: Streaming chat does NOT fall back on transient 5xx (policy diverges from non-streaming)
risks.detail: routeChat only sets shouldFallback for FALLBACK_CODES = {400,402,429} (chat-router.ts:19,156). A cloud provider 500/502/503 leaves shouldFallback=false → 'All cloud providers failed' is thrown and the user gets nothing, even though the AI server cascade is healthy. The non-streaming twin callAiCloudFirst ALWAYS falls back (cloud-ai.ts:236-248). Same path also mis-classifies: extractHttpStatus greps the first 4xx/5xx-looking number anywhere in the error string (chat-router.ts:22-24), so a status inside a provider error body can flip the decision.

risks.title: Ingest jobs are orphaned on process restart — no sweeper
risks.detail: createJob() fires processJobById() as fire-and-forget; the concurrency semaphore (activeJobs/jobWaiters) and retry scheduling (setTimeout, line 491) are pure in-process state. If the Node process restarts (deploy, crash, serverless teardown) while a job is 'processing' or waiting on a setTimeout retry, nothing ever re-drives it — the ingestion_jobs row is stuck forever and the document never gets indexed. There is no startup reconciliation of stale pending/processing rows.

risks.title: EdgeQuake indexing in the hot ingest path runs synchronously under a 30s timeout
risks.detail: job-queue.ts indexes with async_processing:false (line 394) against a client with EDGEQUAKE_TIMEOUT=30s (client.ts:8). Large documents whose chunking+graph extraction exceed 30s will throw, flag edgequake_sync_failed, and (if metadata also failed) fail the whole job — even though async_processing:true (used everywhere else, e.g. syncUnindexedToEdgeQuake) would have succeeded. Inconsistent and the slow path picked the blocking option.

risks.title: runPipeline() is launched un-awaited and un-caught inside ReadableStream.start
risks.detail: chat/route.ts:106 calls runPipeline({...}) with no .catch. runPipeline has an internal try/catch/finally that closes the writer, so normal errors are contained, but any throw escaping that (e.g. writer.close() itself, or a synchronous error constructing the pipeline) becomes an unhandled rejection with the SSE controller left open. Also the pipeline never receives request.signal, so on client disconnect the LLM stream keeps consuming paid tokens.

risks.title: Relay 'encrypted' sync depends on encryptForUser which has a base64 dev fallback
risks.detail: sync-service.ts encrypts every pushed payload via encryptForUser (line 111) and the system is marketed as encrypted offline-sync. Per project context, lib/encryption has a base64 dev fallback (not real crypto). If RELAY/Lit keys are unset, document payloads traverse the relay base64-encoded, not encrypted — a silent confidentiality downgrade with no guard/warning at the sync layer.

code_review.issue: insertEntities omits tenant_id/workspace_id, so ON CONFLICT (tenant_id,workspace_id,name) NULLS NOT DISTINCT merges all users' same-named entities into one row; document_id = COALESCE keeps the first user's doc.
code_review.suggested_fix: Either add a web-specific unique constraint scoped by document_id/organization_id, or pass the org's tenant/workspace into the insert. At minimum change the conflict target to (document_id, name) for web-origin entities so cross-document/cross-user merges can't happen.

code_review.issue: parseSimpleYaml builds arrays of scalars only; cannot represent the list-of-maps that `steps:` requires, so all real YAML pipelines fail validation.
code_review.suggested_fix: Adopt js-yaml (already implied by the TODO comment) and delete the hand-rolled parser, or explicitly document/enforce JSON-only at /api/pipeline.

code_review.issue: FALLBACK_CODES excludes 5xx, so transient cloud 500/503 throws to the user instead of cascading to the AI server; behavior diverges from cloud-ai.ts which always falls back.
code_review.suggested_fix: Add 500,502,503,504 to the fallback set (or fall back on any non-2xx after exhausting providers), matching callAiCloudFirst semantics.

code_review.issue: Search step returns raw EdgeQuake snippets with no readableClause re-filter; given the shared EdgeQuake tenant this leaks other users' content. Same in executor.ts:138.
code_review.suggested_fix: Route all EdgeQuake retrieval through a single helper that re-resolves doc ids against Postgres readableClause(userId,orgId) before returning text, exactly as pipeline.ts does.

code_review.issue: Retries scheduled via setTimeout in-process; lost on restart. Combined with fire-and-forget createJob, there is no durable re-drive of stuck jobs.
code_review.suggested_fix: Add a startup/cron sweeper that re-queues ingestion_jobs WHERE status IN ('pending','processing') AND updated_at < now()-interval, instead of relying on live timers.

code_review.issue: Bare `catch {}` swallows EdgeQuake and metadata-enrichment errors, logging only a generic 'unavailable' — real failure causes (auth, dimension mismatch, 5xx) are invisible in production.
code_review.suggested_fix: Capture (err) and writer.log/console.warn the message; keep the graceful fallback but stop discarding the diagnostic.

code_review.issue: handleShare matches by `$3 ILIKE '%' || title || '%'` using the DB title as a LIKE pattern; titles containing % or _ over-match, and the lookup is user_id-only so team members can't share team-visible docs they can edit.
code_review.suggested_fix: Escape LIKE metacharacters in title, and widen ownership to readableClause/editable scope for the team edition.

code_review.issue: Box-Muller uses Math.log(u1) where u1=Math.random() can be 0 → -Infinity → NaN hyperplane entries, silently corrupting an LSH table. (Module is test-only today.)
code_review.suggested_fix: Guard u1 with (Math.random() || Number.MIN_VALUE), or drop zvec entirely since it's unused outside tests.

code_review.issue: generateAnswer docCount counts WHERE organization_id=$1 with no visibility filter, so the figure injected into the system prompt includes other members' private docs.
code_review.suggested_fix: Apply readableClause to the count, or accept it's only a number and document that.

improvements.what: Delete or quarantine the dead intelligence modules: orchestrator.ts, langgraph.ts, and zvec/engine.ts have zero production callers.
improvements.why: They masquerade as core 'agentic orchestration' but are unmaintained, use a different AI-server request contract ({system,message} vs {messages:[]}), and most dangerously model the unsafe pattern of trusting raw EdgeQuake output. Removing them shrinks the audit surface and kills a leakage footgun.

improvements.what: Centralize EdgeQuake retrieval behind one visibility-enforcing function and forbid direct queryEdgeQuake() consumption of snippets.
improvements.why: Tenant isolation is app-layer-only and the EdgeQuake index is a single shared workspace; today only pipeline.ts re-filters. One choke point makes the security property auditable instead of per-call.

improvements.what: Fix the entities tenant/workspace collision (constraint or insert).
improvements.why: The knowledge graph is currently cross-user-corrupting and a graph-view leak vector — the most serious correctness bug in this subsystem.

improvements.what: Make ingest job state durable: startup sweeper + DB-backed retry instead of setTimeout; consider a real queue (pg-boss/BullMQ).
improvements.why: Fire-and-forget + in-memory semaphore + timer retries silently drop work on every deploy/restart, leaving documents permanently unindexed with no visibility.

improvements.what: Unify the LLM fallback policy between routeChat (streaming) and callAiCloudFirst (non-streaming), including 5xx handling and structured status extraction.
improvements.why: Today streaming chat hard-fails on transient cloud 5xx while background calls recover; users see inconsistent reliability for the same provider outage.

improvements.what: Replace the regex intent/title/topic engine (pipeline.ts ~lines 36-271) with a small structured LLM classifier or at least consolidate the 4-language pattern tables.
improvements.why: Hundreds of lines of brittle multilingual regex silently misroute create/share/search; it's the highest-maintenance, lowest-confidence part of the hot path.

improvements.what: Swap parseSimpleYaml for js-yaml (or make /api/pipeline JSON-only and say so).
improvements.why: The advertised YAML pipeline format does not actually parse its own primary construct.

tech_debt: Two abandoned orchestrators (orchestrator.ts executeAgenticQuery, langgraph.ts LangGraphOrchestrator) with no callers and a stale AI-server request shape.
zvec/engine.ts is a complete LSH vector engine referenced only by p52 tests — dead weight presented as a feature.

subResults.purpose: HTTP/REST + SSE API surface for the web app: documents/search/knowledge-graph CRUD, AI chat, ingestion, sharing (decentralized/IPFS), collab tokens, integrations (Telegram, OAuth connectors, OCP/Codex relay), admin, model management, and the better-auth catch-all. Most handlers authenticate the caller, resolve org/tenant context, delegate to lib/, and enforce isolation in SQL via parameterized visibility clauses.
subResults.architecture: Two-tier auth: (1) lib/ingest/session-helper.ts:getUserIdFromRequest() tries better-auth session first, then falls back to an MCP bearer key (sk-mcp-*) looked up in user_mcp_keys; (2) lib/org-context.ts:getOrgContext() wraps that to also resolve the caller's active organization + role from the member table in one query. Tenant isolation is app-layer SQL: lib/visibility.ts exposes composable clause builders (visibilityClause/readableClause/writableClause/orgScopeClause/sharedWithClause/teamSharedClause/editableViaShareClause) that callers splice into queries with explicit $N placeholder indices and a static alias. Admin routes use a separate lib/admin.ts (getSession + requireAdmin role check). Reads use readableClause (own OR org-shared OR per-user share OR team share); writes use writableClause (creator or org admin) OR editableViaShareClause. The documented Postgres 42P18 indeterminate-datatype pitfall is correctly pre-empted in writableClause by forcing the admin branch to reference $userParam via `$N::text IS NOT NULL`. Errors return a structured {code,message,timestamp} envelope (lib/types ErrorCode) with 401/403/404/400/429/500. SSE endpoints (chat, events/stream, notifications/stream, models/pull, desktop/runtime) use ReadableStream + text/event-stream; events/stream filters an in-process EventEmitter by userId. The pattern is consistent and disciplined on the core data routes, but a cluster of utility/integration/desktop routes bypass auth entirely or under-validate.
whats_good: Core data routes (documents, search, knowledge/graph, share, ingest/text) consistently resolve getOrgContext() and splice readableClause/writableClause into fully parameterized queries — no string-interpolated user values into SQL on these paths; tenant isolation is coherent and centralized in lib/visibility.ts.

The documented Postgres 42P18 (indeterminate_datatype) trap is genuinely handled, not just commented: writableClause forces the admin branch to give $userParam a type via `$${userParam}::text IS NOT NULL` (visibility.ts:61-63), so callers can always pass userId regardless of role.

PATCH /api/documents/:id wraps category reassignment + document update + tag sync in a single transaction with a SAVEPOINT around the optional tags sync, so a missing tags migration degrades gracefully without failing the save (documents/[id]/route.ts:159-262).
Consistent structured error envelope with ErrorCode enum and ISO timestamps across nearly all data routes; 401 vs 403 vs 404 are distinguished correctly in admin paths.

search/route.ts deliberately refuses to return an uncited EdgeQuake answer (EdgeQuake is a shared workspace) and re-runs a Postgres-scoped fallback so cross-tenant synthesized text can't leak (search/route.ts:130-135) — a thoughtful isolation decision.
og/[id] gates image serving on privacy_level==='shared' and returns a placeholder for private docs to avoid a document-existence oracle (og/[id]/route.ts:28-34).
Telegram webhook has real idempotency (in-memory claim + telegram_processed_updates upsert) and per-bot token resolution to avoid replying from the wrong bot.

risks.title: Unauthenticated diagnostic route creates real users and leaks auth env config
risks.detail: GET /api/auth/test returns the values of BETTER_AUTH_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, TRUSTED_ORIGINS and which secrets are set — no auth. POST /api/auth/test calls auth.api.signUpEmail() to create a real persisted user on every hit; the code comment says 'Clean up: delete the test user' but no deletion ever happens, so it is an unauthenticated user-creation / DB-pollution / DoS endpoint. Ships in the web app with no env guard.

risks.title: Unauthenticated global LLM system-prompt overwrite (stored prompt injection)
risks.detail: POST /api/settings/prompts has zero auth and writes a single global .sayknowmind-prompts.json (process.cwd()) that loadPrompts() feeds into chat + document-processing system prompts for ALL users. Any anonymous caller can rewrite every user's system prompt (data exfiltration, jailbreak, defacement). It is also a single shared file at cwd, so it is per-instance/ephemeral on multi-instance or serverless deploys.

risks.title: Unauthenticated desktop runtime route runs shell commands and spawns servers
risks.detail: GET/POST /api/desktop/runtime has no auth check at all and uses execSync/execFile to run `which`, `docker --version`, `ollama`, `git`, `tar -xzf`, `cp -r`, `pnpm build`, `rm -rf`, `lsof|xargs kill -9`, downloads a Node.js tarball over the network and extracts+executes it, and spawns a detached server with a freshly minted BETTER_AUTH_SECRET. It is intended for the Tauri desktop (localhost) but there is no NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_MODE / desktop env guard, so if the route is present in a hosted build it is an unauthenticated remote command/abuse surface.

risks.title: MCP API keys stored and compared in plaintext, DDL on hot path
risks.detail: user_mcp_keys stores api_key as plaintext TEXT and getUserIdFromMcpKey authenticates by a plaintext equality SELECT (no hashing, timing-unsafe). A DB read leak (backup, log, SQL injection elsewhere) exposes live credentials directly. Keys never expire and there is no rotation/audit beyond a single key per user. Additionally ensureTable() runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on every GET/POST of /api/user/mcp-key.

risks.title: IDOR on category assignment — no tenant check on categoryId
risks.detail: assignDocumentCategory() does a raw INSERT into document_categories with no ownership/org check on either id. POST /api/ingest/text passes a caller-supplied categoryId straight through (ingest/text/route.ts:67-68), letting a user attach their document to an arbitrary category id, including another tenant's. Read paths filter categories via readableClause so content does not leak back, but it writes cross-tenant rows into document_categories and is a missing-authz write. Contrast the Telegram 'c:' callback which DOES verify user_id before assigning.

risks.title: SSRF via OG image fetcher
risks.detail: og/[id] server-side fetch()es doc.url (user-controlled at ingest) to scrape og:image whenever no cached image exists, gated only by privacy_level==='shared' and url.startsWith('http'). No IP/host allowlist or private-range blocking, so a shared doc with url=http://169.254.169.254/... or an internal host turns the server into an SSRF proxy (5s timeout limits but does not prevent it).

risks.title: Telegram webhook secret is optional
risks.detail: Both the legacy and per-bot webhook handlers only enforce x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token when process.env.TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set. With it unset (the default), anyone who knows a numeric botId can POST forged Telegram updates that drive ingestion, AI calls (burning the linked user's daily quota), and category assignment for already-linked users.

risks.title: OAuth callback trusts state.userId with no session present
risks.detail: When no better-auth session cookie is present, the connectors OAuth callback authenticates purely from the HMAC-signed `state` (userId = verified.userId) to support the desktop external-browser flow. Security then rests entirely on BETTER_AUTH_SECRET secrecy and the 10-min TTL; there is no nonce/single-use binding, so a captured state within its TTL can be replayed to bind tokens. Acceptable for desktop but worth a single-use nonce.

risks.title: Invitation details (invitee email) disclosed by UUID with no auth
risks.detail: GET /api/invitations/:id returns the invitee email, role, status and organization name to any unauthenticated caller who has the invitation id. Intentional ('public-safe' to render the accept page) but it discloses an email address keyed only on a guessable-if-leaked UUID.

risks.title: Unauthenticated Ollama model pull
risks.detail: POST /api/models/pull has no auth and streams an Ollama model pull for any caller-supplied name — resource/disk abuse when an Ollama backend is reachable.

subResults.data_flow: Client -> route handler -> getOrgContext()/getUserIdFromRequest() (better-auth session cookie OR sk-mcp-* bearer -> user_mcp_keys -> member table for org+role) -> checkAntiBot() rate limit -> JSON/query-param parse + ad-hoc type guards -> pool.query() with parameterized SQL where visibility.ts clauses splice ctx.userId/ctx.organizationId at fixed $N positions for tenant isolation -> delegate to lib/ (agents/pipeline, ingest/*, shared-mode, edgequake/client, versions/store) -> structured JSON or SSE stream. Events flow back via an in-process EventEmitter (lib/events) filtered by userId in events/stream. Cross-service: search calls EdgeQuake (shared workspace, results re-filtered through readableClause); chat/telegram call the LLM provider cascade (per-user encrypted providers, OCP/Codex relay via llm-relay poll/respond long-poll). Tenant isolation is enforced entirely in application SQL — Postgres RLS is inert per project context.

subResults.purpose: Stateless HTTP AI gateway for the web app: multi-provider LLM chat with cascade fallback (streaming + sync), OCR ingestion, web search enrichment, and a Redis-backed "memory" layer (user profile/facts, session context, entity store, pseudo-semantic memory, global learned patterns) plus a span/analytics/learning telemetry pipeline. Web (apps/web/lib/agents/*) calls POST /ai/chat over HTTP as a fallback when no cloud provider key is configured or cloud returns 400/402/429.
subResults.architecture: Standard NestJS module graph. AppModule wires AiModule (AIRouterService + 8 provider services: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Grok, Venice, Upstage, Nvidia, Z.AI, Cloudflare), MemoryModule (RedisService + UserMemory, SessionContext, EntityStore, SemanticMemory, GlobalLearning, ContextBuilder), IntelligenceModule (Span/Tracer/Adapter/Algorithm/Analytics/Feedback/GDPR), OcrModule, SearchModule, KnowledgeModule. Single class-level SignatureGuard on AiController authenticates every route with one shared AI_API_KEY (or RSA-signature legacy path, or SKIP_AUTH bypass). Provider routing: AIRouterService.chatWithCascade picks a cascade list (pro/flash/thinking) loaded from data/cascade.json or hardcoded defaults, then tries each {type,model} in order via tryModel/tryStreamModel; streaming uses a wrapper EventEmitter (chatStreamWithAutoFallback) that falls through to the next model only if a model errors/ends-empty before emitting data. Memory model: ALL state lives in Redis with sliding TTLs (spans 7d, session ctx 24h/history 7d, user memory 30d, entities 60d, semantic 90d, aggregations 30d) — there is NO durable (Postgres) backing; if REDIS_URL is unset or Redis drops, the entire memory/learning layer becomes a graceful no-op. Keys are namespaced via MemoryKeysHelper with optional org prefix (org:{orgId}:user:{userId}:*) falling back to legacy un-prefixed keys. ContextBuilder assembles the final system prompt from user-memory summary + session summary + topics + branding rules; the controller loads memory in parallel (Promise.all) on each request and asynchronously updates memory after the response.
whats_good: Graceful degradation is pervasive and consistent: every memory/learning method checks redis.isReady() and returns null/[]/no-op, so the AI path keeps working with Redis down (redis.service.ts:77, repeated across all services). RedisService also rate-limits error logging to once/min (redis.service.ts:50).

Cascade fallback design is clean and provider-agnostic: tryModel/tryStreamModel encapsulate per-provider readiness checks and the cascade lists are externally configurable via data/cascade.json with hardcoded defaults (ai-router.service.ts:258-295).

Streaming fallback correctly distinguishes pre-data vs post-data errors — it only fails over to the next model if no bytes were emitted yet, avoiding duplicated partial output (ai-router.service.ts:608-628).
Sensitive-data redaction on span ingestion (API keys, email, phone, card, password) with recursive metadata sanitization and sensitive-key dropping (span.service.ts:282-431).

Cost-aware memory extraction: rule/pattern/semantic extraction run free first, and the expensive LLM extraction is gated by message-count cadence + keyword triggers (user-memory.service.ts:215-227, entity-store.service.ts:349-372).

Org-namespacing was retrofitted in a backward-compatible way via a single centralized key builder (memory-keys.helper.ts), and multilingual (ko/ja/zh/en/vi/th) keyword and identity-question coverage is broad.

risks.title: Caller-supplied identity under a single shared key = cross-tenant IDOR on memory
risks.detail: userId, sessionId and organizationId are taken straight from the request body (chat.dto.ts:23-43) / path params, while the only auth is one shared AI_API_KEY for all callers (signature.guard.ts:21-46) — or fully bypassed when SKIP_AUTH=true (signature.guard.ts:35). Any holder of the shared key (or anyone, in SKIP_AUTH/dev) can read, write, or delete ANY user's memory by passing an arbitrary userId. GET /ai/memory/:userId and DELETE /ai/memory/:userId expose this directly (ai.controller.ts:1048-1064). This mirrors the project's known app-layer-only tenancy gap, now reproduced in the AI server.

risks.title: GDPR / memory read+delete endpoints ignore organizationId → silently miss org-scoped data
risks.detail: getUserMemory, deleteUserMemory, getSessionContext, deleteSession never pass organizationId, so they only touch the legacy un-prefixed keys (user:{id}:memory). But the chat path writes org-prefixed keys when organizationId is present (memory-keys.helper.ts:28-32). Result: for any org user, the read endpoint returns 'no memory' and the GDPR delete leaves org:{orgId}:user:{id}:* data behind. AdapterService.deleteUserAggregations only scans metrics:user:{id}:* and ignores span:* and org-prefixed metrics (adapter.service.ts:862-884). GDPR erasure is incomplete.

risks.title: new RegExp on learned/stored patterns → ReDoS and unhandled throws
risks.detail: GlobalLearning compiles user/feedback-derived pattern strings directly: new RegExp(pattern.pattern,'i') in findMatchingAction (global-learning.service.ts:286) and learnFromFeedback (global-learning.service.ts:453), with learnPattern accepting arbitrary pattern text (global-learning.service.ts:400-435). A malformed pattern throws (rejecting the async chain) and a crafted alternation can cause catastrophic backtracking on every matching request. No try/catch around RegExp construction.

risks.title: Memory is ephemeral, not a 'second brain' — no durable store and no auto-recovery
risks.detail: All user knowledge lives in Redis with TTLs and no Postgres backing; a Redis flush/eviction permanently loses every user's profile, facts, entities and learnings. Worse, the client is configured reconnectOnError:false and retryStrategy returns null after 3 attempts (redis.service.ts:29-37), so once the connection is lost it never re-establishes until the process restarts — memory goes dark silently mid-run.

risks.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of the global:learnings blob on a hot path
risks.detail: incrementPatternUsage runs fire-and-forget on EVERY matching query and does a full getLearnings()+saveLearnings() of the entire pattern array (global-learning.service.ts:297,377-395); learnPattern/learnFromFeedback/saveLearnings do the same. Concurrent requests race on one JSON key with last-writer-wins, dropping occurrence counts and confidence updates, plus heavy write amplification.

risks.title: Stale modelUsed reported on streaming fallback
risks.detail: chatStreamWithAutoFallback returns modelUsed read synchronously after the first model starts; later fallbacks triggered by post-start 'error'/'empty' events update finalModelUsed but the value already returned to the controller is stale, so the span trace and model-specific branding record the wrong model when a fallback occurs.

code_review.issue: shouldEnableFeatures() invokes checkGlobalLearningPatterns(query).then(...) but returns the recommendation synchronously BEFORE the promise resolves (lines 230-260). The .then callback mutates enableSearch/searchConfidence after the function has already returned, so the GlobalLearning enrichment NEVER affects the result. Pure dead logic + floating promise.
code_review.suggested_fix: Make shouldEnableFeatures async and await checkGlobalLearningPatterns before computing the final confidence/return, or remove the dead enrichment block.

code_review.issue: getRecentSpansForLearning() does not read real spans. It reads cached global metrics modelDistribution and fabricates span-like objects with success:true hardcoded (lines 393-412). But metrics:global modelDistribution is never written anywhere in the repo (grep confirms only readers in adapter.service.ts:365 and algorithm.service.ts:399), so getGlobalMetrics('24h') is null and the function always returns []. learnPatterns() therefore always returns {patternsLearned:0,patternsApplied:0} — the entire pattern-learning subsystem is non-functional, and when it 'works' it learns from fabricated all-success data.
code_review.suggested_fix: Inject SpanService and query real completed spans via findMany; remove the fabricated success:true objects. Either implement a writer for global modelDistribution or delete the dead read paths.

code_review.issue: Latent TypeError: aggregateByModel reads cachedGlobal.modelDistribution.length (line 365) guarded only by truthiness of cachedGlobal. If a GlobalMetrics object is ever cached without a modelDistribution field (the AggregatedMetrics written by saveAggregatedMetrics has no such field), this throws.
code_review.suggested_fix: Guard with cachedGlobal?.modelDistribution?.length and converge the AggregatedMetrics vs GlobalMetrics shapes.

code_review.issue: SemanticMemoryService is not semantic: getEmbedding requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY to be set (line 51) then ignores it and returns a 128-dim hash-bucket bag-of-words vector (generateSimpleEmbedding, 68-104). Cosine over hash buckets ≈ keyword overlap, not meaning, and the whole feature silently disables itself if the unused key is absent. Also double normalization (vector L2-normalized at 96-101, then cosineSimilarity re-normalizes 122-137).
code_review.suggested_fix: Either call a real embedding API (the key is already required) or rename to KeywordMemory and drop the misleading key gate; remove redundant normalization.

code_review.issue: Memory pollution / false positives: extractByPatterns name regex /I'm ([a-zA-Z]+)/ (line 378) captures 'fine' from 'I'm fine'; extractBySemantic stores arbitrary sentence fragments as facts at 0.75 confidence (lines 500-526). LLM-extracted JSON is parsed with a permissive {...} regex and trusted (extractWithAI 256-261), persisting hallucinated facts.
code_review.suggested_fix: Tighten name/occupation patterns with stop-word filters, lower default confidence for heuristic facts, validate AI JSON against a schema, and require corroboration before persisting profile fields.

code_review.issue: recommendModel session-consistency block (lines 163-170) computes previousModelInAlternatives and only logs; it never alters the chosen model. Dead code.
code_review.suggested_fix: Implement the intended previous-model preference or remove the block; drop unused userId/sessionId params on chatWithCascade (ai-router.service.ts:188-194) too.

code_review.issue: Per-request memory loading is a sequence of N+1 Redis round-trips (each get*Summary/getContext also issues a separate EXPIRE), and SpanService.findMany loops findById per span id (span.service.ts:184-189), making analytics aggregation O(spans) GETs. Hot-path latency and Redis load scale poorly.
code_review.suggested_fix: Batch with MGET/pipelining, fold the sliding-TTL EXPIRE into the read via a pipeline, and cap analytics scans.

code_review.issue: processPDF throws on error (line 176) while processImage returns a friendly string — inconsistent, though processFile's outer try/catch masks it. Base64 images up to the 10MB express limit are fully decoded in memory and resized via native sharp with no additional guard; sharp also has the known macOS quarantine fragility noted in project memory.
code_review.suggested_fix: Make processPDF return a friendly string like processImage, add an explicit decoded-size guard before sharp, and document the sharp xattr workaround in deployment.

improvements.what: Derive userId/organizationId from the authenticated principal (per-client key or signed token claims), not from request body/path; scope every memory read/write/delete to that principal
improvements.why: Closes the cross-tenant IDOR and makes the org namespace a real trust boundary instead of a caller hint

improvements.what: Thread organizationId through the GET/DELETE memory & session endpoints and make GDPR deletion scan all key families (memory, entities, semantic, session, spans, metrics) for both legacy and org-prefixed schemes
improvements.why: Current GDPR erasure and reads silently miss org-scoped data — a compliance and correctness hole

improvements.why: Three interlocking subsystems are currently dead or fed fabricated data, giving a false impression of adaptive learning

improvements.why: A 'second brain' that evaporates on a Redis eviction or a dropped connection is not durable memory

subResults.subsystem: packages/edgequake — Rust RAG engine internals (core / storage / pipeline / query)
subResults.purpose: A LightRAG-inspired Rust RAG engine providing document ingestion (chunk → LLM entity/relationship extraction → embedding), pgvector-backed vector similarity search, an Apache AGE knowledge graph, and a multi-mode query engine (naive/local/global/hybrid/mix/bypass) with keyword extraction, reranking, and token budgeting. Provider-agnostic (embedding/LLM/reranker traits live in the external edgequake-llm 0.2.7 crate). Designed for multi-tenant/multi-workspace operation with per-workspace vector tables of independent dimensions.
subResults.architecture: Clean Cargo workspace of 9 crates with sensible layering: edgequake-core (orchestrator, types, multitenancy, query routing) depends on edgequake-storage (trait-based adapters: VectorStorage / GraphStorage / KvStorage / WorkspaceVectorRegistry, each with a Postgres and an in-memory impl) and edgequake-pipeline (chunker → extractor[simple/llm/sota/gleaning] → merger → embeddings → lineage). edgequake-query holds the SOTAQueryEngine. Provider abstraction is fully trait-driven (EmbeddingProvider/LLMProvider/Reranker from edgequake-llm) and injected as Arc<dyn>, so storage and providers are swappable. Storage adapters use async_trait over sqlx PgPool. Multi-tenancy is modeled three ways at once: (a) per-namespace physical tables/graphs (eq_<ns>_vectors, eq_<ns>_graph), (b) per-workspace physical vector tables via WorkspaceVectorRegistry, and (c) app-layer metadata/property filtering in the query engine. The pipeline exposes three resilience tiers (process / process_with_progress / process_with_resilience) sharing DRY helpers. Vector search returns mixed entity/relationship/chunk rows from one table, disambiguated post-hoc by a metadata "type" filter (vector_filter.rs) rather than separate tables.
whats_good: Strong trait-based seams: VectorStorage/GraphStorage/WorkspaceVectorRegistry + EmbeddingProvider/LLMProvider/Reranker injected as Arc<dyn>, giving genuine provider/storage swappability and an in-memory adapter for tests (adapters/memory/*).

Thoughtful dimension-migration handling for provider switches: get_stored_dimension() reads pg_attribute.atttypmod so it works on empty tables, and ensure_dimension() DROP+recreates on mismatch (vector.rs:155-341) — a real-world pain point handled deliberately.

Query engine is well-documented and faithful to LightRAG: low/high-level keyword embeddings drive local/global modes, with batch graph fetches (get_nodes_batch, node_degrees_batch) and round-robin hybrid merge (vector_queries.rs:456-563).
Per-query graph correctness fixes are visible and reasoned (deterministic ordering via Vec not HashMap; OODA-230/231 fallbacks to popular nodes so chunk collection isn't skipped).
AGE performance awareness: native SQL degree queries instead of slow Cypher OPTIONAL MATCH, plus an explicit index-creation pass on both "Node"/"EDGE" and _ag_label_* tables (helpers.rs:335-486).
Pipeline resilience tier isolates per-chunk failures, tracks timeouts/retries, and downgrades 0-entity results from hard error to warning so embedding-only docs still index (processing.rs:143-258).

risks.title: Vector-search tenant filter is fail-OPEN — cross-tenant data leak
risks.detail: matches_tenant_filter returns true when a vector's metadata lacks a tenant_id/workspace_id key — it only rejects on a present-but-mismatched key. Any vector stored without these metadata keys is visible to EVERY tenant's query. This is inconsistent with the graph node path which is fail-CLOSED (excludes nodes lacking tenant_id, mod.rs:1273-1291) and the graph edge path which is fail-open (r.tenant_id IS NULL OR ...=, mod.rs:1396-1402). Three different isolation policies in one engine. When the shared default vector table is used, the SQL query passes filter_ids=None (no SQL-level tenant predicate), so cross-tenant rows are fetched first and only weakly filtered afterward — causing both leakage and recall loss (other tenants' rows displace valid ones from top-k).

risks.title: Cypher injection via $$ dollar-quote breakout
risks.detail: All Cypher is embedded into outer SQL as cypher('graph', $$ <cypher> $$). escape_cypher_string escapes ', ", \, \n/\r/\t but NOT the $$ dollar-quote terminator. A node_id, entity name, or property value containing $$ (or $tag$) terminates the dollar-quoted literal and injects arbitrary SQL into the outer statement. Entity names and property values originate from LLM extraction over untrusted user documents, so this is reachable with adversarial content.

risks.title: Cypher property-KEY interpolation is unescaped
risks.detail: properties_to_cypher/value_to_cypher escape string VALUES but interpolate map KEYS raw: format!("{}: {}", k, value_str). LLM-extracted property keys containing spaces, braces, colons, or Cypher syntax corrupt or inject into the MERGE ... SET map. Keys are attacker-influenceable through document content.

risks.title: RLS context cannot work over a connection pool
risks.detail: set_tenant_context runs SELECT set_tenant_context(...) on the PgPool, setting a session GUC on whatever pooled connection it grabbed; the subsequent business query acquires a possibly DIFFERENT pooled connection with no context set. Worse, RlsContext::Drop tokio::spawns clear_tenant_context on yet another arbitrary connection. Session-level set_config does not propagate across pooled connections, so RLS is effectively inert here (confirms the known 'RLS is inert' project note). The vector/graph adapters that DO need session state work around this by manually pool.acquire()ing a dedicated connection (helpers.rs), but RlsContext does not.

risks.title: Per-workspace connection-pool explosion
risks.detail: WorkspaceVectorRegistry::create_workspace_storage builds a fresh PgVectorStorage per workspace, and PgVectorStorage::new constructs a brand-new PostgresPool (its own up-to max_connections pool) for each. With many active workspaces this multiplies into max_connections × N database connections and re-runs CREATE EXTENSION / CREATE TABLE / index DDL per workspace, risking connection exhaustion and DDL contention at scale. A single shared pool should back all workspace tables.

risks.title: SSL mode is dead configuration
risks.detail: PostgresConfig has an ssl_mode field (default Prefer) but connection_url() builds postgres://user:pass@host:port/db with no sslmode parameter and no PgConnectOptions usage. Setting ssl_mode=Require has zero effect — connections may proceed unencrypted against a remote DB. Also the password is embedded in the URL and the whole config derives Debug (password included), so credentials can leak via tracing of PostgresPool Debug.

risks.title: AGE session bootstrap repeated on every graph op
risks.detail: Each cypher_query/cypher_execute/cypher_query_count/ensure_indexes/batch_sql_query acquires a connection and issues LOAD 'age' + SET search_path + (sometimes) SET statement_timeout before the actual statement — 3-4 extra round trips per graph operation. For query modes that do many small graph lookups this dominates latency. LOAD 'age' on every call is especially wasteful.

code_review.issue: Fail-open tenant filter: absence of tenant_id/workspace_id metadata is treated as a match, leaking untagged vectors across tenants and contradicting the fail-closed graph-node policy.
code_review.suggested_fix: Make it fail-closed when a tenant/workspace scope is requested: if the requested key is Some but the metadata lacks it, return false. Better, push the predicate into SQL (metadata->>'workspace_id' = $n) so untagged rows never enter top-k.

code_review.issue: escape_cypher_string does not neutralize the $$ dollar-quote delimiter used to wrap the Cypher body, enabling breakout into the outer SQL.
code_review.suggested_fix: Use a randomized/named dollar tag ($eqcypher$...$eqcypher$) AND reject/escape any occurrence of the tag in the payload, or better, pass node_id/properties as bound parameters into the Cypher via AGE's parameterized cypher($graph$, $cypher$, $params$) form instead of string interpolation.

code_review.issue: Property map keys are interpolated into Cypher unescaped; LLM-derived keys can corrupt/inject the map literal.
code_review.suggested_fix: Validate keys against ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ and reject/normalize others, or back-tick-quote and escape keys per openCypher rules.

code_review.issue: Drop spawns an async clear on the pool (arbitrary connection) and set/clear run on different pooled connections than the queries they are meant to scope, so RLS context never reliably applies.
code_review.suggested_fix: Bind RLS to a single acquired connection or a transaction using SET LOCAL within the same Tx, and run all scoped queries on that same connection; drop the spawn-on-Drop pattern.

code_review.issue: upsert loops one INSERT per row with no transaction or multi-row batching — N round trips for ingestion and non-atomic partial writes on error.
code_review.suggested_fix: Batch via UNNEST($1::text[], $2::vector[], $3::jsonb[]) in a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT, wrapped in a transaction.

code_review.issue: format_embedding uses f32::to_string (NaN/inf -> invalid vector literal, lossy/verbose), and parse_embedding silently filter_maps unparseable components, masking corruption.
code_review.suggested_fix: Reject non-finite components up front; serialize with a compact fixed formatter, and bind via a typed pgvector encoder rather than text.

code_review.issue: Vector index creation result is discarded with .ok(); a failed HNSW/IVFFlat build silently degrades every query to a brute-force scan with no signal.
code_review.suggested_fix: Log at warn/error on failure (or surface it); distinguish 'empty table' from real DDL errors instead of swallowing all.

code_review.issue: Global mode calls graph_storage.node_degree(id) inside a loop (N+1), while local mode uses node_degrees_batch — inconsistent and slow for max_entities=60.
code_review.suggested_fix: Use node_degrees_batch(&entity_ids) once, as local mode does.

code_review.issue: Mix mode (advertised FEAT0105 'adaptive blend') is a stub that just delegates to hybrid — feature claim overstated.
code_review.suggested_fix: Either implement intent-adaptive weighting or document Mix as an alias of Hybrid in the public API/docs.

code_review.issue: get_popular_nodes_with_degree computes degree as out-edges only (COALESCE(ec.out_degree,0)) despite 'degree' naming, while node_degree counts in+out — inconsistent popularity ranking.
code_review.suggested_fix: Include in-edges in the CTE (or rename to out_degree) for consistent semantics.

code_review.issue: Louvain phase uses node_to_community.get(node_id).unwrap(); a missing entry (e.g. node id not seeded) panics the worker instead of erroring.
code_review.suggested_fix: Use a checked lookup with continue/Err; community detection should not be able to panic on malformed graphs.

code_review.issue: Workspace table name derives from the first 8 hex chars of the UUID (eq_default_ws_<8>), a collision surface across workspaces sharing a prefix.
code_review.suggested_fix: Use the full UUID (hyphens->underscores) or a hash to avoid truncation collisions.

improvements.what: Unify tenant/workspace isolation into one fail-closed policy enforced at the SQL layer for both vector and graph reads.
improvements.why: Today there are three divergent policies (vector fail-open, graph-node fail-closed, graph-edge fail-open). The vector fail-open path is a real cross-tenant leak, and post-fetch filtering also wrecks recall when a shared table mixes tenants.

improvements.what: Replace Cypher/SQL string interpolation with AGE parameterized cypher() calls (and bound arrays via UNNEST for SQL).
improvements.why: Eliminates the $$ breakout and property-key injection vectors and removes fragile hand-rolled escaping over LLM-derived, attacker-influenceable content.

improvements.what: Share a single connection pool across the default + all workspace vector/graph adapters; bind RLS to a transaction with SET LOCAL.
improvements.why: Stops per-workspace pool/connection explosion and makes RLS actually functional, while cutting repeated DDL/extension setup.

improvements.what: Batch vector upserts (UNNEST + single INSERT in a transaction) and use a typed pgvector codec instead of text formatting.
improvements.why: Per-row inserts and to_string serialization are the ingest hot path; this is straight throughput plus NaN/inf safety.

improvements.what: Cache AGE session setup (LOAD 'age' / search_path) per connection via a pool after_connect hook instead of re-running on every graph op.
improvements.why: Removes 3-4 round trips per graph call, which dominate query-mode latency.

improvements.what: Wire SSL through PgConnectOptions honoring ssl_mode, and stop embedding the password in connection_url / Debug.
improvements.why: ssl_mode is currently inert (silent plaintext risk to remote DBs) and credentials can leak via tracing of config Debug.

improvements.what: Expose ivfflat.probes / hnsw.ef_search at query time and surface index-build failures.
improvements.why: Recall is currently un-tunable and a silently-failed index downgrades all queries to seq scans with no signal.

tech_debt: Mix query mode is a stub delegating to Hybrid despite being documented as an adaptive blend (vector_queries.rs:566).
Heavy reliance on format!-built SQL/Cypher throughout storage adapters; no compile-time-checked sqlx::query! and no central query-builder, so escaping correctness is re-implemented per call site.
Per-workspace PgVectorStorage each owns a PostgresPool, re-running CREATE EXTENSION/CREATE TABLE/index DDL on every workspace init.

Two parallel isolation mechanisms (per-namespace/per-workspace physical tables vs app-layer metadata filtering) coexist without a single source of truth; mirrors the documented EdgeQuake-vs-webapp 'two data models' tension.
RlsContext + RlsQueryBuilder exist and interpolate UUIDs into SQL strings but are largely non-functional over a pool — dead/misleading abstraction.
Mixed entity/relationship/chunk vectors live in one table disambiguated by a metadata 'type' string and 2-3x oversampling at query time, instead of typed tables/columns.
~300+ unwrap/expect across the four crates: predominantly in tests, but live ones exist (community.rs:205,360) that can panic worker tasks on malformed graphs.
get_popular_nodes_with_degree degree semantics (out-only) diverge from node_degree (in+out).
edgequake-llm provider abstraction is an external pinned crate (0.2.7) not in this repo, so embedding/LLM/reranker behavior can't be audited or version-locked alongside the engine.
subResults.data_flow: "Ingest (core orchestrator/ingestion.rs): document → pipeline.chunk → optional parallel LLM entity/relationship extraction → link extractions to chunk ids → embeddings for chunks/entities/relationships → lineage. tenant_id/workspace_id from PipelineConfig are stamped onto vector metadata (ingestion.rs:297-301) and onto graph node/edge properties. Vectors land in a pgvector table (shared eq_<ns>_vectors or per-workspace eq_<ns>_ws_<id8>_vectors) with id/embedding/metadata JSONB; entities/relationships also become AGE graph nodes/edges via MERGE/SET Cypher. Query (SOTAQueryEngine): query text → LLM keyword extraction (cached) → compute query/high_level/low_level embeddings (batch of 3) → mode router. Naive: vector top-k (2x oversample) filtered by type=chunk + matches_tenant_filter. Local: low_level embedding → entity vectors → batch fetch nodes+degrees+edges from AGE → collect source_chunk_ids → fetch those chunks from vector store ranked by cosine. Global: high_level embedding → relationship vectors → entity backfill → chunk collection (per-node node_degree N+1). Hybrid: local+global+naive run via tokio::join, round-robin merged + de-duped. Context → token budgeting/truncation → prompt build → LLMProvider.complete (optionally per-request override). Tenant isolation is enforced post-fetch in the app layer (fail-open for vectors, fail-closed for graph nodes); RLS session GUCs are set but ineffective over the pool."
