subResults.subsystem: packages/edgequake — service layer (edgequake-api / -auth / -audit / -rate-limiter / -tasks) + e2e test suite
subResults.purpose: EdgeQuake is the in-repo Rust RAG engine that fronts SayKnowMind's document ingestion, vector/graph storage, query, chat, knowledge-graph, multi-tenant workspace, and background task pipeline over an Axum HTTP API (default :8080, Ollama-compatible + /api/v1). The reviewed crates provide the HTTP server/routing, an auth subsystem (JWT/Argon2/RBAC/tenant), an audit log, a token-bucket rate limiter, and a worker-pool task system for async document processing.
subResults.architecture: Cargo workspace of 9 crates (Cargo.toml). Binary is the root `edgequake` package (src/main.rs) which builds AppState via `AppState::new_postgres` (DATABASE_URL is mandatory; in-memory mode removed for the binary), runs three startup recovery passes (orphaned tasks, orphaned documents, requeue pending tasks — main.rs:67-372), starts a WorkerPool, then serves the Axum router. edgequake-api is layered: routes.rs (flat route table, ~150 endpoints under /api/v1) -> handlers/* (modularized: auth/, workspaces/, lineage_types/, processor/, etc.) -> state/{postgres,memory,mod} (AppState holds pipeline, llm/embedding providers, kv/vector/graph storage, task queue+storage, jwt/password/rbac services, rate_limiter) -> edgequake-storage adapters. Auth/audit/rate-limiter/tasks are separate crates consumed by edgequake-api. Middleware (server.rs build_router) only wires DefaultBodyLimit(100MB), request_logging, request_id, TraceLayer, permissive CORS, compression, Swagger. Tenant context is an Axum FromRequestParts extractor (middleware.rs:438) reading X-Tenant-ID / X-Workspace-ID / X-User-ID headers; app-layer isolation (handlers/isolation.rs) filters graph nodes/edges/documents by matching those header values. Task system: ChannelTaskQueue (mpsc) + WorkerPool with per-tenant semaphore fairness (tenant_limiter.rs) + exponential backoff + circuit breaker + on_permanent_failure callback. The TaskProcessor trait decouples the worker loop from document-processing logic (DocumentTaskProcessor in api).
whats_good: Task subsystem is genuinely well-engineered: WorkerPool (worker.rs) has bounded concurrency, exponential backoff with cap (calculate_backoff_delay), circuit-breaker awareness, graceful broadcast shutdown, and an on_permanent_failure hook that fixes the classic 'document stuck in processing forever' bug. Documented with WHY rationale.

TenantConcurrencyLimiter (tenant_limiter.rs) is a clean lock-free-ish per-tenant semaphore with lazy creation, double-checked locking on the write path, idle cleanup, and thorough unit tests for isolation/limit/release semantics.
Rate limiter (limiter.rs) is a correct token-bucket over DashMap with refill math, retry-after computation, and clear algorithm-choice rationale.

Password hashing (password.rs) uses Argon2id with sane params (64MiB/t=3/p=4), needs_rehash() upgrade detection, and password-strength validation. JWT service (jwt.rs) validates exp+nbf with clock-skew leeway and maps jsonwebtoken error kinds to typed errors.
Startup recovery logic in main.rs (orphaned tasks, orphaned documents, requeue pending) is thoughtful and directly addresses real restart-consistency failure modes.
handlers/isolation.rs centralizes the previously-duplicated tenant-match predicate into one auditable place with a strict 'both tenant_id AND workspace_id must match, no wildcard' contract.
Audit crate (logger.rs) is a clean async background-worker design (non-blocking log() via unbounded channel + log_sync escape hatch).

risks.title: Entire HTTP API ships with NO authentication or rate-limiting enforced
risks.detail: server.rs build_router() wires only body-limit, logging, request-id, trace, CORS, compression, Swagger. The api_key_auth middleware (middleware.rs:166) and tenant_rate_limit middleware (middleware.rs:287) are defined and exported (lib.rs:119) but never .layer()'d onto the router. No JWT-verification middleware exists at all. Every /api/v1 endpoint (documents, query, graph, users, tenants, workspaces, delete-all) is reachable unauthenticated. Auth handlers issue JWTs that nothing subsequently requires (only /auth/me verifies a token, and only for its own logic).

risks.title: Hardcoded default JWT secret used in production state (env ignored)
risks.detail: AppState::new_postgres constructs auth with AuthConfig::default() instead of AuthConfig::from_env(), so the JWT_SECRET environment variable is never read by the running binary. The default secret is the literal 'change-me-in-production-256-bit-secret-key'. Any party can forge a valid signed JWT for any user/role. BR0851 ('secret must be >=32 bytes') is documented but never enforced at runtime.

risks.title: Unauthenticated user creation with caller-chosen role (privilege escalation)
risks.detail: POST /api/v1/users (create_user) takes only State+Json with no auth/admin check and assigns the role straight from the request body (defaulting to user, but 'admin' is accepted). The OpenAPI annotation even documents '403 Admin access required' that the code never returns. The test suite codifies this as correct behavior (test_create_user_with_role asserts an admin user is created successfully with no auth).

risks.title: Tenant/workspace isolation is keyed on spoofable client headers with no identity binding
risks.detail: TenantContext is extracted purely from X-Tenant-ID/X-Workspace-ID/X-User-ID request headers (middleware.rs:377-398) and handlers/isolation.rs filters data by matching those exact values. Because no auth layer binds the caller to a tenant, any client can set arbitrary header values and read/write another tenant's documents, graph, conversations. This is cross-tenant access by header spoofing, not a theoretical RLS gap.

risks.title: PostgreSQL RLS context set on a pooled connection — silently ineffective
risks.detail: conversation.rs set_context() runs SELECT set_config('app.current_user_id', ..., false) against &*self.pool (a connection pool), then the actual read/write query acquires a DIFFERENT connection from the pool, on which the session variable was never set. The project's own RLS test file documents exactly this pitfall ('Connection pools give different connections - use acquire() for a dedicated connection'), yet the production path does not pin the connection. Where RLS is relied upon, it is effectively inert/broken. All 7 RLS tests are #[ignore], so CI never catches it.

risks.title: Audit subsystem is built but completely unwired (no audit trail)
risks.detail: edgequake-audit is a Cargo dependency of edgequake-api but `edgequake_audit::` is referenced nowhere outside its own crate; AuditLogger::new is never called. No security-relevant action (login, user/role creation, deletion, cross-tenant access) is recorded. The RBAC enum even defines an AuditLogRead permission for a log that is never written.

risks.title: RBAC service present but never enforced
risks.detail: RbacService is constructed into AppState (postgres.rs:296) and defines a full Permission matrix, but no handler calls check_permission/has_permission. There are zero authorization checks anywhere in handlers/. RBAC is dead code, so even if auth were wired, endpoints would not be permission-gated.
risks.evidence: crates/edgequake-api/src/state/postgres.rs:296; grep rbac_service/check_permission in handlers -> no matches; crates/edgequake-auth/src/rbac.rs

risks.title: Login has no brute-force lockout despite config and documented 423 response
risks.detail: AuthConfig carries max_login_attempts/lockout_duration and the login OpenAPI documents a 423 'Account locked' response, but session.rs login() never tracks failed attempts or locks accounts. With no rate-limit middleware either, password guessing is unthrottled.

risks.title: API keys are not bound to their creator (hardcoded demo-user)
risks.detail: create_api_key hardcodes user_id = 'demo-user' with a comment 'In production, this would come from the auth middleware'. Every API key created maps to the same fictitious owner, so ownership/listing/revocation cannot be scoped per user. Endpoint is also unauthenticated.

risks.title: Fully permissive CORS
risks.detail: CORS is configured with allow_origin(Any), allow_methods(Any), allow_headers(Any) and is enabled by default. Any web origin can call the (unauthenticated) API from a browser.

code_review.issue: build_router omits the auth and rate-limit layers entirely; the security middleware is implemented but orphaned.
code_review.suggested_fix: Add .layer(from_fn_with_state(auth_state, api_key_auth)) (or a real JWT-verification middleware) and .layer(from_fn_with_state(rate_state, tenant_rate_limit)) gated by config; fail closed when AUTH_ENABLED but no secret/keys configured.

code_review.issue: AuthConfig::default() used instead of AuthConfig::from_env(); JWT_SECRET env var is ignored and the hardcoded dev secret is used in the postgres (production) build.
code_review.suggested_fix: Use AuthConfig::from_env() and refuse to start if jwt_secret equals the placeholder or is <32 bytes (enforce BR0851).

code_review.issue: Role is taken from the unauthenticated request body; combined with no auth layer this is unauthenticated admin creation.
code_review.suggested_fix: Require an authenticated admin (RBAC UserCreate/SystemAdmin) and ignore/validate client-supplied role; only privileged callers may assign elevated roles.

code_review.issue: set_config(..., false) executed on the pool, not a dedicated acquired connection; the value does not apply to the subsequent query's connection, so RLS context is wrong/empty.
code_review.suggested_fix: Acquire one connection (pool.acquire()), run set_config and the data query on that same connection, or use a transaction with SET LOCAL; consider a connection-scoped wrapper for all tenant-scoped queries.

code_review.issue: Hardcoded 'demo-user' owner for created API keys.
code_review.suggested_fix: Derive user_id from the authenticated principal (JWT claims) once auth middleware exists; reject if unauthenticated.

code_review.issue: get_me maps any verify_token failure to 400 BadRequest; an expired/invalid token should be 401 Unauthorized for correct client refresh handling.
code_review.suggested_fix: Map verify_token errors to ApiError::Unauthorized (401).

code_review.issue: Retries are scheduled via tokio::spawn + sleep in-memory; a restart during the backoff window loses the retry (the task is persisted as Failed, and startup requeue only re-enqueues Pending).
code_review.suggested_fix: Persist a 'retry_at'/Pending-with-delay state in storage and re-enqueue due retries on startup, rather than relying on an in-process timer.

code_review.issue: Fixed 5-minute orphan threshold can mark legitimately long-running tasks (large PDFs, slow LLM) as failed after a restart.
code_review.suggested_fix: Make the threshold configurable and/or key it off a heartbeat/lease timestamp updated during processing rather than updated_at.

improvements.what: Wire the existing auth + rate-limit middleware into build_router and add a real JWT-verification extractor used by handlers; fail closed.
improvements.why: The components already exist and are tested; the only gap is assembly. Closes the single largest exposure (unauthenticated API) with modest effort.

improvements.what: Bind tenant/workspace context to authenticated identity instead of trusting X-Tenant-ID/X-User-ID headers; derive tenant from verified JWT claims and reject mismatched headers.
improvements.why: App-layer isolation is only as strong as the identity it filters on; today it filters on attacker-controlled headers.

improvements.what: Fix RLS connection pinning (acquire one connection / use SET LOCAL in a transaction) and switch the runtime DB role to a non-superuser app_user, then un-#[ignore] the RLS tests in CI.
improvements.why: Provides a real defense-in-depth isolation layer and makes the existing RLS test suite meaningful instead of aspirational.

improvements.what: Either wire edgequake-audit (instantiate AuditLogger, log auth/user/delete/cross-tenant events) and enforce RbacService in handlers, or delete both crates from the dependency graph.
improvements.why: Carrying built-but-unused security crates creates false assurance (and the OpenAPI/permission model implies they are active). Decide and make it true.

improvements.what: Stand up a real Postgres-backed e2e harness (pgvector + AGE) and convert the provider-switching / vector-dimension / isolation / lineage suites to run against it in CI.
improvements.why: ~41/58 test files run on AppState::test_state() with mock embeddings (vec![0.1;1536]); they validate HTTP/serialization/config-tracking but not pgvector dimension rejection, real RLS, or real RAG, so green CI overstates stability of exactly the features these tests are named for.

improvements.what: Add login throttling/lockout (honor max_login_attempts/lockout_duration) and return 423 as documented.
improvements.why: Unthrottled credential guessing against a hardcoded-secret system is a real attack path.

tech_debt: Three security crates (auth middleware, audit, RBAC) and the in-AppState RateLimiter are constructed/exported but never invoked — large surface of dead-but-shipping code that diverges from documented behavior (OpenAPI 401/403/423 responses that never occur).

Documentation/comment debt: FEAT/UC/BR annotations and WHY blocks assert guarantees (auth required, RLS isolation, lockout) that the wired system does not provide; comments are out of sync with runtime.

Test debt: 703 tests but heavily weighted to in-memory mock state; only 6 files touch Postgres and all 7 RLS tests are #[ignore]; 'vector dimension safety' tests assert stored config metadata, not DB-level vector rejection.
create_api_key hardcodes 'demo-user' with an explicit 'in production this would come from auth middleware' TODO — known placeholder shipped.
Retry durability gap: in-memory tokio timer retries are lost across restart; startup recovery only handles Pending, not scheduled retries.
JWT secret handling: from_env() exists but is bypassed by the production state constructor; no startup validation of secret strength.
Two parallel storage/state stacks (memory.rs vs postgres.rs) keep duplicated auth/rate-limiter wiring, doubling the places a security control must be wired correctly.
subResults.data_flow: "Client -> Axum router (no auth gate) -> request_id/logging/CORS layers -> handler. Handler builds TenantContext from X-Tenant-ID/X-Workspace-ID/X-User-ID headers (unverified). Read/graph handlers fetch from storage then filter in-process via handlers/isolation.rs against those header values. Ingestion: upload handler persists doc metadata to KV storage, creates a Task (tenant_id/workspace_id) in TaskStorage (Postgres) AND enqueues to in-memory ChannelTaskQueue; WorkerPool workers receive, acquire a per-tenant semaphore permit (fairness), mark processing, run DocumentTaskProcessor (chunk/embized/graph via pipeline using workspace-resolved providers), then mark success/failed with backoff retry or on_permanent_failure cleanup; status flows back to KV doc metadata and over WebSocket (/ws/pipeline/progress, /ws/progress/{track_id}). On restart, main.rs recovers orphaned tasks/docs and re-enqueues Pending tasks before workers start. Auth flow: login verifies Argon2 hash, issues HS256 JWT (signed with hardcoded default secret) + opaque refresh token stored in KV; only /auth/me re-verifies the JWT. RLS session vars are set in some Postgres adapters but on pooled (non-pinned) connections, so they do not reliably apply."

subResults.purpose: Two edge integration servers. mcp-server exposes EdgeQuake + the SayKnowMind web app as agent-callable MCP tools (query, graph_*, workspace_*, document_*, sayknowmind_* doc/sheet/mindmap/share) over stdio, SSE, and StreamableHTTP, with per-user API-key auth and an audit log. relay-server is a public Hono service (port 3200) that (a) runs a Hocuspocus/Yjs collaboration backend persisting CRDT state to Postgres doc_collab, and (b) acts as a "dumb pipe" store-and-forward relay for client-encrypted offline-sync blobs (relay_messages, 24h TTL), plus a Telegram webhook proxy.
subResults.architecture: mcp-server: entry (index.ts) wires Express with 3 transports; authMiddleware runs an AsyncLocalStorage RequestContext ({userId, rawToken, isAdmin}) so every tool handler sees its caller. createServer() builds an McpServer per HTTP session and monkey-patches server.tool() (patchToolWithAudit) so each registered handler is wrapped by withAudit before SDK registration. Tools split into two trust planes: EdgeQuake-direct tools (query/graph/workspace/document + workspace resources) talk to a MODULE-LEVEL singleton EdgeQuake SDK client (client.ts) bound to one global tenant/workspace, and are uniformly gated by rejectUserScopedEdgeQuakeTool()/...Resource() which blocks per-user keys (isolation unimplemented EdgeQuake-side); sayknowmind_* tools are thin HTTP proxies that forward the caller's Bearer token to the web app's /api/* routes, delegating org/visibility scoping to the web layer. audit.ts writes one mcp_audit_log row per authenticated-user call, fire-and-forget. relay-server: index.ts boots a pg Pool, a Hono app (server.ts), a TTL purge interval, and a raw ws WebSocketServer in noServer mode that hands /collab upgrades to Hocuspocus. Hono routes (push/pull/ack/status) sit behind a Bearer middleware verifying HMAC relay tokens (relay-token.ts); collab connections authorize at handshake via doc-scoped HMAC tokens (collab-token.ts) where room name === document id. Two distinct token audiences (sayknowmind-relay vs sayknowmind-collab) share one RELAY_SHARED_SECRET. Storage is plain pg CRUD over opaque base64 payloads.
whats_good: Isolation gate is applied consistently: every EdgeQuake-direct tool in query/graph/workspace/document and both workspace resources calls rejectUserScopedEdgeQuakeTool/Resource() as the first line, so per-user keys cannot reach the shared global EdgeQuake index (auth-context.ts, verified across all 13 tool registrations).

Token verification is careful: both relay-token.ts and collab-token.ts do a length check then a branchless XOR constant-time HMAC compare, validate iss/aud/exp, and recompute the signature with HMAC-SHA256 regardless of the JWT header — so the classic alg=none / alg-confusion attack is structurally impossible.
Audience separation (sayknowmind-relay vs sayknowmind-collab) prevents a sync token from being replayed as a collab token despite the shared secret.

Collab token is bound to a single document (payload.doc must equal documentName in onAuthenticate, hocuspocus.ts:29) and read-only is enforced via connection.readOnly = !canWrite — clean least-privilege per room.
Audit logging is non-blocking and correctly classifies the isolation-gate result as a distinct 'blocked' status (audit.ts:56-65), and never propagates DB failures into the tool response.

Relay routes validate input with zod, enforce a payload size cap, dedup by (user_id, payload_hash), and a TTL purge job cleans expired + acknowledged rows — the store-and-forward lifecycle is complete.
Short collab token TTL (5 min, web token.ts:45) — tokens only need to survive the WS handshake, limiting the blast radius of a leaked token.

sayknowmind_* doc/sheet/mindmap builders faithfully reconstruct the exact editor metadata (BlockNote blocks, Univer IWorkbookData, mind-elixir nodeData) so agent-created docs open identically to UI-created ones.

risks.title: Open-admin footgun: empty config = unauthenticated admin access to the whole EdgeQuake index
risks.detail: authMiddleware grants isAdmin:true with no token when BOTH MCP_API_KEY and DATABASE_URL are unset. On a public deploy (Railway target) that forgets either var, every caller gets admin EdgeQuake access to the shared tenant/workspace, and /health openly advertises the open mode. Open mode should require an explicit opt-in flag, not be the default-on fallback.

risks.title: MCP API keys stored and compared in plaintext
risks.detail: user_mcp_keys.api_key holds the raw sk-mcp-<hex> token; both the MCP server and the web app authenticate via SELECT ... WHERE api_key = $1 (plaintext equality, non-constant-time). A single DB read (or backup/log leak) exposes every live key. There is also no expiry and exactly one key per user (PRIMARY KEY user_id), so rotation invalidates the old key with no grace window and revocation is all-or-nothing.

risks.title: Telegram webhook proxy is unauthenticated when the secret is unset
risks.detail: The public relay forwards arbitrary request bodies to the internal web app endpoint /api/integrations/telegram/webhook. The webhook-secret check is skipped entirely if TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured, so by default anyone on the internet can POST spoofed Telegram updates through the relay into the internal network, and on failure it returns 200 to suppress retries. Security here is fail-open.

risks.title: Collaboration authorization is checked only at connect time
risks.detail: Hocuspocus runs onAuthenticate once at handshake. There is no re-validation or jti/replay protection, so (a) revoking a share or downgrading write access does not drop an already-connected writer, and (b) a leaked 5-minute collab token can be reused by any party to open that document (with the embedded canWrite) until it expires.

risks.title: 'E2E / relay never decrypts' guarantee overstated for the shared-server edition
risks.detail: Relay blobs are encrypted with server-side AES-256-GCM keyed by ENCRYPTION_KEY/BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (encryptForUser → getUserKey), with a known dev fallback secret 'dev-only-not-for-production'. For self-hosted single-user servers this is effectively E2E, but in the SaaS/shared-server edition the server holds the key, so it is server-side-at-rest encryption, not end-to-end. The relay's dumb-pipe security is only as strong as a client key the relay can't attest to.

risks.title: Single shared HMAC secret with no rotation or revocation list
risks.detail: RELAY_SHARED_SECRET signs both relay-sync tokens (7-day TTL) and collab tokens, shared between web and relay. There is no key id/rotation support and no revocation list; a single secret leak lets an attacker forge tokens for any user/document until natural expiry.

risks.title: API key accepted via query string
risks.detail: extractAuthToken falls back to ?api_key=, so credentials land in access logs, proxy logs, and browser history for the SSE/HTTP transports.

risks.title: No quota / rate limiting on relay push
risks.detail: Each message is capped at 10MB but nothing limits aggregate per-user storage or push rate; getStatus reports storage_used_bytes but no code enforces a ceiling, so a holder of one valid relay token can fill the table up to the 24h TTL window.

code_review.issue: The auth_token parameter is advertised on every sayknowmind_* tool but is effectively dead/misleading. verifyAuthToken() returns true whenever the request context already carries a Bearer token (always true in HTTP mode) or when AUTH_SECRET is unset; the actual outbound credential is the context rawToken or AUTH_SECRET (apiHeaders), never params.auth_token. Agents are told to pass a token that does nothing.
code_review.suggested_fix: Remove auth_token from the tool schemas entirely and document that the transport Bearer is the credential, or actually thread params.auth_token through apiHeaders() when present. Don't expose a no-op security parameter.

code_review.issue: getClient() is a process-global singleton bound to one tenant/workspace, but createServer() is invoked per HTTP session. All sessions therefore share one EdgeQuake identity; combined with silent auto-discovery picking tenants[0]/workspaces[0] (warn-only), a multi-tenant deployment can serve the wrong tenant's data with only a console warning.
code_review.suggested_fix: Either make the client per-resolved-config (not module-global) or hard-fail when multiple tenants/workspaces are discovered and none is pinned via env, instead of warning and continuing.

code_review.issue: The workspace-entities resource parses {workspace_id} from the URI but never uses it — it calls client.graph.entities.list() against the global workspace, so reading edgequake://workspace/A/entities returns workspace B's entities if the client is bound to B (resources/workspace.ts:84).
code_review.suggested_fix: Pass the parsed workspaceId into the entities.list() call, or drop the templated id from the URI to avoid implying per-workspace scoping that isn't honored.

code_review.issue: Fail-open secret check plus a catch-all that returns {ok:true} on forwarding failure. Beyond the auth gap, swallowing forward errors as success means dropped Telegram updates are invisible.
code_review.suggested_fix: Refuse to start the route (or 503) when TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset; log and surface forwarding failures with a metric rather than masking them as ok:true.

code_review.issue: payload_hash is fully client-supplied and never verified against encrypted_payload; it drives dedup (isDuplicate) and is stored verbatim. A client can desync its own dedup, and the hash provides no integrity guarantee despite looking like one.
code_review.suggested_fix: Compute the hash server-side from encrypted_payload (sha256) and reject or ignore the client-supplied value, so dedup and any future integrity checks are trustworthy.

code_review.issue: cors() is applied with defaults to all routes (including /relay/* and /telegram/webhook), reflecting any origin. Auth is Bearer not cookie so impact is limited, but it's needlessly permissive for a service that has no browser-CORS use case on the authed routes.
code_review.suggested_fix: Scope CORS to the known web-app origin(s) via an allowlist, or drop CORS on /relay/* and /telegram/* which are server-to-server.

code_review.issue: Version string drift: McpServer reports version 0.1.0 (server.ts:46) while /health reports 0.2.0 (index.ts:118). Clients reading either get inconsistent identity.
code_review.suggested_fix: Source both from package.json version to keep them in lockstep.

improvements.what: Hash MCP API keys at rest (e.g. SHA-256 of the token) and store a key prefix + hash; look up by hash. Add an expires_at column and support multiple active keys per user for rotation.
improvements.why: Eliminates the plaintext-key-leak blast radius and enables real rotation/revocation; today one DB read compromises every key and rotation has no grace window.

improvements.what: Replace the implicit open-admin fallback with an explicit MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=true flag; otherwise refuse to start (or 401 everything) when no auth source is configured.
improvements.why: Removes the single most dangerous misconfiguration — a public deploy with no env vars silently granting admin EdgeQuake access.

improvements.what: Make the Telegram webhook secret mandatory (fail closed) and verify the forwarded body's signature per request.
improvements.why: Closes the unauthenticated public→internal forwarding path.

improvements.what: Add periodic re-authorization (or a server-pushed disconnect on unshare) to the Hocuspocus connection and an org-membership check inside onAuthenticate against the DB, not just the token claim.
improvements.why: Connect-time-only auth means revocations don't take effect on live collaborators; defense-in-depth beyond a 5-min token.

improvements.what: Introduce a keyId/rotation scheme for RELAY_SHARED_SECRET (support two active secrets during rotation) and a per-token jti with a short-lived revocation set.
improvements.why: Lets the shared HMAC secret be rotated without downtime and lets individual tokens be revoked before expiry.

improvements.what: Add a test suite for relay-server (token verify edge cases, push/pull/ack lifecycle, TTL purge, collab onAuthenticate doc-binding, telegram secret enforcement).
improvements.why: relay-server currently ships with zero tests despite handling auth, encryption-adjacent storage, and CRDT persistence; mcp-server already has unit + e2e tests to mirror.

improvements.what: Compute payload_hash server-side and add per-user storage/rate quotas on push.
improvements.why: Trustworthy dedup/integrity and protection against a single token filling the relay table.

tech_debt: relay-server has no automated tests at all (no *.test.ts under src), unlike mcp-server which has unit + e2e vitest suites.
auth_token parameter is a no-op surface duplicated across ~18 sayknowmind_* tool schemas — dead, misleading API.

Auth model differs per transport: stdio mode has no authMiddleware, so sayknowmind_* proxy calls go out with AUTH_SECRET (which the web app's sk-mcp validator does not accept) or no auth header — proxied tools effectively don't authenticate in stdio unless AUTH_SECRET maps to a web session.

EdgeQuake per-user/per-tenant isolation is explicitly unimplemented; the whole per-user EdgeQuake-direct tool surface is hard-blocked as a stopgap (auth-context.ts), leaving query/graph/workspace tools usable only by trusted admin/stdio callers.
Global singleton EdgeQuake client with silent tenants[0]/workspaces[0] auto-discovery — wrong-tenant-by-warning.
Version strings drift between McpServer (0.1.0), /health (0.2.0), and package.json.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_mcp_keys is run at request time inside the route handler (ensureTable) rather than only via db/migrations/041 — schema defined in two places.
'E2E encrypted, relay never decrypts' is documented as an absolute guarantee but is server-side encryption in the shared-server edition, with a known dev fallback key.
CORS is wide-open (default cors()) on all relay routes including server-to-server ones.
payload_hash trusted from client; no integrity binding to the ciphertext.
subResults.data_flow: "MCP read: agent -> transport (stdio/SSE/HTTP) -> authMiddleware resolves token to RequestContext (admin | per-user userId | open) -> tool handler (audit-wrapped). EdgeQuake-direct tools: isolation gate (block per-user) -> global singleton EdgeQuake client -> EdgeQuake API. sayknowmind_* tools: forward Bearer rawToken -> web app /api/* -> web app enforces org/user visibility in SQL -> JSON back. Per-user calls also append a row to mcp_audit_log. Relay sync: user's web/desktop server encrypts a change blob (AES-256-GCM via encryptForUser) -> POST /relay/push with HMAC relay token -> relay_messages (24h TTL, dedup by hash). Another device GET /relay/pull (same user via token.sub) -> decrypts locally -> POST /relay/ack -> purge job deletes acked/expired rows. Collab: browser gets a 5-min doc-scoped collab token from web -> HocuspocusProvider connects ws /collab -> onAuthenticate verifies HMAC + doc==room, sets readOnly -> onLoadDocument applies Yjs state from doc_collab -> edits merge in memory -> onStoreDocument persists encodeStateAsUpdate back to doc_collab. Telegram: Telegram -> public relay /telegram/webhook (optional secret) -> web app internal webhook."

subResults.purpose: Provide programmatic clients for the platform. In reality two unrelated things live here: (1) packages/sdk is a full-featured, vendored TypeScript SDK for the upstream EdgeQuake Rust RAG engine (api on :8080), and (2) sdk-sayknowmind/sdk-go/sdk-python are thin hand-written clients for SayKnowMind's own Next.js web API (:3000, /api/search, /api/ingest/*, /api/chat, /api/categories).
subResults.architecture: Two distinct SDK families that are commonly mistaken for duplicates but target different servers. (A) packages/sdk = "edgequake-sdk" v0.4.0: a Stripe/OpenAI-style client (new EdgeQuake({apiKey}).documents.list()). 84 TS files, 21 resource namespaces wired in client.ts:155-175 (auth, users, apiKeys, documents, query, chat, conversations, folders, shared, graph, tenants, workspaces, tasks, pipeline, costs, lineage, chunks, provenance, settings, models, ollama), a real transport layer (fetch + retry/backoff + middleware), SSE + WebSocket streaming, Paginator, typed error hierarchy, env-var config resolution (config.ts:80-100, EDGEQUAKE_* vars, default base :8080), dual ESM/CJS via tsup, ~11 unit + ~9 e2e test files, docs/ and examples/. Author "EdgeQuake Team", repo points to github.com/raphaelmansuy/edgequake — it is upstream code vendored in, and is consumed by packages/mcp-server (src/client.ts:7). (B) sdk-sayknowmind = "@sayknowmind/sdk" v0.1.0: single client.ts (164 lines) + types.ts, plain fetch, Bearer-token auth, AbortSignal.timeout, ad-hoc chatStream SSE parser. sdk-go (sayknowmind.go, 249 lines) and sdk-python (client.py + types.py) are line-by-line ports of the same surface: search / ingestUrl / ingestFile / ingestText / chat / chatStream / getCategories / createCategory.
whats_good: packages/sdk is genuinely well-engineered: resource-namespace pattern, injectable transport for testing (config._transport, client.ts:151-152), exponential backoff with jitter, SSE+WS streaming, async-iterable pagination, full typed error hierarchy, comprehensive unit+e2e suites, and a prepublishOnly gate (lint+test+build) — production-grade for what it targets.
The sayknowmind TS/Go/Python trio keeps an identical method surface and JSON wire shape across all three languages, so a fix in one maps cleanly to the others.

Idiomatic per-language ergonomics: Go uses functional options (WithToken/WithTimeout) and typed APIError; Python is a context manager (__enter__/__exit__) with dataclasses; TS re-exports clean types from a barrel.
Search response typing matches the real /api/search contract ({results, totalCount, took}) — the read path is correct.
edgequake-sdk config resolves from EDGEQUAKE_* env vars and works across Node/Deno/Bun/browser (config.ts:81-99), good for deployment portability.

risks.title: chat() is broken against the real server — endpoint is SSE-only
risks.detail: All three SayKnowMind SDKs expose a non-streaming chat() that POSTs /api/chat and calls response.json() expecting ChatResponse {conversationId, messageId, answer, citations, relatedDocuments}. But /api/chat ALWAYS returns text/event-stream (route comment 'Always stream', returns a ReadableStream). response.json()/json.Unmarshal on an SSE body throws. The entire ChatResponse shape is invented — the server never returns messageId or a JSON answer.

risks.title: chatStream event schema does not match the server's SSE events
risks.detail: Server StreamWriter emits {type:'answer', token}, {type:'sources', sources}, {type:'status'|'log'|'error'|'done', ...}. The SDK's ChatStreamEvent type declares {type:'text'|'citation'|'step'|'done'|'error', data:string} and looks for a 'data: [DONE]' sentinel that the server never sends. Consumers get objects that don't match the declared type and the done-handling never fires correctly.

risks.title: createCategory() response shape mismatch — silent wrong data or hard crash
risks.detail: POST /api/categories returns {categoryId, name, path: string[]}. Python create_category reads data['id'] -> raises KeyError (uncaught, crashes). Go unmarshals into Category whose Path is a string -> json.Unmarshal error 'cannot unmarshal array into Go struct field Category.path of type string'; ID stays empty. TS casts the JSON to Category so .id is undefined and .path is an array typed as string.

risks.title: getCategories() field casing mismatch — parentId always null
risks.detail: GET /api/categories returns categories straight from SELECT c.* (snake_case parent_id). SDKs map parentId from camelCase keys, so parentId/parent_id is always undefined/None and category hierarchy is lost client-side.

risks.title: Search filters silently ignored
risks.detail: Server reads filters from a nested body.filters object {categoryIds, dateRange, tags}. The TS SDK spreads SearchParams flat ({query, ...params}) and Python spreads **kwargs flat, so categoryIds/tags/dateRange land at the top level and are dropped. Go's Search has no filter support at all. Category/tag/date filtering never works.

risks.title: Auth model mismatch (Bearer token vs session cookie)
risks.detail: All sayknowmind SDKs authenticate with Authorization: Bearer <token>. The web API authenticates via getOrgContext()/getUserIdFromRequest() which resolve a session (cookie-based). No API-token acceptance path was found for these routes, so Bearer-token SDK auth likely yields 401 against a deployed web app. This is the kind of thing that makes the SDK unusable out of the box.

risks.title: mcp-server depends on a mismatched/external edgequake-sdk version
risks.detail: packages/mcp-server declares 'edgequake-sdk': '^0.1.0' but the in-repo package is 0.4.0, and packages/sdk is not listed in pnpm-workspace.yaml (no sdk entries). If resolved from the npm registry instead of the workspace, mcp-server pulls a different or non-existent package; ^0.1.0 also can't satisfy 0.4.0.

risks.title: edgequake-sdk is vendored upstream code with misleading provenance
risks.detail: packages/sdk is named 'edgequake-sdk', authored by 'EdgeQuake Team', Apache-2.0, repo github.com/raphaelmansuy/edgequake — it is not SayKnowMind-authored. README claims '131+ endpoints across 27 resource categories' but only 21 resource namespaces are wired. The barrel doc-comment calls it '@edgequake/sdk' while package.json names it 'edgequake-sdk' (scoped vs unscoped inconsistency).

code_review.issue: Endpoint is stream-only; the JSON chat() method in every sayknowmind SDK cannot consume it (response.json() on an SSE body throws). ChatResponse.messageId is never produced by the server.

subResults.architecture:
apps/dashboard is NOT an analytics dashboard for apps/web. It is "EdgeQuake WebUI" (per README.md, .env.local.example, login page title) — a standalone ~79k-LOC Next.js 16 / React 19 frontend that was developed separately, vendored into the monorepo, and rebranded "SayknowMind" (commit 67cd2ef). It is a full operator/admin console for the EdgeQuake Rust RAG engine, talking directly to that API at http://localhost:8080/api/v1 (src/lib/api/client.ts:17-33).

Isolation: it shares ZERO code with apps/web or any workspace package — grep for @sayknowmind/ or packages/ imports returns nothing. It is not in pnpm-workspace; it carries its own three lockfiles (bun.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml) and its own Dockerfile/CI image (.github/workflows/ci.yml:69-104, deploy.yml:58). Two completely independent dependency trees from web.

Structure: App Router with two route groups. (dashboard)/* = graph, documents, query, pipeline, costs, workspace, users, api-explorer, settings. w/[slug]/* = thin deeplink resolvers that set workspace context then router.push to the canonical page (e.g. src/app/w/[slug]/graph/page.tsx is 51 lines of redirect logic, not a duplicate impl). State via Zustand stores (use-auth-store, use-tenant-store, use-graph-store 1048 LOC, use-ingestion-store 750 LOC) + TanStack Query. The whole API surface lives in src/lib/api/edgequake.ts (1844 LOC, ~80 exported functions): tenants/workspaces CRUD, document upload incl. PDF vision extraction, rebuildEmbeddings/rebuildKnowledgeGraph, query+SSE streaming, graph entities/relationships/merge, pipeline + task-queue monitoring, document lineage/provenance, and cost/budget tracking. A second, much newer and tiny client src/lib/api/sayknowmind.ts (Apr 30) bridges to apps/web's /api/admin/* endpoints with credentials:'include' — this is where the "admin dashboard for SayKnowMind" repurposing is being grafted on.

Auth: own JWT scheme — login() against EdgeQuake, tokens in localStorage (client.ts:81-82), Zustand persist. Tenant/workspace/user identity is client-asserted via X-Tenant-ID / X-Workspace-ID / X-User-ID headers built from localStorage, with an auto-generated anonymous UUID fallback (client.ts:121-186). No middleware.ts, no route guard.
whats_good: Genuinely feature-complete RAG operator console: 1844-line typed EdgeQuake client covering ingestion, PDF vision extraction, embedding/graph rebuilds, streaming query, entity/relationship editing+merge, pipeline & task-queue monitoring, document lineage/provenance, and cost/budget tracking (src/lib/api/edgequake.ts). This is real depth, not a skeleton.

Strong test footprint for a frontend: 16 vitest unit/store/component tests (e.g. use-ingestion-store.test.ts 1056 LOC, ingestion-progress-panel.test.ts 1033 LOC) plus 69 Playwright e2e specs with multiple config profiles (playwright.config.ts, playwright.config.noserver.ts).

Clean separation of concerns: typed API layer (lib/api), Zustand stores, TanStack Query for server cache, shadcn/ui primitives, i18n (i18next + react-i18next + locales/). SSE streaming implemented as async generators (queryStream, graphStream).

TenantGuard centralizes tenant/workspace bootstrapping and explicitly handles the mutation-success vs query-cache-invalidation race (src/components/layout/tenant-guard.tsx), with documented reasoning.
Deeplink routes under w/[slug] are correctly implemented as thin redirect resolvers (useWorkspaceSlugResolver) rather than copy-pasted page bodies — avoids the obvious internal duplication trap.
Production Docker setup with non-root user, healthcheck, multi-stage build, and a safe-build.sh wrapper that decouples tsc from next build.

risks.title: Re-exposes the abandoned EdgeQuake multi-tenant model at the UI layer
risks.detail: The project memory explicitly says don't revive EdgeQuake tenancy; web tenant isolation is app-layer only. But the dashboard's entire model IS EdgeQuake tenancy: TenantGuard lets users createTenant/createWorkspace and every request carries client-set X-Tenant-ID/X-Workspace-ID headers. Shipping this as a deployed Docker image (deploy.yml:58) means there are now two frontends with contradictory tenancy assumptions against the same data. This is the 'two data models' tension made into two shipping products.

risks.title: No authentication gate on any route
risks.detail: There is no middleware.ts and no isAuthenticated redirect in the (dashboard) layout — TenantGuard only ensures a tenant is selected, not that the user is logged in. The login page has a handleSkipLogin() that routes straight to /graph with no demo-mode flag check (the documented NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_DEMO_MODE is never read in code). BR0501 'Protected routes require authentication' is documented in use-auth-store.ts but unenforced. Access control is entirely delegated to the backend.

risks.title: Client-asserted identity headers; trust fully delegated to EdgeQuake
risks.detail: X-Tenant-ID, X-Workspace-ID and X-User-ID are read from localStorage (or an auto-generated anonymous UUID) and sent on every request. Combined with skip-login, an unauthenticated user can self-assert any tenant/user id. If the EdgeQuake API trusts these headers without revalidating against the JWT, this is cross-tenant data access. The frontend provides no defense in depth.

risks.title: JWT access+refresh tokens stored in localStorage
risks.detail: Tokens persisted to localStorage (and mirrored in a zustand persist store), readable by any injected/XSS script — and this app renders user/document markdown (react-markdown, marked, mermaid, dompurify present but not provably applied everywhere). Comment in use-auth-store.ts even claims 'Tokens stored securely in localStorage' (BR0505), which is misleading.

risks.title: Cross-origin admin bridge likely broken and dangerous
risks.detail: sayknowmind.ts calls the web app's /api/admin/* (including deleteUser DELETE) from a different origin (dashboard :3001 vs web :3000) with credentials:'include'. Cross-origin cookies require SameSite=None + matching CORS, so this is probably non-functional locally; if it is made to work via shared domain, the dashboard's lack of auth gating means the admin user-delete surface is reachable by anyone who loads the dashboard.

risks.title: Three committed, divergent lockfiles
risks.detail: bun.lock, package-lock.json AND pnpm-lock.yaml are all committed. README tells contributors to use bun/npm, CI caches and installs with pnpm (ci.yml:80), Dockerfile uses pnpm --frozen-lockfile. Guaranteed silent dependency drift between local dev, CI, and prod images.

code_review.issue: handleSkipLogin() unconditionally routes to /graph, bypassing auth. The documented demo-mode flag (NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_DEMO_MODE) is never checked anywhere in src — so this is always-on, including in production builds.
code_review.suggested_fix: Gate the skip button behind process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_DEMO_MODE, or remove it. Add a real auth guard (middleware or layout-level redirect to /login when !isAuthenticated).

code_review.issue: Identity (tenant/workspace/user) is client-controlled via headers sourced from localStorage with an anonymous UUID fallback. No binding between the JWT subject and the asserted X-User-ID/X-Tenant-ID.
code_review.suggested_fix: Stop sending self-asserted identity headers; let the backend derive tenant/user from the verified JWT. If multi-tenant switching is needed, validate the requested tenant server-side against the token's allowed tenants.

code_review.issue: Auth tokens persisted in localStorage (lines 81-82); generateUUID uses Math.random() (line ~115) for an identity value.
code_review.suggested_fix: Prefer httpOnly cookies for tokens; if localStorage is unavoidable, document the XSS tradeoff honestly (the current 'stored securely' comment is false). Use crypto.randomUUID().

code_review.issue: Hardcoded fallback WEB_APP_URL 'http://localhost:3000' and credentials:'include' cross-origin admin calls including destructive deleteUser. No error typing, no auth context.
code_review.suggested_fix: Require NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL explicitly, proxy admin calls through the dashboard's own backend/route handler to keep them same-origin and auth-checked, and confirm the web admin endpoints enforce role server-side.

code_review.suggested_fix: Use the standalone output: COPY .next/standalone and .next/static, run `node server.js`, drop the prod node_modules install in the runtime stage.

subResults.data_flow: Browser -> dashboard React (Zustand stores + TanStack Query) -> src/lib/api/client.ts -> EdgeQuake Rust API at NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL/api/v1 (default :8080). Every request attaches Bearer token from localStorage plus client-controlled X-Tenant-ID / X-Workspace-ID / X-User-ID headers (auto-UUID fallback for anonymous). Streaming (query, graph) flows back as SSE consumed via async generators. A separate, secondary path: src/lib/api/sayknowmind.ts -> apps/web /api/admin/* with credentials:'include' (cross-origin), feeding the users/stats admin pages. The two paths hit two different backends with two different identity models — EdgeQuake tenancy headers vs the web app's cookie session — which is the core divergence risk. Why dashboard is v0.5.4 while web is v0.1.0: it is an independently-versioned, externally-developed product (originally edgequake_webui) vendored in and rebranded, carrying its own mature version lineage; it is not a younger sibling of web.

subResults.purpose: Desktop: native shell wrapping the SayKnowMind web app, in two Cargo-feature variants — `full` (bundles a Node.js sidecar + Next.js standalone server on 127.0.0.1:3457 for offline use) and `lite` (thin WKWebView/WebView2 pointed at the cloud https://sayknowmind.ypai.click). Adds OS integration (tray, global shortcuts, OAuth-aware navigation filter) and a bridge of Tauri commands that let the webview drive a local OCP (Open Claude Proxy) / Codex CLI for on-device LLM inference using the user's own ChatGPT/Claude subscription. Mobile: a Capacitor shell intended to wrap the same web app with share-intent ingestion, offline cache, and push — currently a skeleton.
subResults.architecture: Single Rust binary (src-tauri/src/main.rs, ~1817 lines) compiled in two mutually exclusive Cargo features (Cargo.toml:7-10 `default=["full"]`, `full`, `lite`). No bundled frontend dist: the window is always `WebviewUrl::External` (main.rs:1758-1762). Full mode: setup hook spawns the Next.js standalone server (start_server, main.rs:1337) by locating a sidecar `node` beside the exe (find_node_binary:1265) and `web-standalone/server.js` in Resources (find_web_standalone:1283), injects env (PGLITE fallback when no DATABASE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET persisted to data dir, TRUSTED_ORIGINS), waits up to 10s for the port (wait_for_server:1421), then loads http://127.0.0.1:3457; child is killed on window Destroyed (1793-1801). Lite mode: ServerState is a unit struct, no server, window loads REMOTE_URL. Shared layer: tray menu (setup_tray:1437, Korean labels, drives the webview via w.eval/navigate), two global shortcuts (toggle visibility + 'home' escape hatch, 1511), and an on_navigation filter (is_allowed_navigation:1573) that keeps localhost/remote/Google-OAuth hosts in-webview and hands everything else to the system browser (open_external:1608). An initialization_script (1700-1756) re-routes window.open/target=_blank/middle-clicks to the system browser. A large block of `#[tauri::command]`s (registered 1649-1671) exposes OCP/Codex orchestration: system_env_check, find_best_node (fnm/nvm/volta/brew discovery, 212), ocp_install (clones a GitHub repo + npm install + node setup.mjs + launchctl, 1008), exec_codex_login (sidecar→PATH→npx, 782), chat_via_ocp/complete_via_ocp (reqwest to 127.0.0.1:3456, 374/639), chat_via_codex/complete_via_codex (spawn codex exec with read-only/no-network sandbox, 466), provision/revoke_ocp_key, open_external_url. PATH for child processes is reconstructed by running the user's login shell (resolve_shell_path:898) because macOS GUI apps inherit a minimal launchd PATH. Build: beforeBuildCommand → scripts/build-desktop.sh (full bundles web standalone + flattens pnpm hoist + aliases Turbopack-hashed externals; lite skips), scripts/setup-sidecar.sh (Node 22.15), scripts/fetch-binaries.sh (pinned codex rust-v0.130.0). Mobile: Capacitor 7 config (webDir ../web/.next, server.url localhost:3000 cleartext) + a single src/index.ts implementing share-intent parse, localStorage offline cache, pending-sync queue, and push setup — no android/ or ios/ native projects exist in the repo.
whats_good: full-vs-lite split is clean and well-commented: feature-gated ServerState, conditional URL resolution, and a shared command surface that works in both modes (main.rs:35-39, 1678-1693)

resolve_shell_path() (main.rs:898) correctly solves the real and commonly-missed macOS problem that GUI apps inherit a minimal launchd PATH — runs the login shell once, merges a hardcoded safety net, dedupes, and caches via OnceLock

find_best_node() (main.rs:212) is genuinely thorough: probes PATH node, then scans fnm/nvm/volta version dirs and brew node@22..25 formulas, picks the highest ≥22.5 — a frequent silent-failure source handled deliberately

Codex local exec is hardened: --sandbox read-only, approval_policy=never, web_search=disabled, network_access=false, cwd=tmpdir (main.rs:476-487), and JSONL event parsing mirrors the official codex-sdk run() semantics

OAuth navigation handling is thoughtful — keeps the whole google.com/googleusercontent/gstatic/googleapis tree in the session-owning webview to avoid losing cookies on intermediate redirects, with a Cmd+Shift+H escape hatch when a consent page gets stuck (main.rs:1539-1564, 1591-1606)

the recent Windows build fix is correct: the POSIX 0o600 chmod on the admin-key is now behind #[cfg(unix)] (main.rs:1122-1126), and the codex 192MB binary is fetched at build time, not committed (verified untracked)
async LLM commands properly offload blocking reqwest to spawn_blocking (main.rs:379, 645), keeping the IPC runtime responsive
version numbers are consistent across Cargo.toml / tauri.conf.json / package.json (all 0.1.5)

risks.title: Privileged custom commands are reachable from the remote cloud webview in lite builds
risks.detail: Tauri capabilities only gate core/plugin commands; app-defined #[tauri::command]s are NOT ACL-gated (verified: no allow-* permissions exist for them). The remote-cloud capability (capabilities/remote.json) deliberately grants only shell:allow-open to JS from sayknowmind.ypai.click and even warns to 'keep the list tight' — but that scoping does nothing for the custom commands. So in the lite build (the only variant CI ships), JavaScript served by the cloud origin — or any XSS in it — can invoke ocp_install, exec_codex_login, chat_via_codex, provision_ocp_key, open_external_url, etc. directly. Combined with a permissive CSP (script-src 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval', third-party frame-src), an XSS on the cloud app escalates to local code execution on the user's machine.

risks.title: ocp_install clones and executes code from a third-party personal GitHub repo
risks.detail: ocp_install_sync hardcodes `git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/dtzp555-max/ocp.git` into ~/.sayknowmind/ocp, then runs npm install, node setup.mjs (which writes a launchd plist), and launchctl start dev.ocp.proxy. This executes arbitrary, unpinned code from a single personal account on the user's machine — a supply-chain takeover point. Because of the command-exposure issue above, in lite builds this can be triggered by remote JS, not just a deliberate button press. No commit pin, no integrity check.

risks.title: Auto-updater configured with an empty public key
risks.detail: plugins.updater has live endpoints (releases.sayknow.ai) and dialog:true but pubkey:"" while CI signs artifacts with TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY. An empty pubkey means in-app update signature verification cannot work — the updater will either fail to verify (broken updates) or, if mis-handled, weaken the trust path for a binary-replacement channel. The updater domain (releases.sayknow.ai) also differs from both the app origin (sayknowmind.ypai.click) and brand, increasing config-drift risk.

risks.title: Mobile app is non-functional and its release CI will fail
risks.detail: apps/mobile has no android/ or ios/ native projects committed (only package.json, capacitor.config.json, src/index.ts). The mobile-release workflow runs `npx cap sync android` then `cd apps/mobile/android && ./gradlew assembleRelease` — but `cap sync` requires the platform folder to already exist (created by `cap add`), so the build fails before gradle. webDir points at ../web/.next (a non-static Next.js build dir, not servable static assets) and server.url is hardcoded to http://localhost:3000 with cleartext, so even if it built it could not load on a device. WEB_APP_URL and all ingest endpoints in src/index.ts are hardcoded to localhost:3000.
risks.evidence: apps/mobile/capacitor.config.json:4-7; apps/mobile/src/index.ts:16; .github/workflows/mobile-release.yml:43-49; ls apps/mobile (no android/ios dirs)

risks.title: Several synchronous commands do blocking network/IO on the main thread
risks.detail: is_offline (DNS resolve + TCP connect, 3s timeout), system_env_check (multiple subprocess spawns + 800ms HTTP), ocp_status (1.5s HTTP), codex_status, provision_ocp_key, and revoke_ocp_key (5s HTTP) are non-async #[tauri::command]s. Synchronous Tauri commands run on the main thread, so each call can freeze the UI for up to its timeout. The async LLM commands got spawn_blocking but these status/preflight calls did not — inconsistent and user-visible jank on the settings/preflight screens.

subResults.subsystem: db/init + db/migrations (PostgreSQL schema, pgvector/AGE, multi-tenancy, RLS, migrations)
subResults.purpose: Defines the entire relational data model for SayKnowMind: documents/chunks/entities/relationships (knowledge graph + RAG), categories/tags, conversations/messages, doc_collab (Yjs CRDT), document_versions, orgs/members/invitations (team feature), per-resource and per-team ACL shares, better-auth tables, relay offline-sync ledger, and the legacy EdgeQuake multi-tenant schema. db/init/*.sql are Docker first-boot entrypoint scripts; db/migrations/*.sql are applied incrementally by a shell runner tracked in schema_migrations.
subResults.architecture: Two physically-overlapping schemas share one database. (1) The EdgeQuake schema (db/init/01-edgequake-init.sql, db/migrations/001-025) is a polished multi-tenant design: documents/chunks/entities/relationships/tasks keyed by tenant_id+workspace_id, full RLS with session-GUC context functions (current_tenant_id() etc.), partitioned audit_logs, HNSW vector indexes. (2) The webapp schema (db/init/04-sayknowmind-init.sql, 05-10, db/migrations/026-061) is user-scoped: documents.user_id TEXT -> better-auth "user", categories/tags/conversations/messages/ingestion_jobs/shared_content, then a team layer (053-058) built on better-auth organization plugin (organization/member/invitation + organization_id on resources + resource_shares/resource_team_shares ACL). Both schemas issue CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for the SAME table names (documents, entities, conversations, messages, graph_nodes). Docker runs 01-edgequake FIRST (docker-compose.yml:21-25), so the EdgeQuake shape wins and 04-sayknowmind's versions are silently skipped; bridge migrations 043/049 then ALTER the EdgeQuake tables to bolt on the webapp columns (user_id, source_type, document_id, type, confidence). Isolation is enforced purely in the app layer (lib/visibility.ts, lib/org-context.ts); the DB connects as the postgres superuser (docker-compose.yml:61) and no code calls set_config/set_tenant_context, so every RLS policy is inert.
whats_good: Indexing is genuinely strong: HNSW (m=16, ef_construction=64) on chunks/entities/relationships embeddings, GIN pg_trgm on entity names, GIN on JSONB metadata and tsvector FTS, BRIN on chunks.created_at, and well-chosen partial indexes (e.g. idx_documents_workspace_content_hash_unique WHERE ...status='indexed') — 01-edgequake-init.sql:514-680.

Team-feature migrations (053-058) are exemplary: every file has a long header explaining intent, idempotency, and rollback; backfills are guarded and re-runnable; hot-path indexes match the actual read queries (idx_resource_shares_grantee, idx_resource_team_shares_org).

Idempotency is taken seriously almost everywhere: IF NOT EXISTS on tables/columns/indexes, pg_constraint existence guards before ADD CONSTRAINT (043:23-32, 060:17-26), DO-block exception handling around optional AGE extension.
031_conversations_simple.sql:13-24 hardened a previously-destructive DROP TABLE CASCADE behind a column-shape guard, with a comment documenting the data-loss it prevents — good incident hygiene.
AGE graph support degrades gracefully to relational fallback tables (graph_nodes/graph_edges) with upsert/neighbor helper functions when the extension is absent (013_add_age_graph.sql).

Offline-sync data model is clean and privacy-respecting: relay_messages stores only E2E-encrypted blobs with 24h TTL and dedup index; sync_ledger tracks per-user change events (08-relay-sync.sql, 09-sync-ledger.sql).

risks.title: Entities table is GLOBAL across all users — cross-user data leak and corruption
risks.detail: The winning entities table (EdgeQuake) carries constraint entities_unique_name UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) (01-edgequake-init.sql:155). All webapp rows have tenant_id=NULL and workspace_id=NULL, and migration 049 never added a user_id/organization_id column to entities — it only added document_id/type/confidence/properties. Because NULLS NOT DISTINCT treats the two NULLs as equal, the constraint collapses to 'name must be globally unique across the entire installation'. The web insert (apps/web/lib/ingest/document-store.ts:120-126) does ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) DO UPDATE SET document_id = COALESCE(entities.document_id, EXCLUDED.document_id), so when User B ingests a doc mentioning an entity User A already created, no new row is made — B's entity silently resolves to A's existing row, keeps A's document_id, and merges B's metadata into A's row. Result: every user shares one entity namespace; entity->document links point at whoever ingested first; per-user knowledge graphs bleed into each other. This defeats the app-layer visibility model entirely for the entity/graph surface.

risks.title: RLS is enabled+FORCED but completely inert — false sense of isolation
risks.detail: 01-edgequake-init.sql:801-820 ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on documents/entities/etc., and policies isolate by current_tenant_id(). But (a) the app connects as the postgres superuser (docker-compose.yml:61), which bypasses RLS unconditionally regardless of FORCE; (b) no webapp code ever calls set_tenant_context/set_config, so the GUCs are empty; and (c) every policy is written 'tenant_id IS NULL OR tenant_id = current_tenant_id()' — and all webapp rows have tenant_id NULL, so even a non-superuser connection would match ALL rows. There is no user_id/organization_id dimension anywhere in the RLS policies. The protection is purely decorative; isolation rests 100% on app-layer helpers, so a single missing visibility filter = full cross-user exposure with no DB backstop.

risks.title: Schema collision relies on file ordering + IF NOT EXISTS — brittle and surprising
risks.detail: documents, entities, conversations, messages, and graph_nodes are each CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in BOTH 01-edgequake-init.sql and 04-sayknowmind-init.sql with incompatible columns. Correctness depends entirely on Docker mounting 01 before 04 (docker-compose.yml:21-25). Any environment that loads the sayknowmind file first (or a fresh non-Docker bootstrap) gets the opposite shape and the bridge migrations 043/049 — which ALTER assuming the EdgeQuake shape — produce a different table. The webapp documents table is the EdgeQuake one with content NOT NULL/status CHECK/tenant_id, plus 5 bolted-on nullable columns; the design intent (04's clean user-scoped table) never actually exists in production.

risks.title: graph_nodes shape collision breaks the AGE fallback helper functions
risks.detail: 04-sayknowmind-init.sql:84-91 creates graph_nodes(document_id, entity_id, node_type, properties). It runs before migration 013, whose own CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS graph_nodes(graph_name, node_id, label, ...) is therefore skipped. But 013 then defines upsert_graph_node()/get_node_neighbors() that INSERT INTO graph_nodes (graph_name, node_id, label, ...) and reference graph_edges — columns that do not exist on the winning table (and graph_edges is only created by 013). Any call into the relational graph fallback path will throw 'column does not exist' at runtime.

risks.title: No down/rollback migrations; misleading/stale master runner
risks.detail: Not a single migration has a paired down script, so the only recovery path is reset_migrations.sql (full wipe). apply_all_migrations.sql:29-93 references a totally different numbering (001_add_tasks_table.sql, 008_add_rls_policies.sql, etc.) via \i that does not match the files actually present (001_init_database.sql, 009_add_rls_policies.sql...) — running it would fail or apply the wrong set. The real runner is migrate.sh (glob + schema_migrations tracking), making apply_all_migrations.sql/phase*_apply_all.sql dead, confusing artifacts.

risks.title: Hardcoded vector(1536) + ivfflat index without lists/populated data
risks.detail: Both embedding stores fix dimension at 1536: chunks.embedding (01-edgequake-init.sql:110) and vectors.embedding (04-sayknowmind-init.sql:74). The EdgeQuake comment even says '3072 for large models' but the column can't hold them — switching embedding models silently truncates/fails. 04's vectors index uses USING ivfflat (...) with no lists parameter and is created at init time (empty table), which yields a poor/degenerate IVF index; the modern HNSW path lives only on the EdgeQuake chunks table that the webapp does not populate.

risks.title: audit_logs partitions exhaust after 12 months with no default partition
risks.detail: 01-edgequake-init.sql:479-498 pre-creates exactly 12 monthly partitions and provides create_next_audit_log_partition(), but there is no pg_cron/scheduler wired to call it and no DEFAULT partition. Once the pre-created window passes, any INSERT into audit_logs fails ('no partition of relation found for row').

code_review.issue: ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) targets a constraint that, for webapp rows (both NULL), enforces global-across-all-users uniqueness on entity name, causing cross-user entity merging.
code_review.suggested_fix: Add user_id (or organization_id) TEXT to entities, repoint the unique constraint to (organization_id, name) or (user_id, name), and change the ON CONFLICT target accordingly. Requires a migration to drop entities_unique_name and backfill the owner column from documents via document_id.

code_review.issue: UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT on (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) is correct for EdgeQuake tenancy but actively harmful once the table is reused for NULL-tenant webapp rows.
code_review.suggested_fix: Make the constraint tenant-aware only when tenant_id IS NOT NULL (partial unique index) and add a separate per-owner uniqueness for webapp rows.

code_review.issue: ADD COLUMN confidence FLOAT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.8 on a table that may already hold EdgeQuake entity rows is fine, but the migration never reconciles the entities_unique_name constraint that makes the table unusable per-user — it patches columns while leaving the core isolation defect.
code_review.suggested_fix: Extend this migration to add the owner column and fix the unique constraint, since this is the file that already owns 'entities web compat'.

code_review.issue: \i references filenames (001_add_tasks_table.sql, 004_add_audit_log_table.sql, 008_add_rls_policies.sql) that do not exist under db/migrations; the actual files use different numbers/names. The script is stale and would error mid-run.
code_review.suggested_fix: Delete apply_all_migrations.sql and phase*_apply_all.sql, or regenerate them from the real file list. migrate.sh is the single source of truth.

code_review.issue: Per-migration applied-check and INSERT run as separate psql invocations with no surrounding transaction; a migration that half-applies (multi-statement file, no BEGIN) leaves the DB in a partial state yet unrecorded, and a crash between psql -f and the INSERT re-runs the whole file next time (only safe because files are individually idempotent).
code_review.suggested_fix: Wrap each migration apply + schema_migrations insert in a single transaction (psql --single-transaction -f, then insert in the same session), and fail the loop (set -e already) so partial state is rolled back.

code_review.issue: graph_nodes definition collides with migration 013's graph_nodes; whichever runs first wins, leaving 013's helper functions referencing non-existent columns.
code_review.suggested_fix: Rename one of the tables (e.g. doc_graph_nodes for the webapp metadata table) so the two graph stores don't share a name, and update referencing code.

code_review.issue: organization.metadata is TEXT (mirroring better-auth's raw storage) rather than JSONB, so org metadata can't be queried/indexed and silently accepts malformed JSON.
code_review.suggested_fix: Acceptable for better-auth compatibility, but document it; if app code parses it, validate on write.

improvements.what: Add an owner dimension (organization_id or user_id) to entities and replace the global NULLS-NOT-DISTINCT name uniqueness with per-owner uniqueness; migrate ON CONFLICT in document-store.ts to match.
improvements.why: Closes the critical cross-user entity merge/leak; entities are currently the one knowledge surface with zero isolation even at the app layer.

improvements.what: Decide and document one isolation model. Either (a) wire the DB connection to a non-superuser role and call set_config('app.current_*') per request so RLS actually runs, with policies rewritten around organization_id, or (b) formally drop RLS (DISABLE) and the dead EdgeQuake tenancy tables and rely on app-layer visibility explicitly.
improvements.why: The current half-state ships ENABLE+FORCE RLS that does nothing, inviting a false sense of safety and confusing future maintainers.

improvements.what: Split the two schemas physically: stop reusing EdgeQuake table names for webapp tables (or stop loading EdgeQuake init in the webapp DB entirely). At minimum, stop shipping unused EdgeQuake migrations 001-025 into the webapp migration set.
improvements.why: Removes the order-dependent CREATE-TABLE-IF-NOT-EXISTS roulette and the bolt-on patch migrations; clarifies which columns are real in production.

improvements.what: Introduce a real migration tool with up/down and transactional application (e.g. node-pg-migrate, sqlx for the Rust side, or Atlas), and delete the stale apply_all_migrations.sql/phase*_apply_all.sql.
improvements.why: No rollback path today; the master scripts are misleading; transactional safety is only accidental via idempotency.

improvements.what: Parameterize embedding dimension (or add halfvec/separate columns per model) and replace the unparameterized ivfflat index with HNSW; consolidate chunks vs vectors into one embedding store.
improvements.why: 1536 is hardcoded in two places, blocking model upgrades; the ivfflat index built on an empty table is effectively useless.

improvements.what: Schedule create_next_audit_log_partition() (pg_cron) or add a DEFAULT partition to audit_logs.
improvements.why: Inserts fail once the 12 pre-created partitions are exhausted.

subResults.data_flow: Ingestion: apps/web writes documents (insertDocument -> EdgeQuake documents table with bolted-on user_id/organization_id/privacy_level) then entities (insertEntities -> shared global entities table, ON CONFLICT merges across users), then recordSyncEvent enqueues into sync_ledger. Org scoping: 053 mints a personal org per user; 054/057 backfill organization_id onto documents/categories/tags/conversations/ingestion_jobs/shared_content; reads filter by org membership + privacy_level + resource_shares/resource_team_shares in lib/visibility.ts (app layer only). Search/RAG: at-rest projection is documents.content + metadata.blocknote; embeddings nominally in vectors/chunks (vector(1536)); graph via AGE edgequake_graph or relational graph_nodes/graph_edges fallback. Collab: while a doc is open, Hocuspocus (relay-server) reads/writes the Yjs CRDT in doc_collab.state; debounced autosave projects plaintext back to documents and snapshots into document_versions. Offline sync: relay_messages holds encrypted blobs (relay never decrypts); sync_ledger tracks push/pull status. RLS context functions exist but are never invoked, so no tenant GUC ever flows.

subResults.subsystem: Build / CI / Deploy / Ops (Docker, GitLab+GitHub CI, EC2 deploy, Helm, scripts, Makefile)
subResults.purpose: Build, ship and operate the ~12-service SayKnowMind stack: local one-click bootstrap (install.sh / start-all.sh), container builds (per-app + DB Dockerfiles), dual CI (GitLab → GitLab registry; GitHub → ghcr), image-based deploy to the EC2 host at sayknowmind.ypai.click, a Helm chart for K8s, and SQL migration application.
subResults.architecture: Two parallel, partly-overlapping worlds. (1) A docker-compose.yml at repo root defines 12 services (postgres, redis, edgequake, ocr-server, ai-server, web, dashboard, ollama, searxng, mcp-server, relay-server, ipfs) on a single bridge network, wired by compose-internal hostnames and depends_on/healthchecks. Almost every app service uses `build:` (only redis/ollama/searxng/ipfs use `image:`). (2) A registry/image pipeline: GitLab CI builds only `web` to the GitLab Container Registry; GitHub CI builds web/ai-server/dashboard/mcp-server to ghcr via a matrix with gha cache. These two worlds barely touch: the compose file the host actually runs has no `image:` refs for the app services, so `docker compose pull` fetches nothing for them and the registry images are largely orphaned. Deploy has THREE divergent mechanisms (GitLab deploy:production = ssh + compose pull + up; scripts/production-deploy.sh = ssh-less, git pull + up --build; GitHub deploy.yml = generate prod compose + ssh appleboy) plus a Helm chart as a fourth target. Migrations have FOUR orderings (migrate.sh tracked glob; gitlab hardcoded list; production-deploy.sh hardcoded list; github+helm untracked glob). Local dev is native via start-all.sh (nohup background procs, PID files, port-probe readiness) on non-standard ports (web 5400, edgequake 5403, pg 5433). Helm chart is the most coherent artifact: typed values, required-secret guards, securityContext, ingress+cert-manager, resource limits.
whats_good: pnpm pinned deterministically: corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.6 + COREPACK_DEFAULT_TO_LATEST=0 / COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0 (apps/web/Dockerfile:5-7) — directly fixes a real lockfile-mismatch class of bug noted inline.

EdgeQuake Rust build is reproducible and offline: cargo build --release --locked with SQLX_OFFLINE=true and embedded pdfium, multi-arch via TARGETPLATFORM (packages/edgequake/docker/Dockerfile:38-39).
Multi-stage images with non-root runtime users everywhere (web nextjs uid1001 apps/web/Dockerfile:48-61; edgequake useradd -r apps/.../Dockerfile:55-64).
compose uses healthchecks + depends_on: condition: service_healthy for ordering (postgres/edgequake gate web, docker-compose.yml:167-173).

Helm chart is genuinely production-minded: required-secret guards (deploy/helm/.../templates/secret.yaml:8-12), runAsNonRoot + drop ALL caps + allowPrivilegeEscalation:false (values.yaml:231-241), per-service resource requests/limits, TLS via cert-manager issuer, large-upload proxy-body-size annotation.
Secret hygiene at rest is clean: .env is gitignored, only *.env.example files tracked, install.sh generates random BETTER_AUTH_SECRET/ENCRYPTION_KEY/PG password (install.sh:64-66).

production-deploy.sh is a thoughtful ops script: pg_dump backup, DRY_RUN/SKIP_BACKUP/SKIP_RESTART toggles, post-deploy local+external curl verification, and a printed rollback command (scripts/production-deploy.sh:240).
CI migration-check spins a real postgres:16 service and runs every migration without error-swallowing (.github/workflows/ci.yml:167-175) — the one honest schema gate in the whole pipeline.

risks.title: GitHub deploy.yml generates a prod compose that is never shipped to the host AND is itself invalid
risks.detail: The 'Generate docker-compose.prod.yml' step writes the file into the GitHub runner workspace, but the 'Deploy via SSH' step cd's to /opt/sayknowmind on the EC2 host and runs `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml ...` against whatever file already lives there — the generated file is never transferred. Worse, the generated file declares `web: depends_on: postgres: {condition: service_healthy}` but defines NO postgres service, so if it ever were used `docker compose` would error 'service postgres not defined'. The single-quoted heredoc also means REGISTRY/IMAGE_PREFIX/TAG are written literally and only resolved by the host's env, which the runner-generated file never sees.

risks.title: Deploy migration lists are stale by 11 migrations (051-061 never applied on the SSH paths)
risks.detail: Both scripts/production-deploy.sh and .gitlab-ci.yml apply a hardcoded curated migration list that stops at 050_telegram_per_bot_link_scope. Migrations 051-061 — mcp_audit_log, organization tables, organization_id on resources, resource_shares, resource_team_shares, doc_collab, document_versions — are exactly the team/collab/version features in active development and are NOT applied by these paths. A deploy via either path leaves prod schema-drifted, so the new features fail at runtime with missing-relation/column errors.

risks.title: GitHub deploy applies migrations with error-swallowing `|| true`
risks.detail: deploy.yml runs every db/migrations/*.sql with `psql ... || true`, so any failing migration (syntax error, dependency, partial apply) is reported as success and the deploy continues. There is no schema_migrations tracking on this path either, so all migrations re-run every deploy — non-idempotent migrations corrupt or no-op unpredictably. Only the offline migrate.sh tracks applied state.

risks.title: Registry images are disconnected from the compose actually run on the host
risks.detail: docker-compose.yml uses `build:` for web/ai-server/dashboard/mcp-server/edgequake/ocr/postgres and has `image:` only for redis/ollama/searxng/ipfs. GitLab CI builds and pushes ONLY web; GitHub CI builds web/ai-server/dashboard/mcp-server to ghcr. relay-server, edgequake, ocr-server and the custom postgres image are built by NEITHER CI. The GitLab deploy then runs `docker compose pull` + `up -d` (no --build), which pulls nothing for the build-services and would run stale or fail. The whole ghcr/GitLab-registry push pipeline does not feed the runtime compose, which instead rebuilds locally (production-deploy.sh uses up --build). The image pipeline and the deploy unit are incoherent.
risks.evidence: docker-compose.yml:42/204/216/290 (only base images) vs build: blocks; .gitlab-ci.yml:140-141; .github/workflows/ci.yml:93-107

risks.title: Base64-generated Postgres password can break the DATABASE_URL
risks.detail: install.sh generates PG_PASSWORD via `openssl rand -base64 16`, which can contain '+', '/', '=' — characters that are invalid unescaped in the userinfo of a postgres:// URL. It is then embedded raw into DATABASE_URL (install.sh:85) and into every compose `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}` interpolation, producing intermittent auth/parse failures depending on the random output. ENCRYPTION_KEY (hex) and AUTH_SECRET are fine; only the URL-embedded password is the footgun.

risks.title: Weak `:-password` default leaks into runtime DATABASE_URLs
risks.detail: The postgres service hard-requires POSTGRES_PASSWORD (`:?` guard), but every consumer interpolates `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-password}`. If the env file is loaded for some services but not others (or a var name typo), consumers silently connect with literal 'password' while the DB was initialized with the real one — an auth mismatch that surfaces as connection failures rather than a clear config error.

risks.title: Rust engine and relay-server have zero CI coverage
risks.detail: ci.yml runs lint+test+build only for apps/web; ai-server/mcp/dashboard get build-only (no lint/test). packages/edgequake (Rust, 9 crates with an e2e test suite that is currently modified per git status) has no cargo build/clippy/test in any workflow, and packages/relay-server (the collab/sync relay) is neither built nor tested nor image-published by CI. Regressions in the Rust core and the relay ship unverified.
risks.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:14-83 (no rust job; relay absent from matrix :93-107)

risks.title: Host-key TOFU on every SSH deploy
risks.detail: Both SSH deploy paths trust the host key on first contact: GitLab uses ssh-keyscan + StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new; GitHub uses appleboy/ssh-action without a pinned fingerprint. A compromised/spoofed DEPLOY_HOST on first run (or after a key change) would receive the deploy SSH session and any piped registry login, with no pinning to detect MITM.

risks.title: ghcr web:latest is hard-baked to the enterprise/prod URL
risks.detail: The GitHub docker-images matrix passes NO --build-args, so the web image always uses the Dockerfile defaults: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://sayknowmind.ypai.click and NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_MODE=saas (baked into client JS). GitLab DOES pass APP_URL/DEPLOY_MODE. So the ghcr 'web:latest' can never serve the open/local edition and silently ships the prod SaaS origin to any consumer of that image; the two CI systems also produce divergent web bundles.

risks.title: Custom Postgres image ships a release-candidate AGE extension
risks.detail: docker/Dockerfile.postgres builds Apache AGE from tag PG16/v1.6.0-rc0 — a release candidate — into the primary production datastore. pgvector is pinned to a GA tag (v0.7.4) but the graph extension is pre-GA.
