risks.title: Brittle infra healthchecks
risks.detail: The IPFS healthcheck pins a hardcoded CID (`ipfs dag stat /ipfs/QmUNLL...`) that depends on that block being locally pinned, so it can flap/false-fail; searxng SEARXNG_BASE_URL is hardcoded to http://localhost which is wrong behind the TLS reverse proxy.

code_review.issue: Generated docker-compose.prod.yml stays in the runner and is never copied to the host; the SSH step relies on a hand-maintained file at /opt/sayknowmind. The generated file also references an undefined postgres service in depends_on.
code_review.suggested_fix: Either scp the generated file to the host before `docker compose up`, or drop the generation step entirely and commit a real docker-compose.prod.yml that includes postgres (or env_file). Make the deploy use the file it actually generated.

code_review.issue: `psql ... || true` swallows migration failures; no schema_migrations tracking so all migrations re-run every deploy.
code_review.suggested_fix: Call the tracked runner db/migrations/scripts/migrate.sh (which records schema_migrations and skips applied files) and remove `|| true` so a bad migration fails the deploy.

code_review.issue: Hardcoded migration list ends at 050; 051-061 never applied. Every new migration requires editing this script, which has already fallen behind by 11 files including the org/team/collab/versions schema.
code_review.suggested_fix: Replace the curated apply_sql list with a call to the tracked migrate.sh glob runner so new migrations are picked up automatically and idempotently.

code_review.issue: openssl rand -base64 16 can yield +,/,= which corrupt the postgres:// DATABASE_URL it is interpolated into.
code_review.suggested_fix: Generate URL-safe passwords, e.g. `openssl rand -hex 24`, or percent-encode before embedding in DATABASE_URL.

code_review.issue: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-password} default differs from the postgres service's mandatory `:?` requirement, allowing silent auth mismatch.
code_review.suggested_fix: Drop the :-password defaults and use the same `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?}` guard (or a shared DATABASE_URL variable) across all consumers.

code_review.issue: Mixed package managers (web/dashboard pnpm vs ai-server/mcp npm ci) and the root pnpm-lock.yaml is a 611-byte stub — this is not a real pnpm workspace, so shared packages/* are not linked at build and toolchains drift (node 20 in ai-server Dockerfile vs node 22 in CI).
code_review.suggested_fix: Standardize on one package manager + a real workspace lockfile, or document why each app vendors its own; align node versions (22) across Dockerfiles and CI.

code_review.issue: Only apps/web is linted+tested; edgequake (Rust) and relay-server have no CI build/test at all.
code_review.suggested_fix: Add a cargo build/clippy/test job for packages/edgequake and a build+test+image job for relay-server (it is in compose and Helm but invisible to CI).

code_review.issue: Apache AGE built from PG16/v1.6.0-rc0 (release candidate) into the prod DB image.
code_review.suggested_fix: Pin to a GA AGE tag once available, or document the rc pin and its risk.

improvements.what: Collapse the three SSH/script deploy mechanisms into one source of truth
improvements.why: GitLab deploy (pull/no-build), production-deploy.sh (git pull/up --build), and GitHub deploy.yml (generate compose/ssh) make different, conflicting assumptions about whether the host builds or pulls images and which compose file is canonical. One of them works in practice and the others are latent footguns. Pick the registry-image path (compose with image: refs pointing at ghcr) OR the build-on-host path, and delete the rest.

improvements.what: Make migration application automatic, tracked, and the same everywhere
improvements.why: Four different migration orderings, two of them stale at 050 and one swallowing errors, is the single biggest operational risk — it directly breaks the team/collab/versions features now in flight. Route every path (CI check, both deploys, Helm job) through migrate.sh's tracked glob so adding a file is the only step required.

improvements.what: Reconcile the image pipeline with the runtime compose
improvements.why: CI pushes images that the host compose never references; relay/edgequake/ocr/postgres images are built by no CI. Either add image: tags to compose and have CI build all 8 images, or stop pushing images CI doesn't deploy. Today the ghcr/GitLab registries are mostly dead weight.

improvements.what: Add CI coverage for the Rust engine and relay-server
improvements.why: edgequake is the RAG core (9 crates, an e2e suite currently modified) and relay-server backs real-time collab; both ship with zero automated build/test gate. A cargo clippy/test job and a relay build/test job would catch regressions before deploy.

improvements.what: Harden secret/host handling in deploys
improvements.why: URL-unsafe generated DB passwords, :-password defaults, and unpinned SSH host keys are all small, individually-low risks that compound into hard-to-debug auth failures and a MITM window. Fix URL-safe secret gen, unify the password guard, and pin known_hosts fingerprints.

tech_debt: Stale hardcoded migration lists in .gitlab-ci.yml and production-deploy.sh (frozen at 050; real tree at 061).
Root pnpm-lock.yaml is a 611-byte stub; per-app lockfiles + mixed npm/pnpm = not a real monorepo workspace.
Node version drift: ai-server Dockerfile node:20-alpine vs web node:22-alpine vs CI node 22.
Two CI systems (GitLab + GitHub) building overlapping-but-different artifacts to two different registries with different build-args (GitLab bakes APP_URL, GitHub does not).
deploy.yml generates a compose file it never uses and references an undefined postgres service.
better-auth rateLimit table created ad-hoc via inline psql in CI/scripts instead of a committed migration (.gitlab-ci.yml:106-112, production-deploy.sh:191).
Reference/dead files left in tree: docker/edgequake-docker-compose.reference.yml, apps/web/.next/standalone/Dockerfile committed build artifact.
Helm chart relies on db-init being manually synced from db/init via `make helm-sync` — drift if forgotten.
Brittle infra healthchecks (hardcoded IPFS CID; searxng localhost base URL behind TLS proxy).

crossResults.summary: Verified against source: the security posture is structurally broken in two independent ways. (1) The EdgeQuake Rust API — the system of record for documents, vectors, graph, users, tenants — ships with NO authentication, NO rate limiting, NO RBAC, and a hardcoded JWT secret; every endpoint including unauthenticated admin-user creation is reachable by anyone. (2) Tenant isolation everywhere is app-layer-only and the one real engine-level filter (EdgeQuake vector search) is fail-OPEN. On top of this sit a cluster of unauthenticated web routes that execute shell commands, overwrite global LLM prompts, leak env config, and create users; plaintext MCP API keys; caller-supplied identity in the AI server under a single shared key; remote-cloud-reachable privileged Tauri commands that clone+run third-party code; and fail-open Telegram/MCP/encryption defaults. RLS is enabled+FORCED in SQL but completely inert (superuser connection + empty GUCs + tenant_id-IS-NULL escape clauses), so there is no database backstop — a single missing app-layer filter is full cross-user exposure.

findings.title: EdgeQuake HTTP API ships with NO authentication or rate-limiting wired onto the router
findings.detail: build_router() in packages/edgequake/crates/edgequake-api/src/server.rs:85-117 layers only DefaultBodyLimit, request_logging, request_id, TraceLayer, permissive CORS (allow_origin(Any)/methods(Any)/headers(Any)), compression, and Swagger. The api_key_auth and tenant_rate_limit middleware are defined and exported but never .layer()'d, and no JWT-verification middleware exists at all. Every /api/v1 endpoint — documents, query, graph, users, tenants, workspaces, delete-all — is reachable unauthenticated. Auth handlers mint JWTs that nothing downstream requires (only /auth/me ever verifies a token, for its own logic). This is the single largest exposure: the entire RAG datastore is an open API.
findings.evidence: server.rs:85-117 (verified: only body-limit/logging/request-id/trace/CORS-Any/compression/swagger layers); middleware.rs:166 (api_key_auth) and :287 (tenant_rate_limit) defined but unwired; routes.rs ~150 endpoints all ungated.
findings.recommendation: Add a global auth middleware layer (from_fn_with_state) in build_router that verifies the JWT bearer on all /api/v1 routes except a public allowlist (/health, /auth/login, /auth/refresh). Wire tenant_rate_limit. Replace CORS Any with an explicit origin allowlist. Add an integration test asserting an unauthenticated request to /api/v1/documents returns 401.

findings.title: EdgeQuake uses a hardcoded default JWT secret in production state (JWT_SECRET env ignored)
findings.detail: AppState::new_postgres constructs auth with AuthConfig::default() (state/postgres.rs:293) instead of AuthConfig::from_env(). AuthConfig::default() hardcodes jwt_secret = 'change-me-in-production-256-bit-secret-key' (auth/config.rs:51). from_env() exists (config.rs:127) but is never called by the running binary, so the JWT_SECRET environment variable has zero effect. Anyone can forge a valid HS256 token for any user/role using the public default string. Even if the auth middleware above were wired, it would verify forged tokens. The documented '>=32 byte secret' rule is never enforced at runtime.
findings.evidence: state/postgres.rs:293 `let auth_config = AuthConfig::default();` (verified); auth/config.rs:51 default jwt_secret literal (verified); config.rs:127 from_env exists but unused on the postgres path.
findings.recommendation: Switch new_postgres to AuthConfig::from_env(); fail fast at startup if JWT_SECRET is unset or <32 bytes (panic with a clear message rather than silently using a dev default). Remove the hardcoded production-looking default from Default impl (use a clearly-invalid sentinel that forces configuration).

findings.title: Unauthenticated EdgeQuake user creation with caller-chosen role (privilege escalation)
findings.detail: POST /api/v1/users (handlers/auth/user_management.rs:43) takes only State + Json with no auth/admin check and parses the role straight from the request body (role = request.role.map(Role::parse).unwrap_or(Role::User)), so a caller can pass role:'admin'. The OpenAPI annotation documents a '403 Admin access required' that the code never returns, and the e2e suite (e2e_auth.rs) codifies unauthenticated admin creation as correct behavior. Combined with the unwired auth layer, this is anonymous admin account provisioning against the RAG engine.
findings.evidence: user_management.rs:43-99 (verified: no auth, role from body, defaults User but accepts admin); routes.rs registers create_user with no guard; e2e_auth.rs asserts success with no auth.
findings.recommendation: Require an authenticated admin caller (RbacService.check_permission once auth is wired); reject any role elevation above the requested account's own role unless the caller is admin. Update the test to assert 401/403 for unauthenticated creation.

findings.title: EdgeQuake vector-search tenant filter is fail-OPEN — cross-tenant data leak
findings.detail: matches_tenant_filter (edgequake-query/src/sota_engine/prompt.rs:10-37) returns true whenever a vector's metadata LACKS a tenant_id/workspace_id key — it only rejects on a present-but-mismatched key. Any vector stored without these metadata keys is visible to EVERY tenant's query. This is inconsistent with the graph-node path (fail-closed) in the same engine. Worse, on the shared default vector table the SQL passes filter_ids=None, so cross-tenant rows are fetched first and only weakly post-filtered, causing both leakage and recall loss. Because the web app indexes all users into one shared EdgeQuake workspace (edgequake/client.ts hardcoded tenant/workspace), this directly bridges to cross-user content exposure.
findings.evidence: prompt.rs:16-36 verified: `if tenant_id.is_none() && workspace_id.is_none() { return true }` then `if let Some(meta_tid)=...` — absent key falls through to final `true`; contrast graph-node fail-closed policy in graph/mod.rs.
findings.recommendation: Make the filter fail-CLOSED: when a tenant/workspace filter is requested, a vector whose metadata is missing that key must be excluded (return false). Add a SQL-level predicate (metadata->>'tenant_id' = $tid) so cross-tenant rows are never fetched into top-k. Backfill tenant_id/workspace_id on existing untagged vectors.

findings.title: Tenant/workspace isolation keyed on spoofable client headers with no identity binding (EdgeQuake + dashboard)
findings.detail: EdgeQuake's TenantContext is extracted purely from X-Tenant-ID/X-Workspace-ID/X-User-ID request headers (middleware.rs:365-398) and handlers/isolation.rs filters data by matching those exact header values. No auth layer binds the caller to a tenant, so any client sets arbitrary headers to read/write another tenant's documents, graph, and conversations. apps/dashboard amplifies this: it sends the same client-controlled headers from localStorage with an anonymous-UUID fallback (src/lib/api/client.ts:121-186), has skip-login (login/page.tsx handleSkipLogin routes to /graph with no demo gate), and no route auth guard — and it is shipped as a Docker image. Two frontends now assert identity via spoofable headers against the unauthenticated engine.
findings.evidence: middleware.rs:365-398 (header-derived TenantContext); handlers/isolation.rs:1-45 (match-by-header); dashboard client.ts:121-186 (localStorage headers + UUID fallback); login/page.tsx skip-login.
findings.recommendation: Derive tenant_id/user_id from the verified JWT subject server-side; ignore client-supplied X-Tenant-ID/X-User-ID for authorization (use only for routing within the caller's permitted scope). Gate dashboard routes behind real auth and remove always-on skip-login.

findings.title: Three unauthenticated web routes that leak config, overwrite global prompts, and run shell commands
findings.detail: (a) /api/auth/test: GET returns BETTER_AUTH_URL/NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL/TRUSTED_ORIGINS and which secrets are set; POST calls auth.api.signUpEmail() creating a real persisted user on every hit with a 'Clean up' comment that deletes nothing — unauthenticated user creation / DB pollution / DoS. (b) /api/settings/prompts POST: zero auth, writes a single global .sayknowmind-prompts.json that loadPrompts() feeds into chat + document-processing system prompts for ALL users — stored prompt injection / jailbreak / defacement for the whole instance. (c) /api/desktop/runtime: no auth, uses execSync/execFile for which/docker/ollama/git/tar/cp/pnpm build/rm -rf, downloads+extracts a Node tarball, and spawns a detached server — intended for Tauri localhost but has no desktop/env guard, so in a hosted build it is unauthenticated remote command execution.
findings.evidence: auth/test/route.ts:1-37 (verified GET env leak, POST signUpEmail, no deletion); settings/prompts/route.ts:203-225 (verified POST writeFileSync, no auth); desktop/runtime/route.ts:1-55 (verified execSync, export GET, no auth/getOrgContext).
findings.recommendation: Delete /api/auth/test entirely. Add auth to settings/prompts and scope prompts per-user (not a global cwd file). Guard desktop/runtime behind a strict env check (e.g. process.env.SAYKNOWMIND_DESKTOP==='1' AND bind to 127.0.0.1 only) or move it out of the Next.js app into the Tauri Rust side; never ship it in hosted builds.

findings.title: MCP / web API keys stored and compared in plaintext; open-admin fallback
findings.detail: user_mcp_keys.api_key holds the raw sk-mcp-<hex> token and both the web app (session-helper.ts:11-24 — SELECT user_id FROM user_mcp_keys WHERE api_key=$1) and the MCP server authenticate via plaintext, non-constant-time equality. A single DB read/backup/log leak exposes every live key. Keys never expire and there is exactly one per user (PRIMARY KEY user_id), so rotation has no grace window. ensureTable() runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on the request hot path. Separately, the MCP server grants isAdmin:true with NO token when both MCP_API_KEY and DATABASE_URL are unset (index.ts:79-82) — a public deploy that forgets either var gives every caller admin access to the shared EdgeQuake index, advertised openly on /health.
findings.evidence: session-helper.ts:11-24 (verified plaintext equality SELECT); mcp-server/src/index.ts:79-82 (verified `if (!ADMIN_API_KEY && !DATABASE_URL) { ...isAdmin:true }`); user/mcp-key/route.ts ensureTable on hot path.
findings.recommendation: Store only a SHA-256 (or HMAC) hash of the key; authenticate by hashing the presented token and comparing constant-time; show the raw key once at creation. Add expiry + support multiple keys per user for rotation. Make MCP open mode require an explicit OPEN_MODE=true flag instead of defaulting on when config is absent. Move ensureTable into migrations.

findings.title: Privileged Tauri commands reachable from the remote cloud webview; ocp_install runs unpinned third-party code
findings.detail: App-defined #[tauri::command]s are NOT ACL-gated by capability files (capabilities only gate core/plugin commands). The lite build (the only variant CI ships) loads the remote cloud origin, and remote.json grants only shell:allow-open while warning to 'keep the list tight' — but that scoping does nothing for custom commands. So JS served by sayknowmind.ypai.click, or any XSS in it, can invoke ocp_install, exec_codex_login, chat_via_codex, provision_ocp_key, open_external_url directly (all registered in generate_handler! at main.rs:1649-1671). ocp_install_sync hardcodes `git clone https://github.com/dtzp555-max/ocp.git` then runs npm install + node setup.mjs + launchctl — arbitrary, unpinned code from a personal account, triggerable by remote JS. With a permissive CSP (script-src 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'), a cloud XSS escalates to local code execution.
findings.evidence: main.rs:1649-1671 (verified full command list registered globally); remote.json (verified: only core:* + shell:allow-open, with the warning comment); main.rs ocp_install_sync git clone of dtzp555-max/ocp.
findings.recommendation: Do not expose ocp_install/exec_codex_login/provision_ocp_key/chat_via_codex to the remote webview. Split commands so privileged ones are only registered for a local/full-mode window, or add an explicit origin check at the top of each command (reject unless the caller window is the trusted local origin). Pin ocp to a vetted commit hash with integrity verification, ideally vendor it. Tighten the CSP (drop unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval).

findings.title: AI server: caller-supplied identity under a single shared key = cross-tenant memory IDOR; incomplete GDPR delete
findings.detail: userId/sessionId/organizationId come straight from the request body/path, while the only auth is one shared AI_API_KEY for all callers (signature.guard.ts) — or fully bypassed when SKIP_AUTH=true. Any holder of the shared key (or anyone in SKIP_AUTH/dev) can read/write/delete ANY user's memory by passing an arbitrary userId; GET/DELETE /ai/memory/:userId expose this directly. Additionally, getUserMemory/deleteUserMemory never pass organizationId, so they only touch legacy un-prefixed keys while the chat path writes org-prefixed keys — GDPR deletion silently leaves org:{orgId}:user:{id}:* data behind.
findings.evidence: signature.guard.ts:21-46 (verified single shared AI_API_KEY + SKIP_AUTH bypass returning true with dev-client); chat.dto.ts identity from body; ai.controller.ts GET/DELETE /ai/memory/:userId; memory-keys.helper.ts org-prefix write vs un-prefixed read.
findings.recommendation: Bind identity to a per-caller credential: have the web app pass a signed assertion (or forward the user's JWT) that the AI server verifies, and derive userId/organizationId from it rather than trusting the body. Remove SKIP_AUTH from any non-dev build. Make GDPR delete enumerate and clear both org-prefixed and legacy keys plus span:* metrics.

findings.title: RLS is ENABLE+FORCE but completely inert — no database backstop for isolation
findings.detail: 01-edgequake-init.sql enables and FORCEs row-level security with policies keyed on current_tenant_id(), but (a) the app connects as the postgres superuser (docker-compose.yml), which bypasses RLS unconditionally; (b) no webapp or EdgeQuake code reliably sets the session GUC — set_tenant_context/set_config run on a pooled connection (rls.rs / conversation.rs) while the business query grabs a different pooled connection; and (c) every policy is written 'tenant_id IS NULL OR tenant_id = current_tenant_id()' and all webapp rows have tenant_id NULL, so even a non-superuser would match ALL rows. There is no user_id/organization_id dimension in any policy. Result: isolation rests 100% on app-layer lib/visibility.ts — one missing readableClause/writableClause is full cross-user exposure with zero DB defense. Secondary code paths already skip the filter (orchestrator.ts, ultrarag executor.ts, job-queue related-docs).
findings.evidence: 01-edgequake-init.sql:801-836 ENABLE+FORCE + tenant_id-IS-NULL policies; docker-compose.yml superuser connection; rls.rs:123-173 / conversation.rs:57-74 set_config on pool not pinned connection; orchestrator.ts:122 + executor.ts:138 return raw EdgeQuake hits unfiltered.
findings.recommendation: Treat app-layer filtering as the sole control and harden it: connect as a non-superuser role and either make RLS real (pin a dedicated connection per request, set GUCs, add user_id/org_id policies, remove the IS-NULL escape) or remove the decorative RLS to stop the false sense of safety. Add the readableClause re-filter to orchestrator/ultrarag/related-docs paths. Add a CI test that fails if a known cross-tenant query returns another user's row.

findings.title: Fail-open defaults: Telegram webhook secret, relay Telegram proxy, and relay 'encryption'
findings.detail: Telegram webhook handlers only enforce x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token when TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set; unset (the default) lets anyone who knows a numeric botId POST forged updates that drive ingestion, burn the linked user's daily AI quota, and assign categories (webhook/route.ts:795-798, verified). The public relay Telegram proxy is likewise fail-open and returns 200 on forwarding failure (telegram-proxy.ts). Relay offline-sync is marketed as encrypted but encryptForUser has a base64 dev fallback when keys are unset, with no guard/warning at the sync layer — a silent confidentiality downgrade; and in the shared-server edition the server holds the key, so it is at-rest, not end-to-end.
findings.evidence: webhook/route.ts:796 `if (process.env.TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && secret !== ...)` (verified — check skipped when unset); relay telegram-proxy.ts fail-open + ok:true on error; lib/encryption.ts base64 dev fallback + dev-only secret.
findings.recommendation: Make the webhook secret mandatory (reject all updates if unset) and verify it constant-time; have the relay proxy reject when the secret is unconfigured. At the sync layer, refuse to push and log a hard error if real encryption keys are absent instead of silently base64-encoding. Document clearly that shared-server relay is server-side-at-rest, not E2E.

findings.title: SSRF: OG image fetcher and ingest URL paths; IDOR on category assignment
findings.detail: og/[id] server-side fetch()es user-controlled doc.url to scrape og:image, gated only by privacy_level==='shared' and url.startsWith('http') — no IP/host allowlist, so a shared doc with url=http://169.254.169.254/... turns the server into an SSRF proxy (5s timeout limits, not prevents). The main ingest url-fetcher.ts DOES validate (DNS-resolve + reject private/loopback/link-local/metadata), so og bypasses the existing protection. Separately, assignDocumentCategory() does an unscoped INSERT with no ownership/org check, and POST /api/ingest/text passes a caller-supplied categoryId straight through, letting a user write document_categories rows against another tenant's category id.
findings.evidence: og/[id]/route.ts:132-150 fetchOgImageFromPage with only http-prefix check; url-fetcher.ts:24-72 proper SSRF guard (the pattern og should reuse); document-store.ts:189-199 unscoped category INSERT; ingest/text/route.ts:67-68 passes categoryId unchecked.
findings.recommendation: Reuse url-fetcher.ts validateUrl() inside og/[id] before fetching (DNS-resolve + private-range block). Add a readable/writable ownership check on categoryId in assignDocumentCategory and at the ingest/text call site.

crossResults.overall_assessment: The project has thoughtful defense-in-depth in isolated places (web url-fetcher SSRF guard, MCP constant-time token compare with audience separation, pipeline.ts readableClause re-filter, Argon2id hashing), but the overall security architecture does not hold together. The two foundational failures are: (1) the EdgeQuake engine that owns all data runs with no authentication, no RBAC, a hardcoded JWT secret, and header-spoofable tenancy — it is effectively a public datastore; and (2) tenant isolation across the whole system is app-layer-only with an inert RLS layer that creates a false sense of safety, while several real isolation points are fail-open (vector filter, Telegram/MCP/encryption defaults, secondary search paths). Layered on top are multiple unauthenticated high-impact web routes (config leak, global prompt overwrite, shell execution, user creation), plaintext API keys, remote-reachable privileged Tauri commands that run unpinned third-party code, and a cross-tenant memory IDOR in the AI server. Grade D: not F because the web app's core data routes are genuinely disciplined and the worst exploit (EdgeQuake) is plausibly deployed on a private network today — but every one of these is a concrete, verified path, and the absence of any DB-level backstop means a single app-layer mistake is total cross-user exposure. Priority order for remediation: wire EdgeQuake auth + real JWT secret (criticals 1-2), close the unauthenticated web exec/prompt/test routes and gate the desktop runtime, make the vector filter and Telegram/encryption defaults fail-closed, hash the MCP keys, and stop exposing privileged Tauri commands to the remote webview.

crossResults.dimension: End-to-end Data Flow & Consistency (ingest → store → graph; search/chat → query → SSE; collab → relay → version)
crossResults.summary: I traced the three core flows against real code. The ingest path (insertDocument → fire-and-forget createJob → processJob 5-step state machine → EdgeQuake index) and the chat path (detectIntent → searchKnowledge → EdgeQuake query + Postgres readableClause re-filter → SSE) are well-structured on the happy path, and pipeline.ts genuinely re-filters every EdgeQuake hit through Postgres visibility (verified pipeline.ts:589, 649, 688) — the single most important consistency guard, and it holds. But the dual-write seam between Postgres and the single shared EdgeQuake workspace is fragile in several concrete, verified ways: (1) the global entities table merges entities across all users; (2) document deletion has NO EdgeQuake de-index path whatsoever — the client exposes no delete method, so vectors/graph nodes orphan permanently in the shared index; (3) the related-docs linker writes cross-tenant document_relations rows from raw EdgeQuake ids; (4) secondary read paths (orchestrator, ultrarag) skip the re-filter that pipeline.ts relies on for isolation; (5) ingest is a fire-and-forget, in-process job with no durable re-drive, so a restart strands documents in Postgres that never get indexed. These are not theoretical — each is backed by file:line evidence below.

findings.title: Document deletion never de-indexes EdgeQuake — permanent orphaned vectors/graph in the shared index
findings.detail: apps/web/lib/edgequake/client.ts exports only queryEdgeQuake, getGraph, streamQuery, indexDocument, healthCheck, updateEmbeddingProvider, syncUnindexedToEdgeQuake, testEmbeddingProvider — there is NO delete/de-index method (verified by enumerating all exports). Yet documents are hard-DELETEd from Postgres in at least four places: documents/[id]/route.ts:297, documents/trash/route.ts:23, admin/users/[id]/route.ts:69 (DELETE all docs for a user), and relay/sync-service.ts:340 (sync-driven delete). None of these calls EdgeQuake. Because all users share one EdgeQuake workspace (client.ts:10-12), every deleted document's chunks, entity vectors, relationship vectors and AGE graph nodes remain in the shared index forever. The chat path's readableClause re-filter (pipeline.ts:589) coincidentally hides this from search results (deleted ids no longer resolve in Postgres), masking the leak — but the index grows unbounded, the knowledge graph retains nodes for deleted docs, and any code path that trusts EdgeQuake ids without the Postgres re-filter (see related findings) can surface deleted content. This is the most serious consistency gap: a delete in one store is silently a no-op in the other.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/edgequake/client.ts (no delete export, lines 100-338); apps/web/app/api/documents/[id]/route.ts:297; apps/web/app/api/documents/trash/route.ts:23; apps/web/app/api/admin/users/[id]/route.ts:69; apps/web/lib/relay/sync-service.ts:340
findings.recommendation: Add a deleteDocument(documentId, scope) method to the EdgeQuake client and call it from every document-delete path (single delete, trash purge, admin user wipe, relay-sync delete). Until then, run a periodic reconciliation job that diffs EdgeQuake document_ids against live Postgres documents.id and purges orphans. Add document_id → documents FK or a cleanup trigger for document_relations so deleted-doc linkage rows don't accumulate either.

findings.title: Global entities table merges entities across ALL users (dual-model collision is a live data bug)
findings.detail: insertEntities() (document-store.ts:113-140) inserts only (document_id, name, entity_type, type, confidence, metadata) and omits tenant_id/workspace_id, so every web-app entity row has tenant_id=NULL, workspace_id=NULL. The winning table is EdgeQuake's, whose constraint is entities_unique_name UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) (01-edgequake-init.sql:155). Because NULLS NOT DISTINCT treats two NULLs as equal, the constraint collapses to 'entity name must be globally unique across the entire install.' The INSERT's ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) DO UPDATE SET document_id = COALESCE(entities.document_id, EXCLUDED.document_id) (document-store.ts:122-125) means when user B ingests a doc mentioning an entity user A already created, no new row is made: B's entity resolves to A's existing row, keeps A's document_id, and merges B's metadata into A's row. Every entity→document graph edge therefore points at whoever ingested first, and per-user knowledge graphs bleed together. This defeats the app-layer visibility model for the entire entity/graph surface. Migration 049 added document_id/type/confidence but never touched the constraint.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/ingest/document-store.ts:118-136; db/init/01-edgequake-init.sql:155; db/migrations/049_web_graph_schema_compat.sql
findings.recommendation: Add user_id/organization_id to entities for web rows and redefine the uniqueness key to include the owner scope (or use a separate web-entities table). Change the ON CONFLICT target accordingly so per-user entities never merge. Backfill/repair existing merged rows.

findings.title: related-docs linker writes cross-tenant document_relations from unfiltered EdgeQuake ids
findings.detail: In processJob, after metadata enrichment the job queries EdgeQuake for similar docs and INSERTs document_relations rows using rel.document_id straight from EdgeQuake's response, filtered only by score > 0.7 and id != self (job-queue.ts:423-443). Because EdgeQuake is one shared workspace across all users, similar.sources can contain another tenant's document_id. There is NO readableClause / ownership check before the INSERT, so a user's document can get a 'similar' relation row pointing at a document they cannot see. This is the same shared-index trust gap that pipeline.ts carefully avoids, reappearing on the write side. Any UI that renders related documents from this table can then leak the existence (and via a node-detail fetch, possibly content) of another tenant's doc.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/ingest/job-queue.ts:423-443
findings.recommendation: Before inserting document_relations, resolve rel.document_id through a Postgres query gated by readableClause for the ingesting user/org and drop any id that isn't readable. Apply the same guard wherever EdgeQuake-returned ids are persisted.

findings.title: Secondary EdgeQuake read paths skip the visibility re-filter that isolation depends on
findings.detail: Tenant isolation over the shared EdgeQuake index rests ENTIRELY on the post-query readableClause re-filter, and only pipeline.ts performs it (verified pipeline.ts:589, 649, 688). Two other live-or-latent read paths return EdgeQuake content raw: orchestrator.ts:122 returns eqResult.answer || joined eqResult.sources[].snippet with no Postgres re-resolution, and ultrarag/executor.ts:139 returns queryEdgeQuake output directly. orchestrator is currently dead, but /api/pipeline (ultrarag) is wired, so the executor 'search' step can return another tenant's snippets verbatim. The inconsistency is the real risk: isolation is enforced in exactly one of three places that read the same shared index.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/agents/orchestrator.ts:110-122; apps/web/lib/ultrarag/executor.ts:139; apps/web/lib/agents/pipeline.ts:589
findings.recommendation: Centralize EdgeQuake retrieval behind a single helper that always re-resolves document_ids through readableClause and returns only readable sources. Make orchestrator/ultrarag consume that helper rather than calling queryEdgeQuake directly. Delete the dead orchestrator path if it stays unused.

findings.title: Ingest dual-write is fire-and-forget with no durable re-drive — documents stranded in Postgres, never indexed in EdgeQuake
findings.detail: insertDocument writes the Postgres row, then createJob() inserts an ingestion_jobs row and fire-and-forgets processJobById(jobId).catch(...) (job-queue.ts:63-66). The concurrency semaphore (activeJobs/jobWaiters, lines 28-42) and retry scheduling (setTimeout → processJobById, line 491) are pure in-process state. There is no startup reconciliation: apps/web has no instrumentation.ts and no requeue/sweeper for stale 'processing'/'pending' rows (grep found none). So a deploy/crash/serverless teardown while a job is processing or sleeping in a setTimeout retry strands the document — Postgres has the row, EdgeQuake never indexes it, and nothing re-drives it. The two stores diverge silently. (syncUnindexedToEdgeQuake exists but is only invoked on demand, not on startup.)
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/ingest/job-queue.ts:63-66, 28-42, 481-495; absence of apps/web/instrumentation.ts
findings.recommendation: Add a startup reconciler (Next instrumentation.ts register() or a cron) that requeues ingestion_jobs stuck in processing/pending past a threshold, and periodically calls syncUnindexedToEdgeQuake. Persist retry schedule in the DB rather than in-process setTimeout.

findings.title: async_processing flag inconsistent in the hot ingest path — 30s blocking index can fail large docs
findings.detail: job-queue.ts indexes with async_processing:false (line 394) against a client whose EDGEQUAKE_TIMEOUT is 30s (client.ts:8). The client default is async_processing:true (client.ts:218) and syncUnindexedToEdgeQuake uses that default. So the slow path (large documents whose chunking + LLM graph extraction exceed 30s) picked the BLOCKING option: it throws, sets edgequake_sync_failed, and if metadata also failed, fails the whole job — whereas async_processing:true would have returned immediately and let EdgeQuake process in the background. The two index call-sites disagree on the durability/latency tradeoff for the same operation.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/ingest/job-queue.ts:388-406; apps/web/lib/edgequake/client.ts:8,218
findings.recommendation: Use async_processing:true in the hot ingest path (consistent with sync), and track indexed_at via a completion signal/poll rather than a 30s synchronous wait. Or raise the timeout specifically for indexing.

findings.title: Relay offline-sync confidentiality silently downgrades to a predictable shared key
findings.detail: sync-service.ts encrypts every pushed payload via encryptForUser (line 111). encryption.ts derives the master secret as process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY ?? process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET ?? 'dev-only-not-for-production' (encryption.ts:93, with the same fallback at 84). The crypto itself is real AES (wire format base64-encoded, not plaintext base64 as sometimes described), but when neither env var is set the key is the hardcoded literal 'dev-only-not-for-production'. The sync layer emits no warning when this fallback is in effect, so a misconfigured deployment pushes 'encrypted' blobs through the relay under a publicly-known key — a silent confidentiality downgrade for the marketed encrypted offline-sync.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/relay/sync-service.ts:111; apps/web/lib/encryption.ts:84,93
findings.recommendation: Fail closed (or loudly warn and refuse to push) when ENCRYPTION_KEY/BETTER_AUTH_SECRET are unset rather than falling back to a constant key. Log the key source at startup. Consider a real per-user/per-device key rather than deriving from the auth secret.

findings.title: Version-capture guard omits metadata.univer — sheet-only saves can skip the checkpoint
findings.detail: On PATCH, version capture fires only when isContentSave is true, computed as content !== undefined || (metadata.docTabs !== undefined || metadata.mindmap !== undefined) (documents/[id]/route.ts:253-255). metadata.univer (the spreadsheet snapshot) is not in the guard. A save that updates only the Univer snapshot without changing flat content or the docTabs list would not capture a version, despite version history being advertised for sheets. In practice doc-tabs persistence usually co-sends content and docTabs, which masks this, but the guard's omission is a latent gap for any sheet-only persistence path. captureDocumentVersion itself is throttled + content-deduped, so the cost of broadening the guard is negligible.
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/api/documents/[id]/route.ts:253-258; apps/web/lib/versions/store.ts:15-25
findings.recommendation: Add metadata.univer to the isContentSave predicate so spreadsheet snapshots are checkpointed consistently with notes and mindmaps.

findings.title: Chat-path visibility re-filter is solid defense-in-depth (positive control verified)
findings.detail: Confirming the load-bearing guard works: searchKnowledge re-resolves every EdgeQuake vector hit through Postgres readableClause before returning (pipeline.ts:589), and both fallback paths — keyword ILIKE (pipeline.ts:649) and the LLM catalog fallback (pipeline.ts:688) — are also gated by readableClause. search/route.ts additionally refuses to return an uncited synthesized EdgeQuake answer and re-runs a Postgres-scoped fallback. This is the one place the shared-EdgeQuake isolation model is correctly enforced, and it holds. The findings above are about the OTHER paths that don't share this discipline.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/agents/pipeline.ts:589,649,688
findings.recommendation: Promote this pattern into a single shared retrieval helper and route all EdgeQuake reads through it, so the guarantee is structural rather than re-implemented per call site.

crossResults.overall_assessment: The end-to-end flows are coherent and thoughtfully built on the happy path — the regex-first intent router, the 5-step ingest state machine with liveness checks, and especially the chat-path readableClause re-filter show real engineering care. But the Postgres↔EdgeQuake dual-write seam is the weakest part of the system and it is fragile in verified, concrete ways. There is no transactional or eventual-consistency contract between the two stores: deletes propagate to neither EdgeQuake vectors nor graph nodes (no delete method exists), ingest is fire-and-forget with no startup reconciliation so crashes strand documents un-indexed, and the shared single-workspace EdgeQuake index leaks across users at the entity table (global merge), the related-docs writer, and every read path except pipeline.ts. The isolation model works only because one specific function re-filters; everything that forgets to re-filter is a hole. Net: the data model tension flagged in project memory is not dormant — it manifests as live cross-user data bugs and unbounded orphaning. Grade C: functional and well-intentioned, but the consistency guarantees a 'second brain' needs (durable indexing, delete propagation, per-user graph isolation) are not actually in place.

crossResults.dimension: Cross-Cutting Tech Debt, Mocks & Architectural Risk
crossResults.summary: SayKnowMind is an ambitious, genuinely well-engineered system in parts (BlockNote CRDT collab, EdgeQuake trait seams, the task worker pool, the Helm chart), but it carries severe cross-cutting architectural debt concentrated in three themes: (1) the "two data models" tension between EdgeQuake's tenant_id/workspace_id schema and the webapp's user_id/organization_id model is no longer theoretical — it is a live cross-user data-corruption bug in the shared global entities table; (2) authentication/authorization is fundamentally under-wired in two of the shipping backends — the entire EdgeQuake HTTP API ships with no auth layer attached and a hardcoded JWT secret, and several web API routes are completely unauthenticated including ones that run shell commands and overwrite global LLM prompts; (3) large swaths of code are mock/dead/duplicated — abandoned orchestrators, a non-functional learning subsystem, a hand-rolled YAML parser that can't parse its own format, three hand-ported SDKs that don't match the server contract, two divergent frontends with contradictory tenancy models, and a CI/deploy pipeline whose images and migration lists are disconnected from what actually runs. I verified the load-bearing claims directly against source.

findings.title: Two-data-models tension is now an active cross-user data-corruption bug (global entities table)
findings.detail: The winning EdgeQuake entities table carries CONSTRAINT entities_unique_name UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name). All webapp rows write tenant_id=NULL/workspace_id=NULL (migration 049 only added document_id/type/confidence, never user_id/organization_id), so NULLS NOT DISTINCT collapses the constraint to 'entity name must be globally unique across the entire installation.' The web insert does ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) DO UPDATE SET document_id=COALESCE(existing,new), so when user B ingests a doc mentioning an entity user A already created, no new row is made — B silently resolves to A's row, keeps A's document_id, and merges B's metadata. Every user shares one entity namespace; entity→document links point at whoever ingested first; per-user knowledge graphs bleed into each other, defeating the app-layer visibility model for the entire entity/graph surface.
findings.evidence: db/init/01-edgequake-init.sql:155 (entities_unique_name UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT); apps/web/lib/ingest/document-store.ts:120-126 (INSERT INTO entities ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) DO UPDATE SET document_id = COALESCE(...)); db/migrations/049_web_graph_schema_compat.sql (adds document_id/type/confidence, no tenant column)
findings.recommendation: Add user_id/organization_id to entities and make uniqueness per-owner (UNIQUE (organization_id, name) or include user_id), or stamp the webapp's org/user UUID into tenant_id/workspace_id on insert so the existing constraint isolates correctly. Backfill existing rows. Until fixed, the entity graph must be treated as untrusted/shared.

findings.title: EdgeQuake HTTP API ships with no authentication layer and a hardcoded JWT secret
findings.detail: build_router() wires only DefaultBodyLimit, request_logging, request_id, TraceLayer, permissive CORS (allow_origin(Any)), and compression. The api_key_auth and tenant_rate_limit middleware exist and are exported but are never .layer()'d onto the router, and no JWT-verification middleware exists at all — every /api/v1 endpoint (documents, query, graph, users, tenants, delete-all) is reachable unauthenticated. Compounding it, AppState::new_postgres constructs auth via AuthConfig::default() instead of from_env(), so JWT_SECRET is ignored and the literal 'change-me-in-production-256-bit-secret-key' is used in the production build. create_user takes the role straight from an unauthenticated request body (admin accepted). Tenant isolation is then keyed entirely on spoofable X-Tenant-ID/X-Workspace-ID/X-User-ID headers. The RBAC service and audit crate are constructed but never invoked anywhere.
findings.evidence: packages/edgequake/crates/edgequake-api/src/server.rs:90-106 (only body-limit/logging/request-id/trace/cors(Any)/compression layered); state/postgres.rs:293 (AuthConfig::default()); edgequake-auth/src/config.rs:51,129 (hardcoded 'change-me-in-production-256-bit-secret-key'); handlers/auth/user_management.rs:43-46,95-96 (role from request body, no auth extractor)
findings.recommendation: Wire api_key_auth + a JWT-verification middleware onto build_router; switch to AuthConfig::from_env() with a startup assertion that JWT_SECRET is set and >=32 bytes; bind tenant headers to the verified JWT subject; gate handlers through the existing RbacService; wire AuditLogger. If EdgeQuake is meant to sit behind the web app only, enforce network isolation explicitly rather than relying on it implicitly.

findings.title: Unauthenticated web API routes execute shell commands, overwrite global prompts, and create users
findings.detail: Three web routes have no getOrgContext/getUserId/requireAdmin gate (verified by grep). POST /api/settings/prompts overwrites a single global .sayknowmind-prompts.json at process.cwd() that loadPrompts() feeds into chat AND document-processing system prompts for ALL users — anonymous stored prompt injection / jailbreak / defacement. GET/POST /api/desktop/runtime runs execSync for which/docker/ollama/git, tar -xzf, rm -rf, pnpm build, downloads and extracts a Node tarball, and spawns a detached server — intended for Tauri localhost but shipped with no NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_MODE/desktop env guard. GET/POST /api/auth/test leaks BETTER_AUTH_URL/TRUSTED_ORIGINS and calls signUpEmail() creating a real persisted user on every hit ('clean up' comment deletes nothing).
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/api/settings/prompts/route.ts:7,220 (writeFileSync to process.cwd() file, no auth); apps/web/app/api/desktop/runtime/route.ts:3,29-153 (execSync which/docker/tar/serverJs, no auth); apps/web/app/api/auth/test/route.ts:7,18,25 (env leak, signUpEmail, no-op cleanup comment)
findings.recommendation: Delete /api/auth/test outright. Gate /api/settings/prompts behind requireAdmin and store prompts per-org in the DB, not a cwd file. Hard-guard /api/desktop/runtime to desktop builds only (return 404 unless an explicit desktop env flag is set) and add auth.

findings.title: EdgeQuake vector-search tenant filter is fail-OPEN — cross-tenant leak
findings.detail: matches_tenant_filter returns true whenever a vector's metadata lacks tenant_id/workspace_id keys (verified: the function short-circuits to true when both requested ids are None, and within the per-key checks only rejects on a PRESENT-but-mismatched key). Any vector stored without those metadata keys is visible to every tenant's query. This contradicts the graph-node path which is fail-CLOSED, and the graph-edge path which is fail-open — three different isolation policies in one engine. On the shared default vector table the SQL passes no tenant predicate, so cross-tenant rows are fetched first and only weakly filtered after, causing both leakage and recall loss.
findings.evidence: packages/edgequake/crates/edgequake-query/src/sota_engine/prompt.rs:16-37 (returns true on missing keys; only rejects present-mismatch); graph node fail-closed at adapters/postgres/graph/mod.rs:1273-1291 vs edge fail-open mod.rs:1396-1402
findings.recommendation: Make the vector filter fail-CLOSED: a row missing tenant_id/workspace_id metadata must NOT match a tenant-scoped query. Push the tenant predicate into the SQL WHERE (metadata @> filter) so cross-tenant rows are never fetched. Unify all three isolation paths to one fail-closed policy.

findings.title: Cypher injection via $$ dollar-quote breakout from LLM-extracted entity content
findings.detail: All Cypher is embedded into outer SQL as cypher('graph', $$ <cypher> $$). escape_cypher_string escapes quotes/backslashes/newlines but NOT the $$ dollar-quote terminator, and property-map KEYS are interpolated raw (format!("{}: {}", k, value_str)). Entity names, node ids, and property keys/values all originate from LLM extraction over untrusted user documents, so an adversarial document containing $$ (or a crafted key) terminates the literal and injects arbitrary SQL into the outer statement.
findings.evidence: packages/edgequake/crates/edgequake-storage/src/adapters/postgres/graph/helpers.rs:63-66,204-211 (dollar-quote wrap + escape that misses $$); helpers.rs:229-242,265-272 (raw key interpolation)
findings.recommendation: Use sqlx parameter binding for the Cypher body / AGE parameters instead of string interpolation, or at minimum reject/escape $tag$ sequences and validate property keys against a strict identifier allowlist. Treat all LLM-extracted strings as hostile.

findings.title: RLS is enabled+FORCED but completely inert across both Postgres-touching backends — decorative isolation
findings.detail: 01-edgequake-init.sql ENABLEs and FORCEs RLS with current_tenant_id() policies, but (a) the app connects as the postgres superuser which bypasses RLS, (b) no code ever calls set_tenant_context/set_config to populate the GUCs, and (c) every policy is 'tenant_id IS NULL OR tenant_id = current_tenant_id()' while all webapp rows have tenant_id NULL — so even a non-superuser would match all rows. Where code does try to set session context (edgequake-storage conversation.rs set_context, RlsContext) it runs set_config on the pool, then the business query grabs a DIFFERENT pooled connection with no context — the project's own RLS test file documents this exact pitfall, and all 7 RLS tests are #[ignore]. Isolation rests 100% on app-layer helpers (lib/visibility.ts), so a single missed filter = full cross-user exposure with no DB backstop.
findings.evidence: db/init/01-edgequake-init.sql:801-836 (ENABLE+FORCE, IS NULL escape clause); docker-compose.yml:61 (superuser conn); packages/edgequake/.../postgres/conversation.rs:57-74 (set_config on pool, false=session) and rls.rs:123-173; e2e_postgres_rls.rs all #[ignore]
findings.recommendation: Either delete the RLS scaffolding (it gives false confidence) or make it real: connect as a non-superuser role, pin a dedicated connection per request with set_config(...true) inside a transaction, and add a user_id/organization_id dimension to the policies. Keep the #[ignore]d RLS tests running in CI against a real Postgres.

findings.title: Mock/dead code presented as features: abandoned orchestrators, non-functional learning subsystem, broken YAML parser
findings.detail: Verified zero callers for agents/orchestrator.ts (executeAgenticQuery) and agents/langgraph.ts (LangGraphOrchestrator), and zvec/engine.ts (LSH engine, tests-only). The ai-server pattern-learning subsystem is non-functional: getRecentSpansForLearning reads metrics:global.modelDistribution which is never written anywhere, so it always returns [] (learnPatterns always reports 0 learned), and when it 'works' it fabricates all-success spans; shouldEnableFeatures fires checkGlobalLearningPatterns().then() but returns synchronously before the promise resolves (dead floating-promise logic). SemanticMemoryService isn't semantic — it gates on an OPENROUTER_API_KEY it then ignores and returns a 128-dim hash-bucket bag-of-words vector. ultrarag's parseSimpleYaml builds arrays of scalars only and cannot represent the list-of-maps that `steps:` requires, so every real YAML pipeline fails validation — the YAML engine is dead, only JSON bodies work.
findings.evidence: grep: executeAgenticQuery/LangGraphOrchestrator/zvec — zero callers in app/lib/components; apps/ai-server/src/intelligence/algorithm.service.ts:230-260,393-412; apps/ai-server/src/memory/semantic-memory.service.ts:51,68-104; apps/web/lib/ultrarag/parser.ts:66-82 vs validator.ts:38-58
findings.recommendation: Delete the abandoned orchestrators and zvec, or move them behind an explicit experimental flag with a README note. Either fix the learning pipeline (write modelDistribution, await the promise) or remove it — shipping a learning system that silently learns from fabricated all-success data is worse than none. Replace parseSimpleYaml with a real YAML lib (js-yaml) or drop the YAML framing.

findings.title: Streaming chat does not fall back on transient 5xx; quota burned before validation; client-disconnect leaks paid tokens
findings.detail: routeChat only sets shouldFallback for FALLBACK_CODES {400,402,429}; a cloud provider 500/502/503 throws 'All cloud providers failed' to the user even though the AI-server cascade is healthy — diverging from the non-streaming twin callAiCloudFirst which always falls back. extractHttpStatus greps the first 4xx/5xx-looking number anywhere in the error string, so a status inside a provider body can flip the decision. Separately, /api/chat increments the daily usage quota before validating the message is non-empty, and runPipeline is launched un-awaited inside ReadableStream.start without request.signal, so on client disconnect the LLM keeps consuming paid tokens.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/agents/chat-router.ts:19,22-24,156 (FALLBACK_CODES, regex status); apps/web/lib/agents/cloud-ai.ts:236-248 (always falls back); apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts:37 vs 57 (increment before validate), :103-116 (un-awaited, no signal)
findings.recommendation: Add 5xx to the fallback set and pass an explicit numeric status from the provider layer rather than regex-scraping. Validate the message before incrementing quota. Thread request.signal into runPipeline and abort the upstream LLM stream on disconnect; add .catch on the un-awaited pipeline.

findings.title: Ingest jobs are orphaned on restart; retries are in-memory only (no durable re-drive)
findings.detail: createJob fires processJobById as fire-and-forget; the concurrency semaphore and exponential-backoff retries are pure in-process state (setTimeout). A Node restart (deploy/crash/serverless teardown) while a job is 'processing' or waiting on a retry leaves the ingestion_jobs row stuck forever — there is no startup reconciliation of stale pending/processing rows. The same anti-pattern exists in EdgeQuake's worker (tokio::spawn+sleep retries lost on restart, startup recovery only re-enqueues Pending, not scheduled retries). Note EdgeQuake's binary DOES have a startup orphan-recovery pass; the web ingest path does not.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/ingest/job-queue.ts:63-66,131-141,481-495 (fire-and-forget, in-mem semaphore, setTimeout retry); packages/edgequake/crates/edgequake-tasks/src/worker.rs:309-321
findings.recommendation: Add a startup sweeper that resets stale 'processing'/scheduled rows to 'pending' and re-drives them, or move to a durable queue (the ingestion_jobs table already exists — poll it). Persist retry schedule in the DB so it survives restarts.

findings.title: Web-vs-dashboard duplication: two frontends with contradictory tenancy models, dashboard has no auth gate
findings.detail: apps/dashboard is vendored 'EdgeQuake WebUI' (v0.5.4, ~79k LOC) sharing ZERO code with apps/web, carrying three committed lockfiles (bun.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml) and absent from any workspace. Its entire model IS the abandoned EdgeQuake tenancy (project memory says don't revive it): TenantGuard lets users createTenant/createWorkspace and every request carries client-set X-Tenant-ID/X-Workspace-ID/X-User-ID headers with an anonymous Math.random() UUID fallback. There is no middleware.ts and no auth redirect — login has an always-on handleSkipLogin() routing straight to /graph (the documented NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_DEMO_MODE flag is never read). It is shipped as a deployed Docker image, so two products with contradictory tenancy assumptions hit the same data, and a cross-origin sayknowmind.ts bridge calls the web app's destructive /api/admin/* (deleteUser) with credentials:'include'.
findings.evidence: apps/dashboard/src/lib/api/client.ts:121-186 (client-asserted headers, UUID fallback); src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx:41-43 (unconditional skip-login); src/components/layout/tenant-guard.tsx:15; src/lib/api/sayknowmind.ts:1-46; three committed lockfiles
findings.recommendation: Decide ownership: either retire dashboard or scope it to an internal EdgeQuake admin tool behind real auth and network isolation, never customer-facing. Add middleware auth gating, gate skip-login behind the demo flag, delete two of the three lockfiles, and remove the cross-origin admin bridge in favor of a properly authenticated server route.

findings.title: SDK trio (sdk-sayknowmind/go/python) does not match the live server contract; version skew across packages
findings.detail: All three hand-ported SDKs expose a non-streaming chat() that POSTs /api/chat and calls response.json() for an invented ChatResponse {messageId, answer, citations}, but /api/chat ALWAYS returns text/event-stream (verified 'Always stream' + ReadableStream) — json() on an SSE body throws and messageId is never produced. createCategory reads data['id'] but the server returns {categoryId, path:[]} (Python raises KeyError, Go fails to unmarshal an array into a string field). Search filters are spread flat but the server reads body.filters (silently dropped). Auth is Bearer but the web routes authenticate via session cookie. Version skew is broad: web 0.1.0, dashboard 0.5.4, desktop 0.1.5, edgequake-sdk 0.4.0, mcp-server 0.2.0 (McpServer self-reports 0.1.0) — and mcp-server declares 'edgequake-sdk':'^0.1.0' while the in-repo package is 0.4.0, with no pnpm-workspace.yaml to resolve it locally.
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts:102-120 (Always stream / SSE) vs packages/sdk-sayknowmind/src/client.ts:49,99-100 (response.json ChatResponse); apps/web/app/api/categories/route.ts (returns categoryId/path[]) vs sdk-python client.py:194; packages/mcp-server/package.json:58 ('edgequake-sdk':'^0.1.0') vs packages/sdk/package.json (0.4.0); no pnpm-workspace.yaml present
findings.recommendation: Generate the SDKs from a single OpenAPI/schema source instead of hand-porting, and contract-test them against the real routes. Add the SDK packages to the workspace and fix the mcp-server dependency range. Reconcile version strings (at least McpServer vs /health vs package.json).

findings.title: CI/deploy incoherence: orphaned registry images, stale migration lists, error-swallowing migrations
findings.detail: The compose actually run on the host uses build: for web/ai-server/dashboard/mcp/edgequake/ocr/postgres and image: only for redis/ollama/searxng/ipfs — so docker compose pull fetches nothing for the app services, while GitLab CI builds only web and GitHub CI builds web/ai-server/dashboard/mcp to ghcr; relay-server, edgequake, ocr and the custom postgres are built by NEITHER. The GitHub deploy.yml generates a docker-compose.prod.yml in the runner that is never transferred to the host (the SSH step runs whatever file already lives at /opt/sayknowmind) and the generated file references an undefined postgres service. Migration drift is severe: production-deploy.sh and .gitlab-ci.yml apply a hardcoded list ending at 050, but the tree is at 061 — the entire org/team/collab/versions feature set (051-061) is never applied on the SSH deploy paths; GitHub deploy runs psql ... || true swallowing every migration failure with no schema_migrations tracking. Rust engine and relay-server have zero CI build/test.
findings.evidence: docker-compose.yml (build: app services, image: only base); .github/workflows/deploy.yml:41-90 (generated compose never shipped, psql || true); scripts/production-deploy.sh:187 (list ends at 050) vs db/migrations/061_add_document_versions.sql
findings.recommendation: Pick ONE deploy mechanism and one migration runner (the schema_migrations-tracking migrate.sh glob) and use it everywhere — delete the hardcoded lists and the unused generated compose. Build all runtime services in CI to the registry the deploy actually pulls, or commit to build-on-host and drop the registry pipeline. Add cargo build/clippy/test for edgequake and a build/test job for relay-server. Stop swallowing migration errors.

findings.title: Encrypted relay/offline-sync silently degrades to base64; collab authorized only at connect
findings.detail: sync-service encrypts every pushed payload via encryptForUser and the system is marketed as encrypted offline-sync, but lib/encryption has a base64 dev fallback and a 'dev-only-not-for-production' fallback secret — if RELAY/keys are unset, payloads traverse the relay base64-encoded, not encrypted, with no guard or warning at the sync layer. The 'E2E, relay never decrypts' guarantee is also overstated in the shared-server edition where the server holds the key (server-side-at-rest, not E2E). Hocuspocus collab runs onAuthenticate once at handshake with no jti/replay protection, so revoking a share doesn't drop a connected writer and a leaked 5-min token is reusable until expiry. A single RELAY_SHARED_SECRET signs both audiences with no rotation/revocation.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/relay/sync-service.ts:111-114; apps/web/lib/encryption.ts:74-93,199-204 (base64 + dev fallback secret); packages/relay-server/src/collab/hocuspocus.ts:24-40
findings.recommendation: Refuse to push (or loudly warn) when real encryption keys are absent rather than silently base64-encoding. Stop marketing shared-server sync as E2E. Add periodic re-authorization or short-lived token refresh for long-lived collab connections, and support key id/rotation on the relay secret.

findings.title: MCP keys plaintext + open-admin fallback; mindmap/sheet collab are last-write-wins, not CRDT
findings.detail: user_mcp_keys.api_key is stored and compared as plaintext via SELECT ... WHERE api_key=$1 (non-constant-time, no expiry, one key per user, CREATE TABLE on the request hot path) — a DB read leak exposes live credentials, shared by both the web app and mcp-server. The mcp-server grants isAdmin:true with NO token when both MCP_API_KEY and DATABASE_URL are unset (open-mode default-on, advertised by /health) — a public deploy that forgets a var gives every caller admin access to the shared EdgeQuake index. Separately, of the three web collaboration fidelities only BlockNote notes are a true Yjs CRDT; mindmaps stringify the ENTIRE map into one Y.Map key (whoever saves last wins, the 1500ms defer only reduces loss) and the mindmap provider never refreshes its JWT (silent sync death on expiry), while Univer sheets use an unbounded, never-pruned op-log.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/ingest/session-helper.ts:11-24 (plaintext equality); packages/mcp-server/src/index.ts:48,79-80 (open-admin fallback); apps/web/components/docs/mindmap-editor.tsx:286,292-334 (whole-blob LWW, static token); office-tab.tsx:240-288 (unbounded op-log)
findings.recommendation: Hash MCP keys (store hash, compare constant-time), add expiry/rotation, and move table creation to a migration. Make MCP open-mode require an explicit opt-in flag, never a default fallback. Give the mindmap provider the same token-refresh/backoff as notes, and either move mindmaps to a real CRDT or document the LWW limitation; add op-log compaction for sheets.

findings.title: Desktop: privileged custom commands reachable from remote webview; ocp_install runs third-party code
findings.detail: Tauri capabilities only gate core/plugin commands — app-defined #[tauri::command]s are NOT ACL-gated. In the lite build (the only variant CI ships, pointed at the cloud origin), any XSS in the cloud app can invoke ocp_install, exec_codex_login, chat_via_codex, provision_ocp_key, etc., and the CSP is permissive (unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval). ocp_install hardcodes git clone of an unpinned personal repo (github.com/dtzp555-max/ocp.git) then runs npm install + node setup.mjs + launchctl — a supply-chain takeover triggerable by remote JS. The auto-updater has live endpoints but an empty pubkey while CI signs artifacts (broken update trust chain), generate_secret() falls back to a constant 'fallback-desktop-secret', and the mobile app is a non-compiling skeleton whose release CI fails at cap sync.
findings.evidence: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:1649-1671 (commands registered, no ACL), 1058-1074 (hardcoded unpinned clone); capabilities/remote.json:4-15; tauri.conf.json:15,47-53 (CSP, empty updater pubkey)
findings.recommendation: Do not expose privileged commands to a remote-origin webview — gate them behind an origin check / only register them in full (local) builds, tighten CSP, and pin ocp to a commit hash with integrity verification (ideally bundle it rather than cloning). Set a real updater pubkey or disable the updater. Generate a real random desktop secret. Mark mobile clearly as non-functional and skip its release CI.

crossResults.overall_assessment: This is a serious, ambitious project with real engineering depth in spots — the BlockNote Yjs collaboration, EdgeQuake's trait-based storage/provider seams, the Tauri PATH/Node discovery handling, the task worker pool, and the Helm chart are all genuinely well done. But as a consolidated risk inventory it grades poorly because the cross-cutting fundamentals are unsound for anything beyond single-user/local-first use. Three structural problems dominate: (1) the "two data models" conflict is no longer documentation debt — it is a live cross-user data-corruption bug in the global entities table, verified at db/init/01-edgequake-init.sql:155 + document-store.ts:120; (2) authentication is under-wired in two shipping backends — EdgeQuake's entire HTTP API has no auth layer attached and uses a hardcoded JWT secret (server.rs:90 + postgres.rs:293), and several web routes (settings/prompts, desktop/runtime, auth/test) are fully unauthenticated despite running shell commands and overwriting global state; and (3) a large fraction of the codebase is mock/dead/duplicated weight presented as features — verified-zero-caller orchestrators and zvec, a learning subsystem that reads a metric never written (always returns empty), a YAML parser that can't parse its own format, three SDKs that don't match the SSE-only chat contract, two frontends with contradictory tenancy models, and a CI/deploy pipeline whose registry images and migration lists (frozen at 050 vs a tree at 061) are disconnected from what actually runs. The top architectural risks, ranked by blast radius: cross-tenant data leakage (entities table + EdgeQuake fail-open vector filter + no-auth API + inert RLS) > unauthenticated RCE/abuse surfaces (web shell route, desktop remote-command exposure, Cypher injection) > durability/correctness gaps (orphaned ingest jobs, LWW mindmap collab, base64 'encryption' fallback) > maintainability debt (duplication, version skew, broken CI/deploy coherence). The path to a passing grade is narrow but clear: pick a single tenancy model and enforce it at the data layer, wire the auth middleware that already exists, delete the dead/mock subsystems, and unify the deploy/migration pipeline.

crossResults.summary: SayKnowMind's documentation is stratified by age and honesty. The PRD ("SayknowMind (PRD)", v1.0, 2026-03-01) is pure aspirational fiction describing a stack the repo never built (Qdrant, Neo4j, ZeroClaw Gateway v0.1.7, LangGraph, crawl4ai/LlamaParse, MIT license) and contradicts the actual license. README.md (v0.1.0-alpha) is months stale: it markets ZeroClaw :8081 as a shipping service in four places, claims Sigma.js graph viz and next-intl/2-locale i18n that don't match code, undercounts Docker services (9 vs 12), and uses wrong MCP tool names and a non-working Bearer-auth SDK contract. AGENTS.md (2026-06-16) is by far the freshest and mostly accurate, and correctly flags ZeroClaw and the Lit/Arweave/mobile stubs — but still carries a handful of load-bearing false claims (Sigma.js, a phantom zh-TW locale, "RLS-backed" org-context, and dead orchestrator/ultrarag/zvec code listed as "Real Implementations — do NOT replace"). INSTALL.md is the most accurate on service topology yet still presents ZeroClaw as a real in-repo component with a description that conflicts with README and PRD. Meanwhile the product has outgrown its docs: shipped collaborative editors, version history, teams/orgs, SaaS auth, Telegram/OCP-Codex integrations appear only in weekly logs and AGENTS, while README's roadmap still lists already-built features ("Multi-user workspace support", "Additional languages") as future v0.2.0 work.

findings.title: PRD describes an entirely fictional stack and the wrong license — zero coherence with the codebase
findings.detail: "SayknowMind (PRD)" (v1.0, 2026-03-01) specifies a stack that was never built: ZeroClaw Gateway v0.1.7 + LangGraph Agent Runtime, Qdrant 1.12+ for vectors, Neo4j 5.26+ for graph, crawl4ai + LlamaParse + Unstructured for ingestion, bge-m3/voyage embeddings, Vercel AI SDK (PRD lines ~80-130). The actual system is EdgeQuake (Rust) over PostgreSQL+pgvector+Apache AGE, a NestJS AI server with a regex-first pipeline (no LangGraph in the hot path), and Mozilla Readability/Cheerio fetching. The PRD also asserts "오픈소스 여부: 전체 공개 (MIT License)" and "License: MIT" in 5 places, but LICENSE is Apache License 2.0 and every other doc says Apache-2.0. An outside reader treating the PRD as authoritative would be misled on the database, agent runtime, ingestion stack, and the open-source license itself.
findings.evidence: SayknowMind (PRD) lines 5,153,250,366,385 ("MIT License"); PRD §5-6 (Qdrant/Neo4j/ZeroClaw/LangGraph/crawl4ai); LICENSE:1-3 (Apache License Version 2.0); README.md:124 (Apache 2.0)
findings.recommendation: Mark the PRD as a historical/archived vision document with a banner at the top ("Superseded — see AGENTS.md for current architecture"), or rewrite §5-6 to the real stack. At minimum fix the MIT-vs-Apache license contradiction immediately, since it is legally load-bearing.

findings.title: README markets ZeroClaw :8081 as a shipping service in four sections, but it does not exist in the repo or compose
findings.detail: README.md presents ZeroClaw as a live, deployed component in the architecture diagram ("ZeroClaw :8081 Rust Agent Runtime", line 89-90), the tech-stack table ("Agent Runtime | ZeroClaw (Rust), LangGraph Orchestrator", line 113), the Access Points table ("ZeroClaw | http://localhost:8081", line 283), and the Docker Services table ("zeroclaw | Rust build | 8081", line 524). docker-compose.yml has no zeroclaw service at all (12 services: postgres, redis, edgequake, ocr-server, ai-server, web, dashboard, ollama, searxng, mcp-server, relay-server, ipfs), and there is no packages/zeroclaw/. AGENTS.md:39 correctly states ZeroClaw "ships as an external binary — there is no packages/zeroclaw/". INSTALL.md:12 also lists it but describes it differently ("Web crawler and agent runtime") than README ("Agent Runtime") and the PRD ("Gateway"/"Ingestion Agent"). Three docs describe a non-existent in-repo service three incompatible ways.
findings.evidence: README.md:89-90,113,283,524; docker-compose.yml (grep zeroclaw → none; services at lines 5,41,54,81,90,124,183,203,215,228,263,289); AGENTS.md:39,51; INSTALL.md:12
findings.recommendation: Either remove ZeroClaw from README's diagram/tables/access-points or add the same external-binary caveat AGENTS.md uses. Pick one canonical one-line description of what ZeroClaw is (or isn't) and reuse it across README/INSTALL/PRD.

findings.title: AGENTS.md and README claim Sigma.js graph viz, but the knowledge graph uses react-force-graph-2d; sigma/graphology are dead dependencies
findings.detail: AGENTS.md:68 lists "Graph viz: Sigma.js + graphology (knowledge graph)" and README.md:122,219 say "Graph Viz | Sigma.js (knowledge graph)" and "Interactive Sigma.js visualization". In reality there are zero source imports of sigma/@react-sigma/graphology anywhere in apps/web/{app,components,lib} — the knowledge graph renders via react-force-graph-2d (components/knowledge/graph-canvas.tsx), and the category graph uses @xyflow/React Flow. sigma ^3.0.2, @react-sigma/core ^5.0.6, graphology ^0.26.0 and graphology-layout-forceatlas2 are declared in package.json but unused, so both docs document a library that ships as install/supply-chain weight but is never executed.
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:68; README.md:122,219; apps/web/package.json:32,47,48,59 (sigma/graphology declared); grep for sigma/graphology imports in app/components/lib → no matches
findings.recommendation: Update both docs to say react-force-graph-2d (knowledge graph) + @xyflow/React Flow (category graph), and remove the unused sigma/@react-sigma/graphology packages from apps/web/package.json.

findings.title: i18n is misdescribed in both directions: README undercounts, AGENTS invents a zh-TW locale that doesn't exist
findings.detail: AGENTS.md:69 claims i18n covers "ko / en / zh-CN / zh-TW / ja" and README.md:121 claims "Korean, English (next-intl)". Neither matches the code. apps/web/messages/ contains exactly four files — en.json, ja.json, ko.json, zh.json — so there is no zh-TW (Traditional Chinese) bundle despite README.md:15 linking a 繁體中文 intro and AGENTS claiming it. There is also no next-intl: translations run through a hand-rolled zustand store in lib/i18n.ts, and next-intl is not even a dependency. README simultaneously undersells (says only ko/en) while AGENTS oversells (claims 5 incl. a phantom zh-TW).
findings.evidence: apps/web/messages/ → en.json, ja.json, ko.json, zh.json only; apps/web/lib/i18n.ts (custom store); AGENTS.md:69; README.md:121,15; grep next-intl in package.json → not present
findings.recommendation: State the real situation in both docs: 4 locales (en/ko/zh-Hans/ja) via a custom lib/i18n.ts (not next-intl), and either add a real zh-TW bundle or stop advertising 繁體中文 in the README language links.

findings.title: AGENTS.md lists dead/test-only modules under "Real Implementations — do NOT replace with mocks"
findings.detail: AGENTS.md:130-140 places lib/agents/{orchestrator,langgraph}.ts, lib/ultrarag/{executor,parser,validator}.ts, and lib/zvec/engine.ts in the "Real Implementations ✅ — do NOT replace with mocks" table. But orchestrator.ts/langgraph.ts have zero callers (abandoned orchestrators), the ultrarag YAML path is effectively dead (parser.ts's parseSimpleYaml cannot represent the list-of-maps that `steps:` requires, so every real YAML pipeline fails validation), and zvec/engine.ts is referenced only by tests. Telling future agents these are load-bearing real implementations is the opposite of the truth and risks someone building on top of code that never runs in production.
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:130,131,140; apps/web/lib/ultrarag/parser.ts:66-82 (scalar-only array parse) vs validator.ts:38-58 (requires array-of-objects); orchestrator.ts/langgraph.ts have no callers; zvec/engine.ts used only in __tests__
findings.recommendation: Move orchestrator/langgraph/ultrarag/zvec to a clearly-labeled "experimental / not wired" section, or annotate each with its caller status (e.g. "ultrarag: only reachable via /api/pipeline with JSON bodies; YAML path non-functional").

findings.title: AGENTS.md describes org-context as "RLS-backed", but tenant isolation is app-layer only and Postgres RLS is inert
findings.detail: AGENTS.md:126 lists "lib/org-context.ts | Multi-tenant org/workspace context (RLS-backed)". The code resolves the active org from the better-auth session (or first membership for MCP-key auth) and isolation is enforced purely in application SQL via lib/visibility.ts clauses. Per the project's own known context and db/init, RLS policies are ENABLE+FORCE'd but inert (superuser connection, no GUC set_config calls, tenant_id-IS-NULL escape clauses). Calling org-context "RLS-backed" implies a database-level backstop that does not exist, which is exactly the dangerous misconception that leads someone to drop an app-layer visibility filter assuming RLS will catch it.
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:126; apps/web/lib/org-context.ts:55-71 (session/membership resolution, no set_config); known context: RLS inert (superuser conn, no GUCs)
findings.recommendation: Change the description to "Multi-tenant org/workspace context (app-layer enforcement via lib/visibility.ts; Postgres RLS is present but inert)". This single phrase change prevents a whole class of isolation regressions.

findings.title: README's Docker/SDK/MCP sections are wrong: 9-vs-12 services, dotted MCP tool names, and a Bearer-auth SDK contract that 401s
findings.detail: Three concrete README inaccuracies that break copy-paste usage: (1) README.md:123,197,512-525 claim a "9-service" Docker stack and a table that omits redis, ocr-server, relay-server, and ipfs while listing the non-existent zeroclaw — compose actually defines 12 services. (2) README.md:486-491 documents MCP tools as dotted names (sayknowmind.search, sayknowmind.ingest, sayknowmind.document.get) and "6 tool groups", but the registered tool names are underscored (sayknowmind_search, sayknowmind_ingest, sayknowmind_document_get, ...) with far more than six. (3) README.md:349,409-467 instruct SDK users to authenticate the web API with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, but /api/* routes authenticate via better-auth session cookie / sk-mcp-* keys (getOrgContext/getUserIdFromRequest), so plain Bearer-token SDK calls will 401 — and the documented chat() JSON contract can't consume the SSE-only /api/chat.
findings.evidence: README.md:123,197,512-525 vs docker-compose.yml (12 services); README.md:486-491 vs packages/mcp-server/src/tools/sayknowmind.ts ("sayknowmind_search" etc.); README.md:349 vs apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts (session auth + always-SSE)
findings.recommendation: Regenerate the Docker Services table from docker-compose.yml, fix MCP tool names to the underscored registrations, and correct the auth/SDK section to reflect session/MCP-key auth and the SSE chat contract (or mark the SDKs as not-yet-usable against the deployed web app).

findings.title: Implementation has outgrown the docs: shipped features appear only in weekly logs while README's roadmap lists them as future work
findings.detail: Major shipped capabilities — multi-tab collaborative editors (BlockNote notes, Univer sheets, mind-elixir mindmaps), real-time Yjs/Hocuspocus collab with presence, document version history, teams/orgs (better-auth organization plugin), the SaaS auth edition, and Telegram/OCP-Codex integrations — are documented only in the Korean/Chinese weekly logs, Planning DEV/, and AGENTS.md, not in README.
