Worse, README's Roadmap (lines 591-608) still lists already-built items as future: v0.2.0 "Multi-user workspace support" (teams shipped via migrations 053-058) and "Additional languages (Japanese, Chinese)" (ja.json/zh.json already exist). The README's whole framing (v0.1.0-alpha, ~63% complete) badly lags the production-deployed reality AGENTS.md describes.
findings.evidence: README.md:591-608 (roadmap lists shipped features as future); 업무일지-2026-06-08_06-13.md §2 (collab editors/version history shipped to prod); AGENTS.md:9 ("deployed and running in production"); db/migrations 053-058 (orgs/teams); apps/web/messages/ja.json,zh.json
findings.recommendation: Refresh README's Features/Roadmap/Progress sections from AGENTS.md + weekly logs, and remove already-shipped items from the v0.2.0 roadmap. Consider making AGENTS.md the single source of truth and reducing README to a thin pointer to avoid re-drift.

findings.title: Version strings are inconsistent across the repo with no single source of truth
findings.detail: The product version is reported differently everywhere: README.md:2 badge says v0.1.0-alpha; apps/web/package.json:3 is 0.1.0; apps/desktop/package.json:3 is 0.1.5; apps/dashboard is v0.5.4 (vendored EdgeQuake WebUI); mcp-server reports 0.1.0 (McpServer) vs 0.2.0 (/health). AGENTS.md:9 hedges with "Currently v0.1.0-alpha but deployed and running in production". There is no authoritative version, so any consumer reading a badge, a package.json, or a /health endpoint gets a different answer.
findings.evidence: README.md:2; apps/web/package.json:3 (0.1.0); apps/desktop/package.json:3 (0.1.5); AGENTS.md:9; mcp-server /health vs server.ts version drift (from subsystem map)
findings.recommendation: Document that subpackages are independently versioned (web/desktop/dashboard differ by design) and pick one "platform version" for the README badge, or drop the badge. Fix the mcp-server 0.1.0-vs-0.2.0 internal drift regardless.

crossResults.overall_assessment: Documentation health is C: honest and current in the places that matter most for active development (AGENTS.md and the weekly logs accurately capture the production-deployed collab/teams/versioning reality and correctly flag the Lit base64 / Arweave-throws / skeletal-mobile stubs), but the public-facing entry points — the PRD and README — are stale to the point of being misleading. The PRD is an abandoned vision doc describing a non-existent stack (Qdrant/Neo4j/ZeroClaw/LangGraph) and the wrong license (MIT vs Apache-2.0); the README still sells ZeroClaw :8081, Sigma.js, next-intl, a 9-service stack, dotted MCP tool names, and a Bearer-auth SDK that 401s. The most dangerous items are not the obvious staleness but the small, confident, load-bearing errors in the otherwise-trusted AGENTS.md: calling dead orchestrator/ultrarag/zvec code \"Real Implementations — do NOT replace,\" labeling org-context \"RLS-backed\" when isolation is app-layer-only, and asserting a zh-TW locale that doesn't exist. Highest-leverage fixes: (1) fix the MIT/Apache license contradiction, (2) correct the four AGENTS.md false claims, and (3) either archive the PRD with a superseded banner and regenerate README's tables from docker-compose.yml + the real tool registrations, or demote README to a pointer at AGENTS.md to stop the re-drift.

crossResults.summary: Testing maturity is severely uneven and CI gating is the dominant weakness. apps/web has a genuinely strong hermetic property-test suite (37 files / 271 cases / 24 use fast-check, isolation logic exercised against an embedded PGlite engine) and is the ONLY package whose tests actually run in CI. Every other subsystem either has tests that CI never executes (ai-server Jest, mcp-server Vitest, dashboard Vitest+Playwright are build-only) or has no CI at all (packages/edgequake = 94 Rust test files across 9 crates, zero cargo build/clippy/test in any workflow; relay-server has zero tests). The highest-value paths — cross-tenant isolation, auth, RLS, SDK wire contracts — are exactly the ones that are skipped, ignored, or assert the broken behavior as correct. Real effective coverage of the security boundaries that matter in production is far lower than the raw test-file count suggests.

findings.title: CI gates only apps/web; edgequake (the security-critical Rust core) and relay-server have zero CI
findings.detail: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs lint+test+build ONLY for apps/web (lines 15-44). build-ai-server and build-mcp-server run `npm ci && npm run build` (no test/lint), and build-dashboard runs `pnpm build` only (lines 47-83) — despite all three having working test scripts (apps/ai-server/package.json:14 `jest`, packages/mcp-server/package.json:28 `vitest run`, apps/dashboard/package.json:13-15 vitest+playwright). packages/edgequake — 9 crates, 94 test files including e2e_tenant_isolation.rs and e2e_workspace_vector_isolation.rs — is referenced in NO workflow (grep cargo/rust over .github/workflows + .gitlab-ci.yml returns only comment noise). packages/relay-server has only a `lint: tsc --noEmit` script and zero *.test.ts files. So the fail-open vector tenant filter, header-spoofable tenant isolation, unwired auth middleware, and the relay's HMAC/encryption code all ship with no automated gate.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:15-44 (web full), :47-67 (ai-server/mcp build-only), :70-83 (dashboard build-only); packages/relay-server/package.json:11 (only lint); 94 files under packages/edgequake/**/tests/*.rs with no cargo step in any workflow
findings.recommendation: Add a Rust CI job: `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` + `cargo test --workspace` (with a postgres+AGE service for the integration tier) for packages/edgequake. Wire the existing `jest`/`vitest` scripts into build-ai-server, build-mcp-server, build-dashboard (run them, don't just build). Add at least smoke tests + lint gating for relay-server. Make the docker-images job `needs:` the test jobs so unverified images can't be pushed.

findings.title: The most security-critical web test (real-schema tenant isolation) auto-skips in CI
findings.detail: Tenant isolation is app-layer-only via lib/visibility.ts, so its tests are the only backstop. p48-visibility-isolation.test.ts runs the clauses against an embedded PGlite engine but with a HAND-BUILT schema (CREATE TABLE documents/categories/resource_shares at lines 63-81) that does NOT reflect the colliding production shape (EdgeQuake `documents` with NOT NULL content/status CHECK/tenant_id, the global `entities` UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT constraint, bolted-on columns from migrations 043/049). p54-visibility-real-schema.test.ts is the one that clones the live schema — but it explicitly `Skips automatically when DATABASE_URL is unset` (header comment) and the CI lint-test-build job has NO postgres service (sed of ci.yml:14-46 shows 0 service blocks). So in CI p54 always skips, and isolation is only ever validated against an idealized schema that papers over the documented 'two data models' collision.
findings.evidence: apps/web/__tests__/p48-visibility-isolation.test.ts:17,60,63-81 (PGlite + hand-built schema); apps/web/__tests__/p54-visibility-real-schema.test.ts:1-26 (skips when DATABASE_URL unset); .github/workflows/ci.yml:14-46 (no `services:`/postgres in the test job)
findings.recommendation: Attach the same postgres:16 service used by migration-check to the lint-test-build job, run db/init + db/migrations against it, and set DATABASE_URL so p54 actually executes. Fail CI if p54 reports 0 assertions (guard against silent skip). Better: seed p48's PGlite from the real db/init+migrations SQL instead of a hand-built schema so it can catch the entity/document collision.

findings.title: edgequake auth tests CODIFY the vulnerabilities as correct behavior
findings.detail: Tests are supposed to be guardrails; here they lock in the defects. e2e_auth.rs `test_create_user_with_role` builds the router via build_router() (which omits the auth layer) and asserts that an unauthenticated POST /users creating an admin SUCCEEDS — i.e. the test asserts unauthenticated privilege escalation is the expected contract. Any future engineer who wires real auth will break this 'passing' test and may revert. Compounding this, the only Postgres-RLS test file has all its cases `#[ignore]`d, so CI (if it existed) would never catch that RLS is inert. Several isolation/multi-tenancy e2e suites (e2e_multi_tenancy.rs, e2e_advanced_retrieval.rs, api_integration_tests.rs, e2e_ollama_integration.rs, e2e_upload_performance.rs) are also `#[ignore]`d.
findings.evidence: packages/edgequake/crates/edgequake-api/tests/e2e_auth.rs:72-99 (test_create_user_with_role asserts success with no auth); packages/edgequake/crates/edgequake-api/tests/e2e_postgres_rls.rs:179,238 (#[ignore] on RLS tests); 6 test files contain #[ignore] (e2e_postgres_rls, e2e_multi_tenancy, e2e_advanced_retrieval, api_integration_tests, e2e_ollama_integration, e2e_upload_performance)
findings.recommendation: Rewrite test_create_user_with_role to assert 401/403 for unauthenticated admin creation (turn it into a regression guard for the real fix). De-ignore e2e_postgres_rls and e2e_tenant_isolation behind a CI postgres+AGE service so the inert-RLS / fail-open-vector defects are caught. Audit all #[ignore] tests and either gate them in a nightly integration job or delete them — silently-ignored security tests are worse than none.

findings.title: SDK wire-contract bugs are untested; the three first-party SDKs have zero tests
findings.detail: packages/sdk-sayknowmind (only client.ts/index.ts/types.ts — no test dir), sdk-go and sdk-python have NO test files at all, yet they ship chat()/createCategory()/search() methods that are broken against the real server (SSE-only /api/chat consumed via response.json(); createCategory reads `id` but server returns `categoryId`; filters dropped). The web-side serialization property tests (p17-sdk-serialization, p35-api-response-json, p36-api-serialization-roundtrip) test JSON roundtripping in isolation — they never assert the SDK shapes against the actual route handler output, so the contract drift is invisible. No contract/integration test exercises an SDK call end-to-end against a running web API.
findings.evidence: packages/sdk-sayknowmind/src/ contains only client.ts/index.ts/types.ts (no tests); find for *_test.go / test_*.py in sdk-go/sdk-python returns nothing; apps/web/__tests__/p17-sdk-serialization.test.ts, p36-api-serialization-roundtrip.test.ts are roundtrip-only
findings.recommendation: Add contract tests that boot the web API (or a typed mock derived from the route handlers) and exercise each SDK method, asserting the real field names (categoryId, SSE event types). Generate the three SDKs from one schema to kill drift, and add a minimal vitest/go test/pytest suite to each so CI can run them. Until then, mark chat()/createCategory() as known-broken in the SDK READMEs.

findings.title: dashboard's 69 Playwright e2e specs are unmaintained, ungated, and flake-prone
findings.detail: apps/dashboard ships 69 Playwright specs + 16 vitest unit tests, but CI runs neither (build-only). Many specs are clearly throwaway debug/audit artifacts committed to the suite (debug-concatenation, dashboard-debug, test-query-fix, comprehensive-ux-audit, ux-audit-verification, audit-fixes-verification, ui-fixes-verification), and the live-query/streaming/multi-tenant-isolation specs require a running EdgeQuake backend + LLM providers, making them inherently network/provider-dependent and flaky. Because nothing gates them, they have rotted: a high-LOC investment (use-ingestion-store.test.ts ~1056 LOC, ingestion-progress-panel.test.ts ~1033 LOC) delivers zero regression protection in the pipeline.
findings.evidence: apps/dashboard/e2e/*.spec.ts (69 files incl. debug-*/test-*/audit-* artifacts); apps/dashboard/src/**/__tests__/*.test.ts (16 vitest); .github/workflows/ci.yml:70-83 (dashboard build-only, no test step)
findings.recommendation: Run the 16 vitest unit tests in CI (fast, hermetic — easy win). Move the Playwright suite into a separate, non-blocking nightly job with a seeded backend, and prune the ~13 debug/audit one-off specs from the committed suite. Add Playwright sharding + retries config to contain flake once gated.

findings.title: ai-server has only 3 thin spec files and they don't run in CI; IDOR/cascade/learning paths untested
findings.detail: apps/ai-server has Jest configured (package.json:14) but only three spec files: memory-keys.helper.spec.ts, algorithm.multilingual.spec.ts, gdpr.service.spec.ts. The service's actual risk surface is untested: the cross-tenant memory IDOR (caller-supplied userId under one shared key), the streaming cascade fallback, the non-functional pattern-learning subsystem (getRecentSpansForLearning reads metrics that are never written), and the floating-promise dead logic in algorithm.service.ts. None of these have tests, and CI runs `npm run build` only, so even the three existing specs never execute in the pipeline. The gdpr.service.spec exists but the GDPR delete genuinely misses org-prefixed keys — meaning the test passes while the behavior is incomplete (it tests the legacy-key path only).
findings.evidence: apps/ai-server/src/**/*.spec.ts = 3 files (memory-keys.helper, algorithm.multilingual, gdpr.service); apps/ai-server/package.json:14 (jest configured); .github/workflows/ci.yml:59-67 (build-ai-server is build-only)
findings.recommendation: Run `jest` in build-ai-server CI. Add tests asserting that GET/DELETE /ai/memory/:userId reject or scope by org (regression for the IDOR), that GDPR delete erases org-prefixed AND span keys, and that streaming cascade falls back on 5xx. These are the documented critical/high risks and currently have no coverage.

findings.title: Migration-check is the only honest behavioral DB gate, but init scripts swallow errors and it tests apply-only, not data behavior
findings.detail: The migration-check job (ci.yml:138-175) is the single genuinely valuable schema gate: it spins a real postgres:16 and runs every db/migrations/*.sql without `|| true` on the migrations loop (line 173). However the init-scripts step (line 164) uses `|| true`, silently swallowing failures in db/init — exactly where the documents/entities/graph_nodes CREATE-TABLE-IF-NOT-EXISTS collisions live. And the job only proves migrations APPLY cleanly on an empty DB in file order; it does not assert the resulting schema is correct (e.g. that the entities table isn't globally-unique-on-name, or that graph_nodes has the columns 013's helper functions reference). Schema-collision and isolation-constraint defects pass this gate.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:158-164 (init run with `|| true`), :167-175 (migrations run without || true — the one honest part); db/init/01-edgequake-init.sql:155 (global entities constraint never asserted by any test)
findings.recommendation: Remove `|| true` from the init step so collisions surface. After applying init+migrations, run assertion SQL (constraint definitions, column existence on graph_nodes, vector dimension) and the p54 isolation suite against that DB in the same job, so the gate validates behavior not just successful application.

findings.title: Strong, hermetic property-test suite in apps/web is the one bright spot — protect and extend it
findings.detail: apps/web's 37 test files / 271 cases (24 leveraging fast-check) are genuinely good: they use an embedded PGlite Postgres for SQL logic (p48), property-based generators for visibility/serialization/sync-conflict, and are hermetic (in-memory, no external services), so flake risk is low and they actually run in CI. Coverage spans isolation logic, ingestion completeness, OAuth state, input-validation security, relay conflict, versions store, file parsers, and sheet-export fidelity. This is a B/B+ posture for the web layer specifically. The gaps are: no integration tests for the 94 app/api route handlers (the unauthenticated auth/test, settings/prompts, desktop/runtime endpoints have no test asserting they should require auth), and the real-schema isolation test skips in CI.
findings.evidence: apps/web/__tests__/ = 37 files, 271 `it/test` cases, 24 files import fast-check; PGlite-backed p48; hermetic (no DATABASE_URL needed except p54)
findings.recommendation: Treat this suite as the template for the rest of the monorepo. Add route-handler integration tests for the unauthenticated-endpoint findings (assert 401 on /api/auth/test POST, /api/settings/prompts POST, /api/desktop/runtime) so the security regressions are caught. Keep the suite hermetic to preserve its low flake rate.

crossResults.overall_assessment: Overall grade C. The raw numbers look healthy (270+ web cases, 94 Rust test files, 69 dashboard e2e specs), but effective, CI-enforced coverage of the things that actually protect users is thin. apps/web earns a B/B+ on its own — hermetic PGlite + fast-check property tests that genuinely exercise the app-layer isolation logic and run on every push. Everything else drags the grade down hard: CI gates nothing but apps/web, so ai-server (D), mcp-server (C), dashboard (C), and especially the edgequake Rust core (D/F — zero CI on a 9-crate security-critical engine) ship unverified. The deepest problem isn't missing tests, it's mis-aimed ones: the highest-value paths (cross-tenant isolation, auth, RLS, SDK contracts) are skipped (p54 auto-skips with no DATABASE_URL in CI), ignored (all 7 edgequake RLS tests #[ignore]d), or actively codify the vulnerability as correct (e2e_auth.rs asserts unauthenticated admin creation succeeds). Top gaps to close, in priority order: (1) add a Rust CI job with a postgres+AGE service and de-ignore the isolation/RLS suites; (2) run the already-written ai-server/mcp/dashboard test scripts in CI; (3) make the real-schema visibility test (p54) actually execute by giving the web test job a database; (4) flip e2e_auth.rs to assert auth is required so it guards the fix instead of the bug; (5) add SDK contract tests against the real route output. Flakiness risk is concentrated in the ungated, backend-dependent suites (dashboard Playwright, edgequake provider/Ollama e2e) — fine to keep as nightly, but they must not be mistaken for a gate.

crossResults.dimension: Cross-Cutting Refactor & Improvement Roadmap (NOW / NEXT / LATER)
crossResults.summary: SayKnowMind is an ambitious, genuinely capable local-first second-brain monorepo, but it is held together by an app-layer-only security model layered over an abandoned multi-tenant DB schema, and that mismatch has now become live data-correctness and isolation bugs (global entity collision, fail-open vector filter), not just tech debt. The most urgent work is not features — it is closing unauthenticated/cross-tenant holes (EdgeQuake ships with NO auth wired and a hardcoded JWT secret; several web routes execute shell or rewrite global prompts with no auth), repairing the dual-write/two-data-models tension at its source (the entities table + ON CONFLICT), and fixing a deploy pipeline that is 11 migrations stale and ships an invalid/never-transferred compose. NEXT is structural debt reduction: real tenant binding, removing dead/mock subsystems (zvec, orchestrators, unwired RBAC/audit, broken YAML parser), durable ingest jobs, and CI coverage for Rust+relay. LATER is the deeper architecture: collapse the two data models into one, CRDT-ify mindmap/sheet collab, real E2E crypto, and SDK contract codegen. The codebase rewards the effort — the resilience engineering (job-queue liveness, cascade fallback, worker pool, code-splitting) is genuinely good; it is the security/tenancy spine and the build/deploy coherence that are dangerous.

findings.title: NOW: Wire authentication + tenant binding onto EdgeQuake API and stop using the hardcoded JWT secret
findings.detail: AREA: packages/edgequake (edgequake-api). CHANGE: (1) .layer() the already-implemented api_key_auth + tenant_rate_limit middleware onto build_router and add a JWT-verification layer; (2) switch AppState::new_postgres to AuthConfig::from_env() and fail startup if JWT_SECRET is the default/short; (3) bind TenantContext to the verified JWT subject instead of trusting X-Tenant-ID/X-User-ID headers; (4) gate POST /api/v1/users behind an admin check. WHY: Verified — server.rs build_router (lines ~85-117) wires only body-limit/logging/request-id/trace/CORS/compression/Swagger; no auth or rate-limit layer is attached even though both exist and are exported. postgres.rs:293 uses AuthConfig::default(), so JWT_SECRET env is ignored and the literal 'change-me-in-production-256-bit-secret-key' signs tokens. Every /api/v1 endpoint (documents, query, graph, delete-all, user-create-with-role) is reachable unauthenticated, and isolation keys on spoofable headers. EFFORT: L. DEPENDS ON: deciding the canonical identity source (JWT vs header). RISK IF SKIPPED: full unauthenticated read/write/delete of all tenants' data on any exposed EdgeQuake instance; forged admin JWTs.
findings.recommendation: Treat as a release blocker. Add an integration test that asserts an unauthenticated /api/v1/documents request returns 401 and that a forged-default-secret token is rejected. Un-#[ignore] the RLS tests or delete the RLS abstraction (see LATER) so the test suite stops implying isolation that does not exist.
findings.evidence: packages/edgequake/crates/edgequake-api/src/server.rs:85-117 (no auth layer); packages/edgequake/crates/edgequake-api/src/state/postgres.rs:293 (AuthConfig::default()); middleware.rs:166,287 (unused api_key_auth/tenant_rate_limit); handlers/auth/user_management.rs:94-99 (role from body)

findings.title: NOW: Remove or hard-guard the three unauthenticated high-impact web routes (auth/test, settings/prompts, desktop/runtime)
findings.detail: AREA: apps/web/app/api. CHANGE: delete /api/auth/test entirely; add auth + per-user storage (DB, not process.cwd() file) to /api/settings/prompts, or gate it behind admin; gate /api/desktop/runtime behind a NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_MODE==='desktop'/localhost env check so it is never present in hosted builds. WHY: Verified — auth/test POST calls auth.api.signUpEmail (creates real persisted users, never cleaned up) and GET leaks BETTER_AUTH_URL etc. with no auth resolver. settings/prompts writes a single global .sayknowmind-prompts.json at process.cwd() that feeds every user's system prompt, with no getOrgContext/getUserId call — anonymous stored prompt injection. desktop/runtime runs execSync for which/docker/git/tar/pnpm build/rm -rf and downloads+extracts+spawns a Node tarball, with no auth/desktop guard. EFFORT: S (delete/guard) to M (per-user prompt storage). DEPENDS ON: none. RISK IF SKIPPED: anonymous DB pollution/DoS, global prompt hijack (data exfiltration/jailbreak for all users), and unauthenticated remote command execution if the route ships in a hosted image.
findings.recommendation: Ship the deletions/guards this week — they are small and high-severity. Add a CI grep test that fails if any route.ts under app/api lacks an auth resolver call except an explicit allowlist, to prevent regressions.
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/api/auth/test/route.ts:18 (signUpEmail, no auth); apps/web/app/api/settings/prompts/route.ts:7,220 (cwd file, writeFileSync, no auth); apps/web/app/api/desktop/runtime/route.ts:3,29-153 (execSync, no auth)

findings.title: NOW: Fix the global-entity collision — give entities a per-tenant/per-user key and fix the ON CONFLICT target
findings.detail: AREA: db/migrations + apps/web/lib/ingest/document-store.ts. CHANGE: add organization_id (and/or user_id) to entities, replace constraint entities_unique_name UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) with a scoped unique key that includes the owning org/user, and update insertEntities ON CONFLICT to target that key. Backfill existing rows by re-deriving owner from document_id. WHY: Verified — constraint at 01-edgequake-init.sql:155; insertEntities (document-store.ts:120-122) inserts only (document_id,name,...) leaving tenant_id/workspace_id NULL and does ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, workspace_id, name) DO UPDATE SET document_id = COALESCE(...). With NULLS NOT DISTINCT the constraint collapses to global-name uniqueness, so user B's 'React' silently resolves to user A's row and keeps A's document_id. Every entity->document graph link leaks across users and confidence/metadata corrupt. EFFORT: M. DEPENDS ON: choosing the canonical tenancy column (org vs user) — couples to the two-data-models decision. RISK IF SKIPPED: live cross-user knowledge-graph leakage and corruption; defeats lib/visibility.ts for the entity/graph surface entirely.
findings.recommendation: Do the schema+insert fix now even if the broader two-models cleanup is deferred; this is an active data-integrity bug, not just debt. Add a test that ingests the same entity name under two users and asserts two distinct rows with correct document_id linkage.
findings.evidence: db/init/01-edgequake-init.sql:155; apps/web/lib/ingest/document-store.ts:120-122; db/migrations/049_web_graph_schema_compat.sql (added document_id only, not constraint)

findings.title: NOW: Make the EdgeQuake vector tenant filter fail-CLOSED
findings.detail: AREA: packages/edgequake-query (sota_engine/prompt.rs). CHANGE: matches_tenant_filter must reject vectors whose metadata lacks tenant_id/workspace_id when a tenant filter is requested, matching the fail-closed graph-node policy; and push a SQL-level tenant predicate (filter_ids) instead of fetching from the shared table and filtering post-hoc. WHY: Verified — prompt.rs:16-23 returns true when the metadata key is absent (only rejects present-but-mismatched). Any vector stored without tenant metadata is visible to every tenant's query, and shared-table queries pass no SQL tenant predicate so cross-tenant rows displace valid top-k results (leakage + recall loss). Three inconsistent isolation policies coexist (vector fail-open, graph-node fail-closed, graph-edge fail-open). EFFORT: S-M. DEPENDS ON: ensuring ingestion always stamps tenant metadata (ingestion.rs:297-301 does, but legacy rows may not). RISK IF SKIPPED: cross-tenant RAG content leak whenever the shared default workspace table is used.
findings.recommendation: Unify all three paths on one fail-closed predicate and add SQL-level filtering. Add an e2e test storing an untagged vector and asserting tenant-scoped query does NOT return it.
findings.evidence: packages/edgequake/crates/edgequake-query/src/sota_engine/prompt.rs:16-37; vector_queries.rs:28-37,250-256; graph fail-closed node path mod.rs:1273-1291

findings.title: NOW: Unblock and de-stale the deploy pipeline (migration drift, never-shipped compose, error-swallowing)
findings.detail: AREA: Build/CI/Deploy. CHANGE: (1) replace the hardcoded migration lists in scripts/production-deploy.sh and .gitlab-ci.yml with the tracked migrate.sh glob+schema_migrations runner (single source of truth); (2) in .github/workflows/deploy.yml either scp the generated docker-compose.prod.yml to the host or stop generating it, and remove the depends_on: postgres reference to a service it never defines; (3) remove `psql ... || true` so failing migrations fail the deploy. WHY: Verified — db/migrations tree reaches 061; production-deploy.sh applies only through 050 (verified tail), so 051-061 (mcp_audit_log, org tables, organization_id, resource_shares/team_shares, doc_collab, document_versions) — exactly the team/collab/version features on this branch — are never applied. deploy.yml generates a compose in the runner workspace but the SSH step runs the host's pre-existing file. EFFORT: M. DEPENDS ON: none. RISK IF SKIPPED: every SSH-path deploy ships schema-drifted; the new team/collab/version features fail at runtime with missing-relation errors; migration failures are reported as success.
findings.recommendation: Adopt migrate.sh everywhere and delete the stale apply_all_migrations.sql/phase*_apply_all.sql artifacts (they reference a non-existent file numbering). Keep the honest CI migration-check (ci.yml:167-175) as the gate.
findings.evidence: db/migrations/ ends at 061; scripts/production-deploy.sh:160-187 (stops at 050); .github/workflows/deploy.yml:41-90 (generate vs ssh host file), :72-75 (|| true)

findings.title: NOW: Hash MCP API keys and stop running DDL on the request hot path
findings.detail: AREA: apps/web (session-helper, user/mcp-key) + packages/mcp-server. CHANGE: store only a hash of sk-mcp-* keys, authenticate via hashed+constant-time lookup, add expiry/rotation and >1 key per user; move CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS into a migration. WHY: Verified — session-helper.ts:16 authenticates via `SELECT user_id FROM user_mcp_keys WHERE api_key = $1` (plaintext equality, timing-unsafe); mcp-server does the same. A single DB/backup/log leak exposes every live credential; keys never expire; ensureTable runs on every GET/POST. EFFORT: M. DEPENDS ON: migration to add hash column + backfill (keys must be re-issued since hashing is one-way). RISK IF SKIPPED: credential exposure on any read leak; all-or-nothing revocation.
findings.recommendation: Hash with SHA-256 (keys are high-entropy, so a fast hash with constant-time compare is acceptable) and add an expires_at column. Coordinate the web and mcp-server validators so both use the same scheme.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/ingest/session-helper.ts:16; apps/web/app/api/user/mcp-key/route.ts:6-32; packages/mcp-server/src/index.ts:47-48

findings.title: NOW: Fix the AI-server cross-tenant memory IDOR and the dead feature-recommendation async
findings.detail: AREA: apps/ai-server. CHANGE: (1) stop trusting body/path userId+organizationId under a single shared AI_API_KEY — bind identity to a signed token or have the web app pass a verified, server-minted scope; remove SKIP_AUTH from any non-dev build; (2) make getUserMemory/deleteUserMemory pass organizationId so GDPR delete actually clears org-prefixed keys; (3) fix shouldEnableFeatures which returns synchronously before its checkGlobalLearningPatterns().then() resolves. WHY: Verified — chat.dto.ts:27,43 take userId/organizationId from the request body; the floating promise in algorithm.service.ts:230-260 mutates enableSearch AFTER return, so the enrichment never affects output (dead logic + unhandled-rejection risk). Combined with the shared key, any key holder can read/write/delete any user's Redis memory. EFFORT: M (auth), S (async fix). DEPENDS ON: web-side token minting for (1). RISK IF SKIPPED: cross-tenant memory read/write/delete; incomplete GDPR erasure; silently non-functional learning.

WHY: createJob fires processJobById as fire-and-forget; the concurrency semaphore and retry setTimeout are pure in-process state, so a deploy/crash/serverless teardown orphans the job forever and the document never indexes. crossResults.overall_assessment: This is a serious, capable project with real engineering depth (job-queue resilience, provider cascade fallback, the Rust worker pool, disciplined code-splitting, the team-feature migrations) sitting on a dangerous foundation: security and tenancy are app-layer-only, layered over an abandoned EdgeQuake multi-tenant schema, and that two-data-models tension has crossed from debt into live bugs — global entity collision, fail-open vector filtering, and an EdgeQuake API that ships with NO auth wired and a hardcoded JWT secret. The roadmap is therefore security-and-correctness-first: NOW (0-2wk) is pure containment of unauthenticated/cross-tenant holes, the entity-collision data fix, and unbreaking a deploy pipeline that is 11 migrations stale and ships an invalid compose; NEXT (1-2mo) is durable ingest, removing dead/mock subsystems that masquerade as features (orchestrators, zvec, broken YAML pipeline, unwired RBAC/audit), CI for the untested Rust core and relay, SDK contract repair, and desktop command lockdown; LATER (quarter+) is the structural endgame — collapse the two data models, decide RLS real-or-delete, CRDT-ify mindmap/sheet collab, deliver genuine E2E crypto, and pay down perf/ops debt. Grade C: the ambition and much of the implementation deserve a B, but the unwired-auth EdgeQuake, the unauthenticated shell/prompt web routes, and the cross-user entity leak are the kind of defects that define the floor for a product whose entire promise is private, isolated knowledge. Fix the NOW bucket and this becomes a credible B quickly — the bones are good; the spine is not yet load-bearing.
